# 开发入口

语言基础文档从 [docs/README.md](../docs/README.md)进入。当前开发规则是根 [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)，默认直接实现并运行相关测试；[任务图协议](graph-workflow.md)已停用，仅供历史查阅。`main` 用于集成产物，开发在 `dev`。

## 无人值守工具入口

默认使用这些脚本，标准输入关闭，不调用 shell，不自动提权或弹出权限请求。每次调用保存独立的 `/tmp/luna-tools-*/result.json`、`stdout.log`、`stderr.log`，终端只输出报告位置。单通道日志最多保存 8 MiB，超出部分继续排空并标记截断；原始命令、工作目录、耗时与退出码保留在报告中。

启动时立即输出 `running` 和报告路径，完成时再输出最终状态；工具调用提前返回时，也能直接用 report.py 检查本次任务，不必重新启动命令。

子进程已输出的数据即时写入日志，不等待输出凑满缓冲区或进程退出；子进程自己的输出缓冲策略仍由它决定。`running` 报告表示尚未记录完成，不能单独作为进程仍存活的依据。会话返回运行句柄时继续等待该句柄，不重复启动同一构建。

| 入口 | 用途与示例 |
|---|---|
| `python3 -B development/check.py --timeout 900 -- test -p luna --test instantiation` | 有时限的构建／测试，内部仍调用 cargo.py，复用维护锁、缓存清理及离线配置 |
| `python3 -B development/reproduce.py --timeout 60 -- input.fl --interpret entry` | 运行已有 Luna 二进制，使用当前工作目录，不自动构建 |
| `python3 -B development/backtrace.py --timeout 30 -- input.fl --interpret entry` | 可选 GDB 批量诊断，关闭初始化脚本、自动加载与 debuginfo 下载 |
| `python3 -B development/backtrace.py --core /path/to/core` | 读取已有 core，不启动被调试程序 |
| `python3 -B development/report.py /tmp/luna-tools-XXX` | 读取报告和每个日志末尾最多 8 KiB，不重新执行命令 |
| `python3 -B development/command.py --timeout 30 -- python3 -B -m unittest discover -s development` | 其他本地诊断的通用入口，按原样传递参数，不启动 shell；Cargo 仍走 check.py |

选项放在 `--` 前，被调用程序的参数放在后面。reproduce/backtrace 的 `--binary` 可以指定已有二进制；默认 `/tmp/luna-dev-002/target/debug/luna`。缓存被清理后先通过 check.py build 重新构建。工具不会保存输入源码快照，复现依赖报告所指的工作区版本。

普通失败保持退出码；信号退出映射为 128+信号编号，超时返回 124，不可用或日志写入失败返回 125。超时覆盖等待构建锁和继承的输出管道，并终止本次进程组，避免主进程结束后子进程继续挂住入口。它不限制其他独立启动的任务，也不重试普通编译失败。Cargo 的配额恢复仍由 cargo.py 处理。

外层封装收到 SIGTERM 或键盘中断也会清理本次子进程组，并保存 interrupted 报告；SIGKILL 无法被捕获。代理启动这些入口时应使用短工具等待时间（如 1000 ms），取得运行句柄后继续读取，避免一次工具调用长时间占住会话。

报告中的 `exit_code` 是子进程原始退出码，`wrapper_exit_code` 是工具最终返回码；判断是否超时或诊断不可用应读取 `status` 和后者，不能因为主进程提前退出 0 就误报成功。2026-10-14 在 `/home/fin/luna` 执行 `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s development -p 'test_*tools.py'`，退出 0，5 项通过，覆盖无交互输入、失败退出码、日志上限、信号退出与主进程退出后的子进程超时清理。

脚本不能绕过沙箱权限。backtrace 是可选诊断：ptrace 被拒时保存原因、返回 unavailable，继续用复现日志或已有 core，不因缺少回溯启动交互授权。GDB 的退出码只说明调试器状态，不代表被调试程序通过测试。真正必需的受限操作仍遵守环境授权要求，不能用包装脚本规避。

2026-10-14 实测：脚本单元测试与既有 cargo 测试共 14 项通过；check.py 运行 optional_inline_pass 5 项通过（`/tmp/luna-tools-08kxrfgk/result.json`）；reproduce.py 执行 `--help` 退出 0；沙箱拒绝 ptrace 时 backtrace.py 返回 125 并记录 unavailable（`/tmp/luna-tools-4qtx467_/result.json`），没有等待授权。

## Cargo 与缓存维护

统一通过 `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test execution` 或 `python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- input.fl --emit nir` 构建。入口自动补齐 `-j 1 --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-dev-002/target`，禁用 incremental 和 dev/test debuginfo，复用现有工作区；参数中的 `--` 及其后应用参数原样保留。无需再手写这些公共选项。历史验证记录中的直接 Cargo 命令仅保留作当时的证据，不作为当前默认入口。

开放签名、延迟类型及相关赋值资源回归使用独立入口：`python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test open_functions`。这些用例已从 `execution` 和 `resources` 移出；修改这组用例无需重编两份大型测试文件。共同的源码编译辅助函数位于 `compiler/luna/tests/support/execution.rs`。

整数程序规格与 CMTT 方法也有独立入口，优先按修改范围运行：

| 测试入口 | 覆盖范围 | 命令 |
|---|---|---|
| `integer_contracts` | comptime 整数条件、复制、参数／返回值、元组、三次表达式、版本失效及消项 | `python3 -B development/check.py --timeout 900 -- test -p luna --test integer_contracts` |
| `cmtt_methods` | 生成器方法声明、trait 分派、接收者、类型／值子句、父级捕获及契约兼容性 | `python3 -B development/check.py --timeout 900 -- test -p luna --test cmtt_methods` |

这些测试分别从 `execution`、`cmtt` 移出，原入口不再重复包含它们。跨领域改动仍需运行相关的原入口。CMTT 的源码到 IIR 执行辅助函数统一使用 `support/execution.rs` 中的 `run_iir`，实例化预算和解释执行路径保持一致。

显式执行已完成的 comptime 入口：`python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/computed-environment-types.fl --invoke-comptime run_comptime`。结果输出为 S-expression；可用 `--output value.lisp` 保存。`--fuel 100000` 控制本次 invocation 的步数预算（不替代前端自身预算），深度限制为 128。入口使用唯一函数名，不提供命令行实参；有必填参数或泛型参数时写一个具体的无参 wrapper，全默认参数的函数直接复用语言调用计划。`--invoke-comptime` 与 `--emit` 互斥。


用户已授权自主清理编译缓存。入口在构建前后检查 2 GiB target 大小上限及 2 GiB 文件系统余量，先 `cargo clean -p luna`，压力解除就保留 elaboration 编译缓存；仍有压力再清理 elaboration，最后才清理该 target 的全部生成产物；不触碰源码、Cargo.lock 或 registry 下载缓存。文件系统可用量不能反映全部配额，因此同时限制 target 大小。构建日志出现存储配额错误时，当前仍在运行的沙箱进程直接清理、最多重试一次；普通测试/编译失败保留退出码，不通过重试掩盖。构建与清理共用维护锁，不能与直接 Cargo 命令并发运行。生成的 target 产物是可回收缓存，需保留的 dump/报告应输出到 target 外。

配额错误触发的恢复会在包级清理后继续完整清理受管 target，不依赖文件系统剩余量判断，避免隐藏配额使重试仍无空间。日常容量检查仍优先保留依赖缓存。2026-10-09，在 `/home/fin/luna` 执行 `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s development -p test_cargo.py`，9 项通过；实际执行 `python3 -B development/cargo.py clean -p elaboration -p luna`，退出 0，回收 75 个文件、384.2 MiB，全程在沙箱内，无需额外授权。

2026-10-07，`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s development -p test_cargo.py` 7 项通过，覆盖命令分隔、清理范围、压力升级、存储恢复上限、真正失败不重试及真实子进程标准流分离。`python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p comptime_runtime` 实际自动清理 1.4 GiB 后完成 8 项整数测试（`/tmp/luna-cargo-cache-real.log`，退出 0），无需再次申请沙箱外清理权限。

## Runtime 参考执行

资源义务可独立检查：`python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/resource-obligations.fl --analyze-resources entry --copy-protocol CopyForAnalysis --output /tmp/luna-resource-obligations.lisp`。入口解析唯一的普通 runtime 函数；当前要求非泛型且无待满足的类型／capability 假设。`--copy-protocol` 显式指定源 trait 的声明身份，是开发驱动配置，不会因 trait 名叫 Copy 就自动赋予权限。重名入口／协议均拒绝。

报告使用 S-expression，包含 ownership obligations、移动与清理候选；成功不表示已执行 Drop 或证明完整内存安全。用户声明的 Copy 实现仍须有表示与资源合法性证据，当前入口不会仅凭声明批准复制。分析失败不覆盖已有输出；该模式与 emit、interpret、instantiate、invoke-comptime 互斥。`--fuel` 分别约束分析及类型查询，不是全请求总预算。

2026-10-09，在 `/home/fin/luna` 执行 `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test frontend_cli resource_cli`，退出 0，3 组通过（`/tmp/luna-resource-cli-final.log`）。覆盖报告输出、显式协议身份、移动失败、Copy 证据缺失、预算耗尽、入口与协议歧义、泛型协议两种声明顺序、参数冲突及失败时保留旧文件。

`python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/instantiated-functions.fl --interpret entry` 完成源码检查、具体 IIR 实例化和参考解释执行；示例结果为 `(unsigned-integer 41)`。`--interpret` 仅接受唯一的普通 runtime 函数名；必填参数或泛型参数需要具体 wrapper，全默认参数入口复用普通调用计划和默认参数作用域。该入口与 `--emit`、`--instantiate`、`--invoke-comptime` 互斥，支持 `--output`；失败保留旧文件，诊断写 stderr。`--fuel` 是各阶段独立的工作预算，不表示整个编译请求的总步数；解释深度上限 128。

执行带资源清理的示例：`python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/resource-execution.fl --interpret entry --copy-protocol CopyForExecution --drop-protocol DropForExecution`，结果为 `(bool true)`。这两个参数必须一起提供：入口先准备默认参数 wrapper、按声明身份绑定协议、为可达函数和闭包上下文生成清理计划，再安装计划并执行。验证或析构失败不会退回无清理的解释路径，`--output` 的旧文件也会保留。未指定协议的 `--interpret` 仍是原有的底层参考执行入口，不提供资源验证或自动 Drop；协议自动注册与完整安全模式集成仍待完成。


这是现有值／控制流片段的参考执行器，供行为验收及后续后端对照，不是 native 可执行产物，也尚未接入完整资源／代数效应系统。comptime invocation 继续使用独立的阶段检查入口。

## 具体函数实例 IR

`python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/instantiated-functions.fl --instantiate entry` 从显式 runtime 入口构建高级 IIR 实例图，输出 `(iir-package ...)`。支持 `--output instances.lisp` 和 `--fuel 100000`，与 `--emit`、`--invoke-comptime` 互斥。CLI 入口按唯一函数名选择；泛型入口须提供具体 wrapper。此操作生成实例图，不调用入口函数。

实例按声明身份和类型实参去重，递归复用实例键；保留结构化函数体、闭包、默认参数和程序契约，以及具体 nominal 定义、接口契约和选定 dispatch。未使用的条件方法不强制生成函数体，接口签名引用的类型仍保留。Normal-form 头保持不透明。发布前检查未替换类型参数、runtime 身份可用性和类型／调用依赖；失败不交付半成品或覆盖旧输出。

2026-10-08 本轮验证（工作目录 `/home/fin/luna`）：

- `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p iir -p elaboration -p luna -p comptime_interpretor --tests`：退出 0，970 项通过，日志 `/tmp/luna-iir-regression.log`。
- 补齐接口签名依赖后，`python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test instantiation --test frontend_cli`：退出 0，56 项通过，日志 `/tmp/luna-iir-final.log`。覆盖三组泛型实例、递归／闭包、trait 选择、契约要求拒绝与恢复、范式头不展开、缺失类型／函数依赖、预算失败及 CLI 输出保护。
- `emacs --batch -Q --script /tmp/luna-verify-iir.el /tmp/luna-instantiated-functions.lisp`：退出 0，Lisp reader 确认单一 IIR 表达式，格式化前后结构相同。修改文件已 rustfmt，`git diff --check` 通过。

具体实例现在可通过 `comptime_interpretor::Interpreter::from_iir` 与 `invoke_instance` 进行参考解释执行。函数体、类型定义和接口契约直接取自实例图，不保留源 NIR 或在执行时重新实例化泛型模板；支持现有值／控制流求值器已实现的操作，保留 runtime 契约检查。CLI 的 `--instantiate` 仍仅生成实例图。LLVM 降码尚未完成；验证仍依赖输入 NIR 的操作／局部作用域合法性，不等于完整 IIR 语义验证器。外部 runtime 身份集合不构成资源或存活性证明；缺乏保留值存储证据的 `Term::Value` 暂时明确拒绝。后续需要完善这些证据与执行接口。

## 工程地图

以下是 2026-10-07 的本地核对，不是永久不变的架构；每项任务仍须读取当前 manifest 和相关文件。

| 范围 | 当前证据与使用方式 |
|---|---|
| `compiler/` | Rust workspace；包含前端、query、middle、interface、luna、comptime 与 IIR 等 crate；具体成员以根 Cargo.toml 为准 |
| 后端旧目录 | typeck、mir、mir_build、codegen 当前未列为启用成员；workspace 检查不覆盖它们，不由目录存在推定后端完整 |
| `library/` | 当前有 builtin 与 std 源码；文档定义的其他内置包不代表已经实现 |
| anar | 未在当前 checkout 或 /home/fin/anar 发现；第一次任务先定位真实仓库、协议、工具链与测试入口，再分配写入范围 |
| `compiler/query/tests/query_engine.rs` | 已有行为断言，覆盖缓存、环、panic 恢复及键隔离，可作为现成局部测试入口 |
| `compiler/luna/tests/frontend_cli.rs` | 独立进程的 CLI 回归测试，覆盖参数、阶段失败、输出通道、文件保护及重复 dump；每个子进程有超时与回收 |
| `compiler/hir/tests/display.rs` | 直接构造 HIR，检查现有变体的载荷、转义、节点关系与输出顺序 |
| `test_project/`、根 `test.fl` | 示例与手工输入；不由文件存在推定为通过的自动化语言用例 |

测试覆盖范围以各阶段的行为验收为准；AST 的部分旧测试仍需扩充，不能仅凭 crate 构建成功推定语言特性完整。

luna driver 接收显式输入文件，默认把 HIR dump 写到 stdout。`--emit ast` 在解析成功后导出 AST，`--output <path>` 显式指定文件输出，`--sysroot <path>` 指定库目录。它不会隐式读取 test.fl 或写入 ast.lisp、hir.lisp。诊断写到 stderr；成功退出 0，编译阶段或 I/O 错误退出 1，用法错误退出 2。

输入为 `main.fl` 或 `lib.fl` 时，HIR/NIR 阶段把该输入的父目录作为选定源码根，按排序后的目录快照发现 `.fl` 文件；其他文件名保持单文件模式，`--emit ast` 仍导出选定文件。文件模块、无入口目录、`mod.fl` 及内联模块进入同一 HIR 包，未引用文件的语法失败不会隐藏。源码目录中的符号链接目前明确拒绝。此 driver 入口尚不代替 anar 的 package 根选择、额外源码根和生成输入协议。

限定静态调用、模块内词法查找、跨文件类型别名、具名/通配导入与再导出已接通。导入按声明身份去重；直接声明和显式导入遮蔽通配候选，内部通配歧义在使用处报告，公开出口歧义由提供者检查。带种子的导入环和空通配环可以收敛。别名、嵌套分组、`private use` 及 `@`/前导点定位已接通。名称入口的权限与原始声明权限分开保留和检查；显式再导出可以使用合法可访问的内部别名，公开通配仅传播公开入口。权限核心有两个 package 作用域的单元验证，但实际多 package 输入/导入接线与增量源码失效尚未完成。带共同前缀的分组内部再写定位锚点目前明确拒绝。

可运行 `cargo run -p luna --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-dev-002/target -- development/examples/modules/main.fl --emit nir` 查看三文件示例，模块行为测试入口为 `cargo test -p luna --test modules --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-dev-002/target`。

文件输出在所选阶段成功后通过临时文件发布；阶段失败保留已有输出。拒绝输出路径与输入相同，包括可确认的路径别名与 Unix 硬链接，以及自动发现的其他源码文件。需要新建输出目录时由调用者提前准备。

HIR 的 `Package`、表达式、模式及其相关结构提供 `Display`，使用完整 S-expression；`dump_to_lisp()` 委托同一实现。body 表按完整 ID 排序，文本显式转义。新增 `--emit nir` 可导出已接入构造的带类型表达式树；它尚未经过资源/效应验证，不能据此生成可执行程序。

字面量前端保留整数、浮点的精确源码拼写，不经 i64/f64 转换。HIR dump 使用 `(integer (spelling "..."))` / `(float (spelling "..."))`；这些节点尚未求值。字符、固定字符串按文档解码，空白相邻字符串合并；后缀保存为 `literal-conversion` 节点，等待 elaboration 查询 LiteralInto。字符串插值和 BitVec 模式降码尚未实现，会明确报 unsupported，避免输出错误的固定值或模式。

完整开发目标、阶段依赖与实际能力边界见[实现地图](implementation-plan.md)。各个任务图的通过只证明其验收范围，不表示整门语言已经实现。

NIR 已有不可变类型 core、runtime 依赖抽象、引用端 substitution、使用点绑定检查、依赖参数契约接口与 S-expression Display。24 项局部测试覆盖共享 core 与 runtime identity 的分离、无捕获替换、normal form 保留以及非法绑定拒绝。函数签名实例化按参数顺序替换依赖契约和返回类型，保留 normal form 的头，并在嵌套函数返回类型中避免捕获。结构相等不充当完整类型等价判定；契约的语义检查仍由后续 elaborator 提供，driver 已接入单态函数检查和 NIR dump；依赖类型求解、泛型、comptime 执行及资源检查仍未接通。

PTC 的首个类型相等片段位于 `compiler/elaboration/src/ptc.rs`，已经用于单态检查器的参数、结果与分支类型要求。支持布尔组合、等价类、闭合结构构造器的同余/分解，以及显式准入的 normal-form 头同余；不会展开 normal form。每次查询独立持有事实，分支与后续查询不共享可变合并状态。结果区分 Entailed、带实际闭合类型反例的 NotEntailed、Unknown 和 IllFormed；抽象模型不能验证时保留 Unknown。证明树携带假设与同余契约，可在相同上下文回放并检查冲突；证明、反例和残余义务都有 S-expression 输出。

该实现是有预算的布尔分支搜索与相等理论，不是完整 CDCL(T) 引擎；尚无学习子句、增量缓存或优化的回滚并查集。证明回放共享相等理论检查器，尚不是独立形式化证明内核。依赖绑定结构保守处理，程序状态完全不进入 PTC。源码泛型/where 假设尚未传入求解上下文，其余原子命题、一般线性/同余整数、BV/行类型理论、trait 选择与推断义务调度尚未接通。

数学整数差分逻辑位于 `compiler/elaboration/src/ptc/integer.rs`，与类型等式通过统一原子和布尔搜索组合。`IntegerTerm` 表示独立数学整数参数加常数，`IntLe` 表示两项的小于等于；否定转换严格处理整数的一单位差。Bellman–Ford 检测负环并产生具体整数赋值，零点归一后再核对完整源公式；整数与类型变量即便使用同一声明编号也属于不同逻辑域。冲突进入同一证明树并支持回放。内部采用 checked i128 运算，超容量返回 ArithmeticRange/Unknown，不赋予数学整数机器溢出语义；这是当前实现容量限制，不是任意精度整数的完整实现。此接口仅供准入的静态命题，不接受程序内存规格，也未接入源码整数 predicate lowering。

类型分类 A02 的基础片段位于 `compiler/elaboration/src/ptc/classification.rs`。当前登记 bool、整数、有符号/无符号整数、浮点、tuple、pointer、function 八种查询；整数包含有符号与无符号类别，分类不是互斥枚举。分类事实沿类型等价类传播，并与封闭结构描述及分类间已定义的包含/互斥关系共同产生冲突。反例选择实际类型后核对整条公式，有限候选未能构造模型时保留 Unknown。没有完整描述的名义/newtype、normal-form 和 closure 分类保守保留，不能由底层表示、工厂实参或环境猜测。公开反射入口和源码分类 predicate lowering 尚未连接，宇宙、限定和槽观察仍待实现。

其中端到端测试单独运行时用 `cargo test -p luna --test elaboration`；推断状态测试用 `cargo test -p elaboration --test inference`。40 组端到端测试覆盖函数、前向/递归调用、高阶函数值、别名、局部绑定、分支、return、void、短路逻辑、lambda 参数上下文、结果推断、捕获次序/去重和嵌套捕获、具名 optional 输入及前序参数默认链与拒绝路径，7 组推断状态测试覆盖候选隔离及冻结。调用计划把源码求值顺序与目标参数位置分别保留；缺省表达式只读取定义作用域的前序参数，当前仅对有限的标量/元组表达式给出 P3 依据，任意调用仍需纯度与终止分析。闭包环境在 NIR 中显式保留；非空环境不能隐式传给普通 fn，捕获责任尚未经过资源检查。候选状态仓库尚未与单态检查器连接，不能视为完整 elaboration 引擎。源码中的数值转换、未实现的属性/阶段协议和资源操作会被拒绝或保留为后续阶段义务；NIR dump 不表示程序通过资源安全验证。

`compiler/elaboration/src/obligations.rs` 将推断状态、PTC 事实、义务、等待者和证明统一为候选区域。尚未稳定的相等/分类要求可以组合为布尔树；等待集跟随推断别名更新，赋值仅唤醒相关义务。队列与单次 PTC 查询分别有预算，稳定 Unknown 只在显式重试或事实变化后重新求解。增加事实会使旧上下文的证明/反例重新检查。试探复制整套区域，提交同时检查父区域版本与所有义务已证明，再发布推断和证据；未决/反例/非法输入拒绝提交或冻结。`assume` 只接收调用方已经建立且允许在该区域使用的事实，候选适用条件必须调用 `require`，不能循环假设自己的结论。

该区域引擎仍未接入单态源码检查器、泛型候选选择或 comptime 工作调度；目前等待事件只有推断变量赋值。提交要求整个区域的义务已经证明，尚无跨区域残余契约交付和诊断来源链。2026-10-07 在 `/home/fin/luna` 执行 `cargo test -p elaboration --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-dev-002/target` 退出 0（`/tmp/luna-obligations-final.log`），44 项通过，其中 8 项区域引擎测试覆盖别名等待、定向唤醒、失败候选隔离、嵌套提交、上下文失效、预算重试、非法推断与冻结边界。`cargo run -p elaboration --example obligations --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-dev-002/target` 生成 `/tmp/flurry-obligations.lisp`，挂起、候选提交和稳定导出结构通过 Emacs 单表达式读取与缩进检查。本轮未重复前端回归，源码检查器未改动。

`Engine::match_types` 已提供候选内的类型推断提案：从未解变量、tuple、pointer、函数与闭包结构中提取赋值，并为原始完整类型关系登记 PTC 义务。所有提案位于新候选，发生检查、预算失败或最终等式冲突不修改父状态；已有等待义务也进入同一候选重新检查。函数绑定下只提取可独立成立的闭合类型，不能把局部绑定捕获到外围替换。normal-form 与名义类型没有通用单射规则，不反推其参数；不支持的开放匹配仍保留等待。这是推断引擎接口，尚未用于源码泛型签名实例化，不代表实现选择、依赖模式统一或完整高阶推断已经完成。

`compiler/elaboration/src/calls.rs` 提供类型参数化签名的调用实例化：输入是已完成阶段资格检查的签名、按形参路由的类型/运行时对象和可选结果上下文。一次候选同时匹配全部参数与结果，所以后面的实参可以解决前面不透明契约所依赖的类型参数；显式类型参数也进入同一检查。运行时参数契约仅替换此前对象，结果替换完整调用环境，保留 runtime identity 和 normal-form 头。只有全部关系证明且类型参数已解才能导出 Instance（替换、实例化签名、结果类型），提供 S-expression Display。这里只支持外层 Type 参数及内层 runtime 形参，不执行实参、不选择实现、不补造运行时对象，也未连接源码泛型 lowering；命名/缺省实参仍由现有调用路由层负责。

解释执行器已有 NIR 值与控制流内核。`luna::frontend::compile` 供 CLI 与测试共同使用，返回不借用 HIR arena 的产物；33 组源码执行测试经同一前端编译后检查真实返回值和调用轨迹，覆盖短路、捕获快照、默认值、提前返回、局部赋值、块作用域、嵌套循环、具名 break/continue、预算耗尽和非法调用计划。匹配保留有序臂、守卫、臂内绑定及单次输入求值；bool 覆盖与无守卫兜底用于当前标量片段的穷尽检查。`if/while … is … do` 共用该链路。`or` 分支校验相同导出名称与类型，再映射到统一局部身份；支持嵌套选择和整体 `as` 绑定。`let … else` 保留模式、守卫和失败分支，失败分支在引入新绑定前检查且必须发散。有限标量匹配可用于默认值的 P3 稳定片段。元组/列表 pattern view 和任意 comptime 模式尚未接通。循环目标在 lowering 时绑定到独立身份，不能越过函数或 lambda；块退出保留外层绑定的写入并移除内层绑定。捕获状态写入仍需闭包效应与资源检查，当前明确拒绝。执行器尚未接入阶段资格与资源验证，因此 CLI 不自动执行普通函数，也没有把这部分称为完整 comptime invocation。

源码 `when` 已接通表达式解析、显式 fallback 的 HIR 表示、分支类型检查和 NIR 有序条件降码。条件按源码顺序执行，首个命中后跳过后续条件与主体；else 必须处于最后。各返回分支统一类型，未写 else 时丢弃分支值并得到 void；无 else 的 if 同步按正式语义丢弃主体值，保留赋值和提前退出。有限 when 可以作为默认值计算，return/break/continue 沿既有 NIR 控制流传递。

普通非泛型 struct 已接通源码声明、名义类型、完整指名构造、嵌套字段读取和解释执行。NIR Package 保留按声明顺序的字段描述，Record 构造计划按该顺序检查/执行，Field 节点保留名义声明身份与字段索引。显式输入覆盖默认表达式；默认表达式在定义作用域检查，每次实际采用时执行，允许普通函数调用。未知/重复/缺失字段、字段类型错误、同形异名义类型混用、重复字段声明与按值递归表示均拒绝；指针间接递归可声明。花括号构造的 lowering 已从错误的 NFApplication 修正为 ExtendedApplication。未实现的字段属性、可见性修饰及 struct body 配置明确保留为不支持的语义，不能静默忽略。

## 可用检查入口

下列命令来自实际 manifest 与测试文件；列出命令不表示本次已执行或已通过。执行者需记录工具链、工作目录、退出码和输出，并按任务选择检查范围。

```sh
cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --locked --offline
cargo test -p hir --test display --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-hir-check
cargo test -p luna --test frontend_cli --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-cli-check
cargo test -p luna --bin luna --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-cli-check
cargo test -p lex -p parse -p hir -p ast_lowering -p luna --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-literal-check
cargo test -p query --test query_engine --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-query-check
cargo test -p nir --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-dev-002/target
cargo check -p luna --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-driver-check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-workspace-check
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

这些命令从仓库根执行。并行任务把示例 target 目录换成自己的唯一目录，避免锁竞争及产物混用；对比基线和新版本时保持构建条件一致。大型缓存需要复用时，由协调者明确管理，不能多个任务清理同一目录。

可用以下入口导出一个包含调用、分支和字符串的 HIR，并交给 Emacs 的 Lisp reader 与 formatter 核对结构：

```sh
cargo run -p luna --locked --offline --target-dir /tmp/luna-driver-check -- development/runs/001-frontend-entry/example.fl --output /tmp/flurry-example.hir.lisp
emacs --batch -Q --script development/runs/001-frontend-entry/verify-lisp.el /tmp/flurry-example.hir.lisp
```

Emacs 仅用于这项编辑器兼容性检查，Rust 测试没有该依赖。首轮实现范围与独立验收证据见 [001-frontend-entry](runs/001-frontend-entry/contract.md)。

trait 参数的主体相关能力（例如 `trait Adapter where T :- Read<Self>`）已贯通。Self 身份在解释声明 binder 之前登记；形成 Adapter<T> 时暂缓主体相关能力，把它与父接口义务一起在实现上下文代入 Self 后证明。非主体相关参数能力仍按既有形成规则检查。编译期 materialization 与解释器的能力依赖校验都同时替换 Self 和显式参数，不能把 trait 声明的刚性 Self 留进具体世界。

comptime_runtime 的占位加法已替换为真正的任意精度 Integer 值内核，无新增第三方依赖。数值采用规范化符号与 base-2^32 magnitude，零无负号；字面量按十/二/八/十六进制精确解析，保留超过宿主 u128 的值。提供比较、取负、加减乘及显式 `div_rem_trunc`，后者只是商向零截断的底层运算 API，不替语言决定运算符协议。1..=128 位 signed/unsigned 转换逐项检查范围，绝不默默 wrapping。Display 使用确定顺序的 `(integer (sign ...) (hex "..."))`，输出成本与 limb 数量成正比。

解析与算术接受共享燃料和 magnitude/scratch 大小上限；失败返回 InvalidLiteral/BudgetExhausted/SizeLimit/DivisionByZero/OutOfRange 等明确结果，不改变输入，燃料不足耗尽剩余额度。大小上限是每个缓冲区的资源上限，不是 Integer 的语言位宽。乘法使用 O(nm) schoolbook，除法使用有预算的二进制长除法作为精确基线，尚未做大数优化。这一内核尚未接入数值表达式 elaboration、阶段许可、splice 目标推断、LiteralInto 或库的固定宽度算术；Float 也未实现，不据此声称数值源码已经可执行。

## Finite floating-point literal proxies (2026-10-07)

`comptime_runtime::decimal::DecimalLiteral` retains exact decimal coefficient/exponent and a separate sign (including negative zero). Parsing and conversion consume shared fuel; f32 conversion parses directly into that format, avoiding an intermediate f64 rounding. This is lexical literal support, not general comptime Float arithmetic. Runtime proxy formation selects f32/f64 from context and defers the f64 fallback while generic constraints are still being collected. NIR and interpreter values retain IEEE bits, with format/type validation and IEEE value equality for literal patterns. Direct literal type observation still reports comptime Float.

[float-proxies.fl](examples/float-proxies.fl) is also the input to an execution regression. Coverage includes a double-rounding counterexample, ties-to-even, signed zero, smallest subnormals, underflow, generic inference, definition defaults, pattern matching, malformed NIR formats and conversion budget recovery. Float operators, LiteralInto suffix protocols, nonfinite source literals and full comptime Float arithmetic remain unimplemented. Overflowing finite literals produce an explicit unsupported diagnostic; this does not settle the language's eventual overflow policy. Resource verification and comptime execution authorization remain separate from the NIR interpreter.

The by-value aggregate-pointer dependency gap has been traced to the interface:
memory::ParameterPlace begins at a direct pointer argument's pointee (including
newtype pointer representations). Its through segments load pointers from that
pointee; they cannot stand for selecting a field of a by-value input before the
first pointer load. Supporting that case requires explicit input-field origin
paths, matching aggregate pointer provenance in Infer environments, and matching
caller ownership relocation in moves::map_memory_target. Existing pointer-free
admission must stay closed until those producer/consumer paths agree. No new
aggregate pointer authorization was introduced by this audit.



## BitVec baseline value kernel (2026-10-07)

`comptime_runtime::bitvec` now represents arbitrary fixed-width defined bit values as canonical little-endian u32 words. It implements checked word construction, same-width and/or, width-limited not, indexing, half-open slicing, high-left/low-right concatenation and zero extension. Width arithmetic is checked before allocation, zero width has a unique empty representation, nonzero padding is rejected, and operations consume the shared budget with bounded buffers. `Integer::to_bitvec` converts nonnegative arbitrary-precision literal values with a checked target width, including zero into BitVec<0>; negative or out-of-range inputs are never truncated. Display preserves width and bits in an S-expression.

This is the executable value baseline described in `docs/program-synthesis/bitvec-algebra.md`, not source BitVec elaboration, memory-location writeback, target layout mapping, unsafe construction authorization or synthesis. Source evaluation order and resource contracts still need their own lowering; these pure value operations do not justify removing operand evaluations.

Verification from `/home/fin/luna`: `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p comptime_runtime`, exit 0, 18 tests passed (`/tmp/luna-bitvec-core.log`). Five BitVec groups compare all slice ranges through width 160 and concatenations through widths 97 against independent boolean-sequence models; they cover word boundaries, tail masking, width mismatch, invalid endpoints, narrowing rejection, resource failure/recovery and a 1025-bit integer conversion. `python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p comptime_runtime --example bit-values`, exit 0, produces `/tmp/luna-bit-values.lisp`; Emacs reader/formatter preserves its structure. Changes remain uncommitted on dev.


## BitVec source views and eager logical operations (2026-10-07)

The concrete-width NIR type now retains BitVec width as part of type identity. Fixed-width signed/unsigned integer `'bitvec` views lower to an explicit `take-bits` node; signed values use their declared-width two's-complement representation. Integer literals with a BitVec context use checked arbitrary-precision conversion. Type substitution and dispatch materialization visit the new nodes. `++` now survives AST lowering as a distinct HIR operator and produces a checked-width NIR concatenation; bitwise `not`, `and`, `or` execute through the bounded value kernel. Boolean and/or still short-circuit; BitVec and/or evaluate both sides in order. Interpreter fuel is shared with kernel operations; representation-size exhaustion is distinct from fuel exhaustion.

[bitvec-values.fl](examples/bitvec-values.fl) is compiled by the source execution regression. It uses type reflection over a typed local view to expose concrete bit types until builtin `BitVec<N>` value-argument elaboration is connected. Function calls inside top-level type observation currently encounter the existing requirements-collection ordering limitation; the example does not bypass missing contracts. Tests cover contextual generic integer arguments, signed views, concatenation order, integer patterns, both eager logical operations, snapshot independence after mutation, malformed NIR padding/width and invalid source conversions. This is value execution only: source slicing/indexing, explicit BitVec<N>, width inference from general comptime expressions, representation conversion, writable views, unsafe construction and synthesis remain pending. Only fixed integer and already formed BitVec inputs are currently supported for source views.

## BitVec source slices and conversions (2026-10-07)

Source BitVec values now support constant single-bit indexing, explicit half-open constant slices, same-width equality/inequality, zero-extension to a wider BitVec and unsigned conversion to a fixed-width integer at least as wide as the source. Narrowing is rejected based on width even if the value is zero. Other reinterpretations remain unsupported and do not gain unsafe construction permission. Runtime endpoints and general comptime endpoint computations remain unimplemented; runtime bound obligations belong to program verification, never PTC.

Range expressions now retain endpoints and inclusivity in HIR. The parser's old index production incorrectly parsed the brackets as a list literal; it now consumes the delimiters and preserves the single enclosed expression, as required by `index_application -> expr [expr]`. Explicit nested list expressions remain distinct. NIR retains `bit-slice`, `bit-convert` and `bit-equal`, with Display, specialization traversal, materialization traversal and bounded interpreter execution. Invalid NIR endpoints fail before subtraction or indexing; target widths are validated independently. General standalone range expression protocols remain unsupported.

## Static BitVec writeback to owned scalar places (2026-10-07)

`BitVec::replaced` constructs a checked replacement value without modifying either input, with word-oriented clearing/insertion and bounded allocation/work. Elaboration now distinguishes an assignment location from a read snapshot: direct integer bit views and stored BitVec places can select static indices/slices (including nested slices) and receive a same-width RHS. Integer literals receive that selected width as context. Existing local/field place checks and captured-state restrictions apply; accepted storage is limited to fixed integer and BitVec representations whose every bit pattern is valid. No general unsafe reconstruction, pointer access or concurrency permission is inferred.

NIR `bit-assign` retains the place, storage type, selected interval and RHS, including Display and specialization/materialization traversal. The interpreter obtains the full RHS first, re-resolves the current place, checks representation/width, constructs the updated value, then commits. Writes by the RHS to preserved bits or sibling fields survive. Empty updates still evaluate the RHS. Signed integer reconstruction restores the declared-width sign (including i128); saved read values remain independent. This is the existing owned scalar/local interpreter fragment, not completion of the affine/resource verification layer.

[bitvec-writeback.fl](examples/bitvec-writeback.fl) exercises the documented overlapping update (0x1234 to 0x1344), snapshot preservation, nested bit selections, RHS writes to the same storage and sibling fields, signed updates and stored BitVec independence. ## Demand-driven function signatures and observed call obligations (2026-10-07)

Function signatures are now collected on demand with completed-signature caching, active dependency-cycle detection and a 64-level depth limit. This removes declaration-order dependence for the supported function-call type observations, including forward references and multi-level return-type observations. Function bodies are not executed or unfolded. Signature checking isolates definition-local context, runtime locals/captures and numeric-default policy from a caller's speculative argument probe.

Call/function-value formation during signature/contract collection queues its type and capability obligations for the existing complete-definition check. Every record retains its originating definition and whether that definition's requirements may be assumed; contract operands cannot assume the contract being defined. Declaration-owned signature obligations are kept separately from speculative call obligations, so an aborted input probe can roll back its own work without discarding obligations attached to an already cached signature. Until requirements are collected, observed function references conservatively retain instance identity rather than indexing an absent requirements entry.

[signature-observation.fl](examples/signature-observation.fl) covers forward calls, constrained generic calls and chained signatures. [bitvec-values.fl](examples/bitvec-values.fl) now uses direct `byte()'bitvec'type`, superseding the workaround/ordering limitation recorded above. Tests reject false type requirements, absent trait bounds, signature/alias cycles and self-justifying contract operands; verify obligations survive abandoned argument probes; and check a 24-level successful chain versus explicit depth exhaustion. Existing general comptime scheduling, value/dependent parameter elaboration, optional-default observations and trait lookup before its implementation world is complete are not thereby implemented.

## Explicit comptime declaration phases and guarded interpretation

Explicit `comptime fn` and `pure comptime fn` now retain modifiers through AST lowering, record execution phase/purity in NIR and participate in normal declaration identity/import/visibility lookup. The scanner unwraps attribute/modifier chains for binding without authorizing their semantics. Normal-form heads have a separate HIR marker and remain unavailable for ordinary execution; `pure` is retained as a trusted promise, not a license to unfold heads or assume PTC facts. Runtime purity modifiers remain unsupported rather than silently inheriting comptime's trusted-promise treatment.

`nir::phases::validate` checks the current first-order fragment, including function defaults, guards and pattern computations, with an iterative tree walk. A comptime body cannot call or obtain a runtime function. Runtime calls/values of comptime functions remain explicit unsupported invocation/splicing boundaries. Comptime indirect calls, closures, first-class function values, generic instances and trait dispatch await their phase-aware type and elaboration support. Dead ordinary branches are still checked; this does not implement inline branch selection or the full loose checking model.

`Interpreter::for_comptime` validates phases at construction and checks declaration phase again at each executed entry/call. Runtime entries fail before recording an invocation. The existing `Interpreter::new` remains a semantic execution harness for runtime NIR tests; it does not authorize comptime. The guarded entry shares value/control-flow semantics, fuel, recursion-depth failure and restoration with that harness. No value-result cache is introduced, and pure/impure declarations both execute normally. This is a phase boundary, not resource/effect verification, a bytecode executor, or a frontend automatic invocation hook.

Nontrivial comptime defaults retain an explicit normalization diagnostic instead of being misreported as runtime P3 obligations.

## Concrete comptime Integer values and arithmetic

Explicit comptime functions now retain unsuffixed integer values as arbitrary-precision Integer when no runtime proxy context is requested. Explicit fixed-width contexts still use the existing checked proxies, and runtime literal defaulting remains i32. `.Integer'builtin` is available through the explicit compiler type entry while prelude integration remains pending. NIR now carries Integer negation and binary operations with stable S-expression names. Add, subtract, multiply and the six equality/order comparisons execute using the exact Integer kernel. Source calls/operands retain left-to-right evaluation, and early returns propagate without evaluating later operands. Concrete Integer literal patterns compare canonical numeric values, with parsing/comparison charged to the same invocation budget. Negation and comparison also charge limb work; arithmetic distinguishes fuel exhaustion from representation-size failure. This does not attach kernel truncating division/remainder to source operators: those still await their language protocol contract. Generic operator dispatch and fixed-width runtime arithmetic remain separate work.

Phase validation rejects comptime-only Integer/Float/Type values in runtime storage. It inspects tuples, signatures, closure environments, pointers and instantiated struct/enum fields with bounded, cycle-aware traversal. Phantom type arguments do not create stored values. Opaque normal-form heads are not unfolded. Integer computation nodes themselves cannot remain in runtime NIR even when type parameters obscure their storage phase. Automatic evaluation and Splice are still required before legitimate compiletime results can enter runtime dataflow.

## Concrete comptime Type values and BitVec type construction

Comptime functions can now return and forward Type values. Source builtin types, aliases, nominal applications, static tuple/function/pointer types and type observations become explicit NIR `TypeValue` payloads. `Identity(value: Type)` uses ordinary call semantics and returns the supplied type value. NIR type substitution traverses the payload as well as the outer annotation, and dispatch dependency collection follows types retained inside those payloads. No normal-form head is evaluated or unfolded; holding a type identity does not turn structural carrier equality into general semantic type equality.

The explicit `.BitVec'builtin<width>` expression additionally has a type-value construction node. Its operand is a comptime Integer expression, so a concrete function can compute widths using earlier arithmetic or accept them as inputs. Negative widths and widths beyond the implementation usize limit report `InvalidBitWidth`; zero and non-byte widths are valid. Type construction does not allocate bit storage, including at usize::MAX. Early return from the width operand propagates before construction. This applies to expressions executed by the comptime interpreter: aliases/signatures that require automatic invocation still use the existing pending boundary, and arbitrary normal-form heads do not become constructors.

Type observations use the existing static type-checking path and produce a type value without executing the observed operand. Source nominal formation requirements remain checked. The concrete interpreter validates type-value sort, shape and binding scope within bounded traversal; it allows internal function binders while rejecting free binders, holes, active rigid inputs, external value-store handles and runtime identities without environments. This is not a replacement for elaboration's formation/trait proofs, nor general runtime-dependent TypeRef environment support.

`development/examples/comptime-types.fl` demonstrates type selection/identity calls, primitive and nominal aliases, a generic nominal application, static structural types, computed 257-bit and zero-bit types, invalid width failures, Integer literal reflection and observation of a runtime function's result type. Tests confirm the observed runtime function is absent from the execution trace, preserve opaque normal-form terms, substitute inside type-value payloads without unfolding heads, recover after invalid inputs and retain properly scoped internal binders. A former generic-struct expression rejection now distinguishes missing type arguments, a non-callable constructor and a Type value that would escape into runtime storage.

## On-demand type contracts for required computation (2026-10-08)

Required comptime execution now prepares type-only declaration contracts on demand instead of rejecting all constrained calls during initial collection. Successful contract preparation is retained per declaration with its operand-formation obligations. The ordinary collection pass finishes remaining contracts and attaches requirements to nominal metadata. Contract preparation has a bounded active-dependency guard, uses binder context without assuming its own requirements, and restores the caller context on both success and failure.

Before executing a required computation, the elaborator closes over contract-operand dependencies and newly observed signature obligations, then checks each use in its recorded scope. Function bodies may use definition requirements; the operands that define those requirements may not. A cached contract replays its formation obligations at required-use sites. Trait capabilities that need the still-incomplete implementation world remain an explicit wait/error. This is not general asynchronous elaboration scheduling, program verification or comptime trait dispatch.

`development/examples/comptime-contracts.fl` exercises a forward generic call constrained by `T == Bool`, forwarding to another constrained function, a body returning Bool under that equality, and a non-generic `requires true` call. Rejection tests cover false contracts, mismatched generic arguments, nested false requirements, and attempts to use a contract to justify its own constrained nominal operands. Earlier blanket waiting diagnostics for false type contracts now report the unsatisfied requirement itself.

## Demand-driven ordinary parameter defaults (2026-10-08)

Function default preparation now has an isolated definition frame and a bounded dependency guard. It is shared by the ordinary collection pass, generic call inference, ordered ordinary calls and required comptime preparation. Only preceding parameters are bound; caller locals, returns, captures and loop targets are restored after preparation. Cached defaults retain formation obligations for replay during required computations. Runtime defaults still require the existing finite/stable fragment; ordinary comptime parameter defaults may use the supported comptime value/control-flow operations and are checked by the function-phase validator. Clause-parameter default normalization and defer remain separate, unimplemented features.

The existing call plan executes explicit arguments in source order and supplies missing defaults afterwards with earlier parameter bindings. Defaults are prepared but not evaluated merely because a function is declared. Explicitly supplying an input skips its default. `development/examples/comptime-defaults.fl` includes Type defaults, computed Integer widths, prior-parameter dependencies, generic defaults, and a recursive default skipped by an explicit argument. Generic inference now excludes declaration-bound default types from concrete caller evidence; those defaults are substituted only after instance inference. Concrete default types can still contribute inference evidence.

Rejections cover mutually dependent default preparation, unsatisfied default-call requirements and runtime callees in comptime defaults. One robustness issue was exposed: the recursive interpreter can overflow a small host test-thread stack at the default depth-128 limit. The budget regression uses an explicit depth of 8 and checks DepthExhausted; this does not establish host-stack safety at the default limit. The remaining issue is recorded in the implementation plan.

## Interpreter recursion stack regression (2026-10-08)

The small-stack overflow reported in the ordinary-default work was reproduced and repaired. In the unoptimized development build, the monolithic expression match reserved temporaries for many unrelated arms in each recursive frame. The pattern matcher had the same issue, exposed by extending the regression to nested or-patterns. Dispatch is now small, with separate non-inlined expression and pattern evaluators. Existing fuel accounting, depth accounting, argument/default order, transfer propagation and pattern binding rollback remain in their original shared entrypoints.

The ordinary-default test now uses the default depth-128 budget again. A separate regression explicitly creates a 2 MiB host thread and checks recursive calls, 384 nested expressions, and 384 nested patterns against depth budgets 128, 256 and usize::MAX (the latter retains the existing implementation cap of 256). Every case returns DepthExhausted, and a subsequent normal invocation succeeds on the same interpreter. These are concrete debug-build/stack-size regressions; arbitrary smaller host stacks and a fully heap-framed evaluator are not claimed supported.

## Source normal-form type heads (2026-10-08)

Type-parameter, Type-result normal-form heads now have a connected source path. The parser recognizes `pure comptime fn Head<T: Type> -> Type` with block or expression bodies; the resolver registers its head and clause scope, and lowering enters/restores that scope while retaining the pure/comptime/head markers. Elaboration checks parameter kinds, the result type, body and formation contracts. Applied heads produce `Term::NormalForm { head, sort: Type, arguments }`; aliases, generic signatures and ordinary comptime Type-value transport preserve that term.

NIR uses the displayed `normal-form` definition tag in its function metadata to distinguish this non-invocable definition from ordinary runtime/comptime entrypoints. It is not an additional executable stage. Phase validation checks its body under comptime availability rules, rejects ordinary calls to heads, and both interpreter entry modes reject invoking such a definition. Head application never evaluates its body, including a well-typed body that would recurse forever. The type solver is not given a body-based equality rule: Identity<u8> versus u8, and distinct heads with identical bodies, remain unproved.

`development/examples/normal-form-types.fl` covers aliases, generic signatures, Type-value transport, a nonterminating unused head body and type requirements. Source rejection tests cover mismatched arity, unsatisfied formation requirements, invalid body results and ordinary invocation; a module test checks identity through reexport. Non-Type value parameters, dependent parameter telescopes, optional head arguments, inferred results and complete loose/residual normalization remain incomplete. Existing arbitrary value/clause mechanisms are not silently reclassified as supported normal-form inputs.

## Contextual normal-form conditionals and blocks

Dependent normal-form inputs now retain owned conditional and block structure around contextual literals and independently typed expressions. Source conditions are checked as Bool, statements retain ordinary elaboration, and block-local bindings do not escape. Generic substitution, phase checks, required-function discovery and materialization visit all contained ordinary expressions. Each new input form has S-expression Display; divergence inspection is iterative.

Once the earlier Type input arrives, preparation checks both ordinary branches against that type, including literal range checks. It does not execute their calls or effects. Converted literals are held in an invocation-local cache keyed by immutable node identity, then moved into the selected execution path. Only the selected branch runs; local cleanup and return propagation follow ordinary block behavior. Thus an unselected overflowing literal still fails its ordinary type check, while an unselected divergent function call does not run. Both preparation and execution are bounded.

`development/examples/contextual-normal-form-inputs.fl` covers branch selection, condition/statement effects, mutation order, generic substitution, early returns, local bindings and skipped recursive calls. ### Normal-form tuple value inputs

Captured-state mutation remains explicitly rejected pending closure effect/resource checking, as before. ## Executable range patterns

Range patterns now support exact Integer, fixed-width integer and Char subjects: `a..b`, `a..=b`, `a..`, `..b`, and `..=b`. `..` is parsed and lowered as an unrestricted pattern. Inclusive ends survive AST lowering; quoted/computed endpoints resolve in the surrounding expression scope rather than introducing binders. Endpoint parsing keeps alternatives, propagation and guards outside the completed range while allowing endpoint projections/applications.

Lowering elaborates endpoint expressions against the subject type. The residual pattern binds the subject once, evaluates present endpoints once from left to right, and performs comparisons without incrementing/decrementing bounds (so maximum/minimum machine values do not overflow). Empty/reversed intervals fail normally. Endpoint control flow or failure propagates before subsequent endpoint evaluation. NIR adds `(scalar-less-equal ...)` for fixed-width integer and Char comparisons; Integer reuses its budgeted arithmetic operations. Bool/Str/custom ordering protocols are not provided by this implementation. Literal/negated-literal range unions now contribute to interval coverage, including fixed-width boundaries and the valid Char domain. Dynamic endpoints and unfamiliar computations remain conservative and require an independent coverage proof or fallback.

## Interval coverage in pattern matrices

`elaboration::interval_coverage` extracts bounded symbolic constraints from supported scalar literals and pure residual range guards without running code. It partitions each scalar column at exact Integer cuts, then recursively checks the remaining pattern columns for every inhabited cell. Fixed-width integer endpoints use arbitrary-precision successor arithmetic, and Char uses two valid Unicode scalar intervals, excluding surrogate code points. Unknown expressions/outer dynamic bounds provide no coverage evidence. This is program coverage analysis, not PTC; the existing PTC structural view is used only to identify the type domain.

## Ordinary scalar ordering expressions

Ordinary `<`, `<=`, `>` and `>=` now support fixed-width integers and Char as well as exact Integer. NIR adds `(scalar-less ...)` alongside `(scalar-less-equal ...)`; greater comparisons negate the appropriate ordered predicate without swapping operand evaluation. All specialization, materialization and phase/dependency traversals retain both operands. ## IEEE scalar float comparisons

Builtin f32/f64 equality and ordering now execute through scalar NIR comparisons, following the IEEE formats specified in `docs/basics/primitives.md`. NaN compares unequal to every value, including itself, and every ordered comparison involving NaN is false. Signed zeros compare equal; infinities and subnormals retain their numeric ordering. Operand precision must agree, and float literals can take the other operand's precision on either side. Computed float value patterns use the same equality semantics and still require a fallback for coverage.

NIR now has explicit `scalar-greater` and `scalar-greater-equal` nodes with named left/right fields. Neither direction is implemented as the negation of a different ordered comparison, which would be incorrect for NaN. Source order and single evaluation are preserved; specialization, required dependencies, dispatch materialization, phases and stable-default traversal handle the nodes. Integer/Char interval analysis recognizes the new directions, but float comparisons do not become PTC equalities or integer interval evidence. This implements comparison results, not floating-point arithmetic, floating environment flags/traps or the associated NaN/Infinity source members.

## Versioned program arithmetic and range proofs

`elaboration::verification` now provides an independent mathematical-integer specification fragment. Program values have owner/local/version identities; `Facts::assign` and `invalidate` advance a place's version, and proof replay rejects stale dependent values while permitting unrelated place changes. Facts are trusted inputs established by the caller's analysis/checks; the module does not infer ownership or aliasing and callers must invalidate every affected place for memory writes. No program propositions or these identities enter PTC.

Polynomials are canonical sorted sums with exact integer coefficients, at most degree three and configurable term/work/coefficient-size limits. Addition, subtraction and multiplication normalize equal monomials and remove zero coefficients. Expansion and coefficient growth fail transactionally with Unknown reasons. Interval evaluation preserves repeated-variable square/cube bounds and handles signed coefficients. It proves containment in explicit targets, including 1–128-bit machine ranges, and exports immutable range proofs with expression, premises, enclosure and target. Replay rechecks current premises and recomputes containment. Conservative interval failure is `InsufficientBounds`, not a false proposition; e.g. the cross-term fact `x*x+x >= 0` for integers is not inferred by this fragment. This is bounded interval reasoning over cubic expressions, not a complete cubic inequality decision procedure.

The new IR/value/proof Displays use deterministic S-expressions. Source `assumes`, predicate lowering, control-flow facts, alias/effect invalidation and machine-operation obligation discharge still require frontend integration. The proof of a final expression's range does not by itself authorize unsafe intermediate machine operations; every operation needs its own prerequisite evidence.

## Branch-aware program range facts

`elaboration::verification::Facts` now supports budgeted branch snapshots, interval refinement, six integer comparisons with either truth value, short-circuit `Condition` trees and convex control-flow joins. A branch-shared version allocator gives separate assignments distinct identities even when both branches assign the same range. Joins preserve unchanged identities, create new merge identities for changed/missing values, discard unavailable bounds and exclude unreachable alternatives. Contradictory paths cannot yield executable range proofs. A proof also retains its analysis lineage, so another analysis with coincidentally identical IDs/bounds cannot replay it.

Compound condition application is transactional: failed work/size/depth budgets or stale identities do not publish partial refinements. Conditions are limited to 128 nested levels and use the shared arithmetic budget; `or` never publishes both alternatives as unconditional facts. All new verification structures display as S-expressions. This remains a program-analysis API: callers must establish each condition through a successful check or selected control-flow edge. It has not yet been wired into the source/NIR control-flow pass, alias-effect invalidation, loop invariants, or machine arithmetic admission. Bounds are finite intervals; interior disequalities and cross-variable correlations can lose precision.

## NIR program range flow

`verification::flow::analyze` now consumes an elaborated NIR function and returns ordered check/arithmetic snapshots plus its conservative exit facts. It initializes fixed-width integer parameter domains, follows local bindings and writes, records successful-check refinements, splits conditional/short-circuit edges, excludes returned paths and joins surviving ranges. Operand ranges are captured in evaluation order. Exact Integer add/subtract/multiply/negate operations produce interval results; comparisons recognize a scalar local against a constant in either operand order. Report points and failures retain source ranges and use S-expression Display.

Unknown calls conservatively invalidate all tracked local refinements, restoring only their type domains. Loop bodies start from type domains and can use their guard/check facts; exit analysis drops iteration-specific refinements. This is a safe overapproximation, not inferred loop invariants or a precise termination analysis. Closures, match/pattern constructs, default argument frames and other unhandled nodes explicitly return Unsupported; depth/work/size failures yield no report. Unbounded Integer parameter refinements and relational comparisons still need a richer domain. The pass is an explicit analysis API exercised from source-to-NIR tests, not yet a mandatory frontend validation or a machine-arithmetic authorization path. Fixed i8/i16/i32/i64/i128 and u8/u16/u32/u64/u128 add, subtract, multiply and nonliteral negation now elaborate and execute when program range analysis proves each operation representable. Typed `integer-binary` / `integer-negate` nodes retain the representation in their NIR types; exact comptime Integer semantics remain separate. Later checks, stale assignments, one-sided branch facts, unknown calls and a safe final expression do not authorize an overflowing intermediate operation. No implicit runtime assumption, wraparound or PTC program-state proposition is introduced.

The final elaboration gate and required-comptime snapshots both validate machine operations before delivery/invocation. Full phase traversal identifies affected owners through bodies, defaults, closures and patterns; unsupported flow analysis rejects instead of skipping hidden operations. Stable machine default expressions are range-checked, and call analysis gives defaults a separate parameter frame populated with already evaluated arguments. Diagnostics preserve the failing operation's source span. The interpreter additionally uses the checked machine kernel, validates representations/result types and reports `MachineOverflow` for forged unsafe NIR rather than wrapping.

Current admission remains conservative: closure/match/pattern flow, generic parameter ranges derived from type evidence, precise callable effect/result contracts, relational bounds and loop invariants are unfinished. Unknown calls forget refinements, and loops require checks valid for an arbitrary iteration. Pointer-sized arithmetic awaits target data. Integer division/remainder/operator protocols, native lowering and the broader resource model are not enabled by this change. Program safety validation is an elaborator responsibility; standalone interpreter phase validation is not itself a range proof.

## Scalar pattern range flow

Program range analysis now follows scalar `match` and guarded `let` candidates in their execution order. Literal success/failure edges refine current scalar identities; bindings capture the matched value's range. Guards and `and ... is ...` expressions retain their writes on failed candidates, while candidate bindings are removed before later arms or let-else bodies. Or alternatives follow first-success semantics; remapping snapshots binding values before installing destinations and removing obsolete source bindings. Successful arm results/facts join conservatively, returned paths do not produce normal results, and match-local bindings do not escape the match.

This permits checked machine arithmetic in literal fallback arms, guarded bindings, transformed patterns and closures created inside arms. The domain remains convex: an interior disequality can lose precision, and a stale scrutinee reference is not treated as its newly written value. Tuple/record/variant/type-view patterns and general relational binding evidence remain unsupported by this safety pass; these are implementation limits, not syntax/semantic restrictions added to Flurry.

### Checked polynomial relations in NIR flow

Program range facts now retain checked integer polynomial inequalities (degree at most three), distinct from PTC propositions. `Condition::PolynomialCompare` supports comparisons between symbolic arithmetic expressions, including two unknown local or direct field values. Strict integer inequalities include the unit offset; equality establishes both directions; disequality remains conservative when its excluded set is nonconvex. Budgeted monotone contraction propagates unit-coefficient variable bounds. Expression enclosure also uses the checked row `q <= 0` through the sound rewrites `p <= upper(p-q)` and `p >= lower(p+q)`, preserving correlations such as `start <= end` when proving `end - start`. NIR add/subtract/multiply/negate now carry bounded polynomial expressions during evaluation, and each machine operation is checked before a later predicate can use its result. Degree/term expansion limits discard optional symbolic precision while retaining ordinary interval safety checks; they do not ban higher-degree executable expressions whose intermediate ranges are already safe.

Rows are keyed by program-value versions. Forks retain current rows; live branch joins retain common rows referring to unchanged identities. Writes and scope removal make dependent rows unavailable, and unknown calls still havoc affected values. Proofs record their relational dependencies as S-expressions and replay rejects lost relations even when scalar marginal intervals are unchanged. Budget exhaustion during a compound assumption leaves the incoming facts unchanged. General polynomial elimination, arbitrary coefficient isolation, correlation transfer through copied/captured aggregates, independently renamed field identities at branch joins, memory aliasing and interprocedural contracts remain incomplete. A degree-three expression is not a promise that this procedure can decide every inequality.

## Direct-call program preconditions

Normalized functions now carry a separate `preconditions: Vec<Expr>` / `(program-requires ...)` field. Resolved ordinary-parameter predicates in `requires` are elaborated as effect-free Bool expressions; type requirements remain `TypePredicate` values handled by PTC. Contract preparation retains the separation in both ordinary elaboration and required-comptime snapshots. Non-function declarations, normal-form heads and trait/implementation members do not silently acquire unsupported program contracts.

Range analysis checks predicate arithmetic in declaration order, then admits each entry condition while analyzing the body. At a direct call it freezes arguments in evaluation order, copies their justified scalar/aggregate relations into a fresh parameter frame, evaluates defaults in that frame and proves the callee predicates before treating the call as valid. Earlier requirements can justify later predicate arithmetic. Default expressions themselves are checked without assuming the call's as-yet-unproved preconditions. The mandatory validation gate includes contracted functions and their callers even if their bodies contain no machine arithmetic. Boolean parameters use a logical 0/1 proof encoding, without specifying their runtime layout; comparisons, negation and short-circuit values participate in call proofs.

The interpreter checks instantiated entry predicates after binding all arguments and before entering the body, including raw host calls and generic declaration instances. Failure rejects the invocation before dependent body operations and allows a later independent invocation to succeed. Taking a contracted declaration as an ordinary function value currently diagnoses contract erasure: callable-type program contracts, trait/member program contracts and ensures are still unimplemented. The automatic program verifier remains bounded and incomplete, especially for unbounded Integer parameters and richer specifications; this milestone does not complete memory/resource verification.

## Named results and checked program postconditions

Named results now lower from `-> result: Type` into explicit HIR/NIR bindings. The binding is available only while lowering `ensures`, so a body or `requires` cannot read an uninitialized result; body locals with the same spelling have independent identities. NIR functions retain `(result-binding ...)` and `(program-ensures ...)`, separate from type requirements and entry predicates. Normal-form named return syntax also preserves its metadata without unfolding the head; program contracts on such heads and trait members remain unsupported.

The program verifier checks postcondition arithmetic and entailment at every explicit return and reachable fallthrough. Closure returns temporarily use their own exit context and cannot satisfy or violate the surrounding function's contract. Earlier proved postconditions may support later ones; unknown obligations reject the definition. Interpreter invocation binds the actual returned value and checks instantiated postconditions before handing it to the caller, including generic/required-comptime invocation paths. These checks do not imply termination, ownership or effect correctness.

Direct callers can now use result-only postconditions for supported scalar/owned-aggregate result shapes. The isolated result frame imports the mathematical consequence of an already-verified guarantee rather than re-executing specification arithmetic at the call site; the callee still proves and checks that arithmetic at its exits. This supports scalar bounds and relations between returned record fields. Parameter-dependent guarantees are conservatively omitted because parameters in `ensures` describe exit-state bindings, which may differ from original caller arguments. Unsupported result domains retain the baseline unknown result; old-state/effect summaries, callable/trait contracts, outcomes and broader verification remain open.

### Entry snapshots and input/result contract relations

Program postconditions now support the `'old` view over ordinary entry parameters. AST lowering emits a dedicated HIR `TakeOld`; elaboration rewrites parameter reads under the view to explicit NIR `EntrySnapshot` bindings. The metadata has deterministic S-expression Display. The interpreter initializes these bindings from evaluated arguments before entry predicates/body execution. It freezes parameter values, not the evaluation of the entire old expression: a guarded `(value + 1)'old` remains guarded at the exit. Nested views reuse the same entry binding. Outside postconditions, and for exit-result bindings, the view produces a diagnostic.

The program verifier materializes owned record/tuple components before taking their snapshots. Frozen roots and their component identities survive conservative call/loop havoc; ordinary mutable locals still lose observations. Exact equalities allow stored degree-two/three expressions to use immutable input versions across later writes. A computed RHS is frozen before overwriting a source it reads; bounded relation projection preserves links to surviving snapshots. None of these facts enter PTC or grant access to referenced allocations.

Direct-call guarantees may mention the result and explicit entry snapshots. The ordered argument/default frame binds callee snapshots after argument evaluation. Caller entry values travel through private frame bindings; returning evidence is mapped back only when both the lineage and value versions still match. Exact current equalities connect intermediate input copies when transporting polynomial guarantees. Bare callee parameters continue to mean exit values and are excluded from this summary. NIR validation rejects malformed snapshot roots and writes/rebindings to protected snapshot slots.

Scope remains the supported effect-free predicate and owned-value analysis fragment. This does not implement heap/pointee history, memory permissions, full Once/Clone/Copy legality, first-class callable program contracts or trait-method contracts. Unknown value domains and more general polynomial obligations remain subject to the bounded verifier's explicit limitations.

### Trait and implementation program contracts

Trait method declarations now retain a separate `ProgramContract` containing entry predicates, exit predicates, named results and entry snapshots. It has a stable S-expression Display and explicit type/local substitution. Type requirements and implementation selection remain in PTC; program predicates do not influence implementation priority. Ordinary, inherent and comptime member bodies elaborate the same supported predicate fragment as free functions.

Implementation checking maps declaration-side parameters and results to the chosen body. An omitted program entry clause inherits the interface domain. An explicit entry clause must be provably no stronger under the trait's conditions; its predicate arithmetic must also be valid. Inherited guarantees remain attached to the body even when parameter/result names differ or the implementation omits a named result. For an explicitly weaker domain, inherited guarantees are guarded by the original trait entry conditions over frozen inputs, so they do not acquire obligations outside the trait domain. Omitted-domain implementations need no redundant guard. Explicit implementation guarantees remain checked too. The same preparation runs for required-comptime execution snapshots, before they can contribute a Type-valued result.

Trait calls use the instantiated declaration contract, including parent-interface provenance and interface arguments. Generic callers can prove entry obligations and use input/result guarantees without examining a concrete implementation. Ordered argument/default frames retain declaration-side bindings. The interpreter checks the public interface's entry conditions before entering the selected body, even if that body has a weaker domain, and the body enforces its inherited exit conditions. First-class uses that erase nonempty interface entry contracts remain rejected; a method with only a result guarantee can still be used as a function value, conservatively losing that guarantee at indirect call sites.

Contracted function tails now check `if`/`match` alternatives before joining their facts. Explicit returns use the same tail traversal. This preserves branch-dependent guarantees, including a weaker implementation returning a different value outside the trait's input domain; it does not infer general disjunctive invariants for arbitrary intermediate computations.

### Source whole-local move analysis — 2026-10-08

`verification::moves::analyze` transfers whole-local availability through ordered evaluation, ordinary explicit call arguments, let, root assignment, aggregate construction, if, short-circuit Boolean expressions, lexical blocks and return. ### Closure capture ownership and invocation-state reports — 2026-10-08

Move analysis now acquires closure captures in their declared order, copying or moving each source according to the supplied delivery evidence. ### Local closure invocation environment transfer — 2026-10-08

Known local closures now retain body provenance independently of their resource state. Invocation reads the current stored capture subtrees into a fresh parameter frame, analyzes the body, merges capture states across returning paths and writes them back into the same environment. Calling does not move the whole callable. Read-only repeated calls succeed; repeated consumption and consumption after a conditional earlier call are rejected. Cleanup after a call excludes capture responsibilities already transferred by its body.

Whole-local closure moves/assignments carry provenance to the new binding, invalidate moved sources and preserve ordinary availability checks. Branch joins retain provenance only when both paths identify the same stored callable. A generation identifies each stored receiver: if argument evaluation replaces or moves it, the analysis reports an explicit limitation instead of writing invocation effects into a different environment with coincidentally identical body provenance.

### Object construction state and ordered cleanup candidates (2026-10-08)

Ownership aggregates now retain an independent construction flag alongside field availability. Moving every field out of a completed aggregate no longer makes its state identical to moving the entire aggregate. A completed enclosing object can still require user Drop even with no remaining fields. Partial initialization retains initialized child responsibilities without granting a whole-object destructor; installing the final missing field completes the object. Whole moves/installations, branch joins, invocation remapping and overwrite state preserve these flags. Legacy `remaining`, `replace` and `retire` results still enumerate leaves only; callers needing enclosing obligations must obtain `cleanup_tree` first.

`State::cleanup_tree` produces a bounded hierarchical snapshot: parent construction state plus live children in reverse field order. `Report::cleanup_sites` captures typed structural candidates at explicit returns, implicit function ends, break/continue, lexical retirement and replacement. Exit sites interleave pending argument/field/capture values with lexical locals using acquisition anchors, so nested locals are retired on the correct side of previously prepared values. Loop edges exclude preparations outside the target loop and do not duplicate local retirement sites. Replacement captures the old partial hierarchy before installing the new value; self-move has no old-object cleanup. The new structures have stable S-expression Display implementations.

These are not executable Drop plans. User Drop selection and captured environment evidence, its actual reads/moves and post-Drop remaining fields, conditional execution flags, expression-temporary and pattern-decomposition integration, dependency checks, error/effect unwinding and runtime execution remain required. In particular, the children of a cleanup-tree are the pre-Drop state and cannot simply be executed unconditionally after an arbitrary user Drop.

### Aggregate pointer-origin delivery (2026-10-09)

Resource analysis now carries known pointer leaves relative to a delivered value. Tuple/record construction evaluates each field once with the existing pending-cleanup protocol, retaining its origins before later field effects. Struct fields follow declaration order even when named inputs are written in a different order. Local and field delivery snapshots the source's origin subtree before ownership transfer; installation rebases slot paths under the destination while leaving pointee identities unchanged. Whole/partial replacement clears the previous subtree, and self-moves preserve delivered origins.

Aggregate block results and conditionals propagate those origin trees. Both live branches must supply a known leaf before their candidates are joined; returning a value containing a reference to retired block-local storage drops that leaf's provenance. Tests cover nested construction/field moves, scope-exiting moves, exact replacement, conditional dependencies and unavailable owners. This does not yet propagate origins through arbitrary pattern decomposition, enum payload variants, temporary projections or aggregate-valued call results; general interprocedural storage/escape contracts and executable cleanup remain incomplete.

### Acquired structural cleanup plans (2026-10-09)

Drop now exposes a two-stage interface: `acquire_cleanup` fixes destructor resolutions recursively for known struct/tuple/closure layouts; `plan_cleanup` consumes those bindings and a current ownership state without selecting implementations again. The luna adapter obtains Drop identity from trusted LangItems. A plan invokes a constructed parent's Drop before reverse-order remaining fields and releases each completed ownership responsibility after its children. Partially initialized parents skip whole-object Drop, moved positions produce no steps, and all-fields-moved constructed parents retain their own responsibility. Access checks reuse the captured method and supported state-preserving memory footprint. Plans retain their initial state snapshot and each invocation's access evidence; subsequent steps require normal completion.

The subset explicitly rejects conditional construction without a runtime guard, unknown/enum layouts without active-variant evidence, stale worlds/assumptions/layouts, runtime environment acquisition and undischarged program specifications. Type traversal, layout traversal and planning are bounded; failures leave input ownership state unchanged. Acquisition still needs wiring into actual ownership creation/moves and executable cleanup lowering; the API does not claim to execute Drop or free backing allocations.

### Source ownership to captured cleanup plans (2026-10-09)

`luna::protocols::analyze_cleanup` now connects ownership analysis to a `CleanupSession` in one immutable package/implementation world. Local establishment, retained temporaries and successful argument/component preparation acquire fixed Drop choices. The arena retains captured field/variant subtrees, so subsequent field and whole-value moves can reuse the same choices. Planning refuses types absent from the arena and never performs selection. This arena is limited to choices without runtime environment values; it is not a general cross-world responsibility transport mechanism.

Each supported structural candidate is wrapped once in `planned-cleanup`, together with its checked plan. Local exit/replacement uses the actual current state; temporaries retain their decomposition/tag evidence, and pending completed values use their full prepared shape. Failure, closure/default nested reports and converged loop reports preserve their existing scheduling boundaries. The old evidence lists remain observations, not additional cleanup schedules. Conditional temporary presence is rejected until guarded cleanup is implemented. Missing fields needed by a destructor are diagnosed at the actual cleanup point, and a failed analysis returns no partial report.

The CLI accepts optional `--drop-protocol <trait>` with resource analysis. Both protocol names resolve to explicit, unique source identities; output identifies `(stage acquired-cleanup-plans)`. Without that option the existing ownership-obligation mode is unchanged. This remains analysis: it does not invoke destructors, provide arbitrary destructor post-state transitions, or certify full program safety.

A release replaces that position's interpreter representation with Unit; it is not an allocation-deallocator ABI. Rejected predicates and exhausted execution fuel stop later operations while retaining completed writes/releases. There is no implicit retry or rollback.

### Scheduled source cleanup execution (2026-10-09)

`luna::cleanup::prepare_source` publishes an `Executable` containing the concrete graph and a per-instance cleanup schedule. It analyzes every reachable concrete function, adds captured destructor bodies to the materialization roots, and repeats until all demanded functions have schedules. Cleanup sites must map to one runtime boundary; ambiguous normalized source boundaries are rejected rather than merged across different executions. Each site retains ordered local identities, field paths and previously validated cleanup programs. The bounded IIR expression visitor is now public for this consumer.

`Interpreter::with_cleanup_schedule` enables execution of that published schedule. Scope completion, return, function completion, break/continue, replacement and supported predicate rejection now execute local cleanup at the matching boundary. Function entry parameters are owned before runtime precondition checking. The active concrete function identity is saved/restored across calls, so transferred arguments and returned owners are cleaned only by the responsible frame. Field replacement cleans the old field after RHS evaluation using a projection into the existing parent storage. Ordinary predicate rejection cleans the callee and then caller's remaining owners; a failure inside cleanup stops subsequent cleanup across the active call chain, without retry or rollback.

Eight source execution groups check scope ordering, whole moves, returned responsibility transfer, explicit returns, break/continue, self-move assignment, whole/field replacement, sibling pointer storage identity, generic calls, by-value argument transfer, enum dispatch, cross-frame predicate rejection, destructor failure and external-entry precondition rejection. The implementation does not infer ownership by enumerating interpreter environment values; it follows the resource pass's schedule.

This is an explicit API path, not yet the default `--interpret` mode. Publication rejects nontrivial temporary/prepared owners without runtime storage mappings, closure schedules, cleanup inside default-argument environments, result postcondition scheduling and interface preconditions needing argument frames. Trivial intrinsic scalar/pointer temporaries whose captured plans consist solely of releases use the evaluator's ordinary representation disposal. General unwind/termination policy, runtime capability environments and complete memory safety remain unfinished. Scheduled reference execution is not a complete safety certificate.

The updated evidence survives returning and forwarding the containing closure. Failure exits only propagate resource state for unwinding, never establish a normal continuation.

### Tuple variadic calls and preparation lifetimes

Default positional variadics now collect heterogeneous tuples, including empty collections, in ordinary/generic calls and inherent/trait methods. `program/arguments.rs` separates declaration routing from source-order evaluation. NIR/IIR `(call-preparation (statements ...) (result ...))` retains internal input bindings without introducing source `let` full-expression boundaries. This distinction is necessary for projected temporary owners: normal return, early exit and failed runtime checks must preserve the same destructor order as explicit package construction. Phase validation checks the preparation shape and unique bindings. Type substitution, visitors, materialization, memory/range/resource analysis, interpretation and cleanup scheduling recognize the node; generated bookkeeping uses empty diagnostic anchors rather than borrowing user-expression cleanup locations.

Writes reinstall the selected subtree and reconstruct ancestors only when every field is present. Conditional cleanup reads these tokens and releases them after destruction. Shared capture cells retain enclosing-owner guards so moving a closure does not let cleanup through its former owner retire the new owner's captures. ### Construction implications across ownership joins

Ownership states now retain bounded, descendant-only implications of the form “if this construction token is present, this descendant token has the following availability.” Joins keep a fact only when every contributing path on which the antecedent is present agrees. An empty antecedent contributes no live-path evidence. Unguarded reads remain unchanged. Guarded cleanup can therefore call a field-reading destructor after a conditional whole-object move, while genuine partial-field losses still reject. These are program ownership facts, not PTC propositions. Stable S-expression dumps expose `(construction-implications (if-constructed ... (facts ...)))`.

Facts rebase through capture import, exit snapshots and writeback, and retire with their owner. Moves invalidate facts about the transferred subtree. Installation/replacement invalidate ancestor premises asserting absence: reconstruction can introduce new live-parent paths not covered by old negative facts. Positive facts about untouched descendants remain valid because newly completed objects have all fields present. The mutation audit found a pre-existing construction-flag gap: a last field write may complete an object on only some paths. Such a previously empty parent now becomes Conditional, so its destructor is not silently omitted. Refinement still rejects contradictory premises; zero-budget import/writeback leaves the destination untouched. Further reconstruction implications are described below. This remains a structural ownership analysis, not general relational program-state solving.

### Reconstruction facts and selected enum payload cleanup

A field installation/replacement now retains positive ancestor-guard facts about untouched descendants. Negative facts are invalidated because newly completed parents cannot inherit old absent-field premises. When a previously absent parent becomes conditionally constructed, the new live-parent paths establish full field presence; the verifier records those implications without granting any unguarded access. Source examples exercise destructors reading both nested fields after replacement and after partial reconstruction.

Reconstruction inference consumes analysis fuel. `install_with_budget` and `replace_with_budget` stage only the affected owner's hierarchy and implications and commit on success; an exhausted prefix preserves every original owner. Source assignment analysis uses the budgeted replacement entrypoint. The existing low-level `install`/`replace` convenience APIs retain their unmetered structural behavior for trusted callers. Exhaustion/recovery tests exercise every budget prefix from 0 through 199 for both operations, including another owner's preservation.

Selected decomposed enum payloads now plan conditional cleanup with explicit `VariantSelection` evidence. Parent Drop/release remain guarded by the parent construction token, while payload fields retain their own independent guards and reverse order. An unconstructed parent does not suppress live children. Opaque conditional enums still guard tag dispatch with construction presence. Missing variant evidence, wrong payload shape, invalid tags and exhausted planning budgets reject; this does not infer a common payload layout across different enum variants.
