### Distinct closure bodies retain separate capture evidence

Closure provenance now carries a flat set of code candidates when branch results have the same full callable type. Each candidate retains its own captured callable and enum-domain evidence; capture binding IDs from one body cannot be reused for another. Public callable inputs validate each candidate's definition, type, capture paths, uniqueness and budget. Legacy expression-only evidence returns unknown where it cannot represent these choices. Displays include `(choices ...)` in the existing S-expression format.

Invocation prepares ordinary arguments once, preserving each argument's evidence at its evaluation point, then analyzes every possible body from that prepared caller state. Normal ownership continuations join independently from failed continuations. Cleanup publication keeps each body's own context and emits one joined caller failure continuation; runtime selects the actual body. A candidate set does not restore consumed captures. This is conservative ownership analysis: code-specific ownership correlations lost by an outer join are not reconstructed merely from code provenance.

Current boundaries: candidates must be closures with equal full types; mixed named-function/closure sets and differing environment layouts are not supplied with a new common representation here. Distinct instantiated bodies sharing one source identity remain rejected until context identity can distinguish them. Recursive aggregate return summaries still require separate fixed-point work.

Joining a named-only alternative set flattens all its targets into the mixed set. The common preparation frame evaluates each argument once. Named candidates export the prepared scalar, aggregate and enum premises into the existing contextual named-call analysis; closure candidates import the same snapshots into their own parameter frames. ### Empty-environment closure memory footprints

`memory::infer_closure` now derives a parameter-relative footprint for an empty-environment runtime closure, including reads/writes, checked-predicate failure and pointer results from both early returns and the tail expression. Calls to named helpers use complete package fixed points. Anonymous code is not registered under a synthetic function declaration. The existing `ArgumentSummary` representation and S-expression display carry this expression footprint; malformed parameter frames and exhausted budgets fail explicitly.

Closure invocation snapshots pointer origins with each ordinary argument's evaluation. For every possible body, it checks the footprint against those actual targets before applying the body's ownership continuation, and unions all established pointer-result targets. Named members of a mixed set use their ordinary memory summaries. Construction-side and invocation-side body analysis establish conditional borrowed parameter roots; those roots never enter the cleanup order. The runtime body and cleanup context remain the original closure, so failures clean the owning caller's pointees exactly once.

The previous blanket rejection of pointer-taking immediate closures is replaced by actual footprint checking. Regressions cover writes, aliases, early returns, direct/temporary calls, mixed targets, reading after the actual owner moved, and failure cleanup. Captured environments still require an environment memory contract; unknown higher-order memory callees and pointer-bearing escaping aggregates retain their existing restrictions.

### Aggregate callable-return memory fixed points

Unsupported summaries leave evidence unknown, while budget/depth exhaustion propagates as failure instead of being hidden by the optional supplement.

Function-argument-dependent aggregate return identities still need contextual memory premises, and enum/captured-code result summaries remain separate work. This extension does not unfold normal-form type heads or send resource facts to PTC.

### Callable parameter origins and finite recursive cleanup contexts

Memory summaries now retain symbolic code sources as `CallableInput { parameter, fields }`. A result can combine named targets and forwarded inputs without unfolding function type heads. Call sites substitute the already evaluated argument snapshots simultaneously, so caller-relative inputs are never reinterpreted in the callee's frame. This covers scalar and owned struct/tuple/record leaves, generic/transitive forwarding, branch alternatives and recursive return fixed points. Later argument effects cannot retroactively change an earlier argument's code evidence. Default expressions use the prepared-parameter code environment; copying that environment consumes analysis budget.

The ownership pass can supplement missing scalar or aggregate return identities from these converged summaries after substituting actual named-code inputs. It preserves stronger contextual evidence and never drops an unknown/anonymous alternative to manufacture a named-only footprint. An unresolved forwarded input remains insufficient to invoke a callee in body-derived memory inference. Higher-order invocation effects, enum-tag-dependent memory callees and general captured anonymous-code memory summaries remain separate work; forwarding code is not a blanket higher-order contract.

Default stability admits environment-free function representations without invoking their bodies. Resource delivery still requires a real Copy capability. The driver permits declared/assumed Copy for a `Term::Function` only after establishing that no custom Drop applies in the current world; it does not infer intrinsic Copy or authorize duplication of captured closure resources. A default that consumes a still-required affine prepared argument remains rejected.

Contextual cleanup publication now records finite `ContextAlias` backedges when a recursive named call has the same instantiated function and exact callable/enum premises as a published ancestor. Changed premises produce their own specialization before a backedge can be reused. Only the cleanup specialization key is reused: each runtime invocation keeps its own frame and responsibility flags. Schedule installation rejects self/non-ancestor targets, mismatched callees, duplicate aliases and missing target/parent scopes before execution. The alias and symbolic-input displays use S-expressions.

### Named callback premises in higher-order memory inference

`memory::infer_with_inputs` accepts concrete code evidence indexed by parameter and owned field path. Its worklist key contains both the instantiated function and those premises, so two calls of the same higher-order helper cannot share a footprint derived for different callbacks. `Summary.callable_inputs` records the conditional premises in its S-expression dump. Before a body uses them, inference checks parameter/path shape, runtime phase, generic arguments, exact callable signature, nonempty candidate sets and duplicate identities. Public inputs cannot supply `Unknown`, forwarded symbols or the private `NoReturn` worklist bottom.

Calls now snapshot arguments before requesting callee summaries. Concrete named leaves specialize the callee; unresolved forwarding leaves retain their symbolic behavior. Internal bottom inputs allow factories and recursive summaries to converge without claiming that an unknown callback has no effects. The completed footprint still accounts for every candidate's accesses, rejection possibility and returned pointer targets. An unresolved or anonymous alternative is never discarded to retain only the named subset.

Ownership analysis uses the same prepared argument evidence for direct calls and dynamically selected named candidates. Candidate bodies share one evaluation of actual arguments; signature and access checks run against that completed frame. Named-call cleanup publication rechecks the contextual memory footprint before introducing borrowed parameter roots. Closures can also receive named-code parameter premises, separate from captured-code premises. Their construction-only unresolved callback obligations are deferred until invocation; publication still rejects unresolved invoked obligations. This does not give an opaque callback a memory contract or infer a general higher-order specification.

The implementation covers scalar and aggregate callback inputs, instantiated generic callbacks, transitive/recursive forwarding, factory-produced code, pointer writes/reads and returned pointer dependencies. General anonymous callback summaries passed into named helpers, enum-tag-dependent memory callees and unrestricted higher-order contracts remain separate work. Invalid direct parameter binding frames now produce a diagnostic before argument-snapshot indexing.

### Implementation-specific dependent associated defaults

Trait declarations retain checked symbolic default expressions when they contain associated references; they do not publish one implementation's result as the trait default. Associated declaration contexts have their enclosing Self/interface evidence, like default methods. Independent defaults retain the existing completed-value path. Runtime calls in default initializers are rejected. Forward edges and cycles broken by explicit overrides work; a cycle remaining in the selected implementation fails through the existing bounded demand mechanism.

### Inherited initializer environments and Self-specialized comptime calls

Selected associated initialization now substitutes its Self and interface arguments before inherited/cross-interface member lookup. Parent origin and full interface arguments remain part of selection, including same-named members on distinct parents. Queries use the selected implementation's type context and capability premises only while checking that initializer; declaration templates are still checked independently under their declared bounds. A concrete implementation cannot supply missing evidence to a trait definition or a later unrelated function.

Required comptime roots also receive this initializer substitution before dependency discovery. A generic body can demand associated values not previously encountered syntactically in the initializer, using the existing per-implementation cycle guard. Defaults containing Self/type-parameter operands remain symbolic templates even when the result type is scalar and there is no direct AssociatedValue node. Reference dispatch has a crate-private context-taking entrypoint for these private snapshots; runtime IIR entrypoints retain their original context construction. This supports Self-specialized calls for concrete and unconstrained generic implementations.

### Given capabilities in private comptime snapshots

The previously failing conditional-Self probe now executes. Private associated-initializer snapshots carry the selected implementation's declared capability premises alongside its rigid type context. Materialization uses these premises for qualification and skips executable-interface construction when a queued item only discharges a given obligation. Actual method and associated-value demands still require selected implementation evidence and concrete dispatch entries. Standalone runtime IIR construction supplies no premises.

`Interpreter::for_comptime_with_assumptions` accepts caller-established trait premises in a separate interpreter-local set. It expands parent/parameter capabilities with bounded work, checks interface arity, and consumes the expansion allowance from the interpreter budget. Premises can satisfy call/type obligations; they never populate method or associated-value tables. The package is unchanged and a subsequent ordinary interpreter does not inherit them. This host API requires established premises, just as the type-solver callback requires a valid host theory; it does not prove user-supplied assertions itself.

### Selected associated type views during reference/comptime execution

Reference materialization now proves demanded associated Type projections and retains their originating Type-valued members in selected dispatch tables. It also discovers projected types in retained ordinary/generic method signatures, including methods whose concrete interface is retained independently of the current call. Complete projection normalization supplies cycle/selection checks; only implementation-selected values enter execution.

The interpreter's bounded selected-type view resolves these tables for associated value/result checking, callable signature compatibility, pointer pointee compatibility and explicit Type values. Compound types retain their structure and function phase; normal-form heads remain opaque. Constructor validation checks associated payloads against the instantiated member contract and validates override signatures against selected views. All entries are collected before signature comparison so dispatch iteration order does not determine whether another member's type is available. Missing, non-Type and cyclic selected entries reject. Closed Type values retain their earlier validation path.

### Associated type predicates across source checking and comptime invocation

Source formation checks first try the original predicate in the caller's context, preserving established abstract projection equalities. When that proof is not established, they may expose implementation-selected associated type views and retry the type proof. The bounded transformation retains And/Or/Not structure and opaque normal-form heads. It applies to type predicates only; program-state/memory specifications do not enter PTC.

Reference materialization now collects type dependencies from function, retained method and formation predicates, including projections absent from signatures and expression bodies. The comptime interpreter substitutes selected type views before handing unresolved type predicates to its host solver, charging this transformation to the invocation budget. Ordinary function instances in `for_comptime` now recheck their type requirements before instance publication. The low-level ordinary `Interpreter::new` entry retains its existing caller-validated static-contract convention.

### 条件 impl 的世界查询与 comptime 快照身份

Trait 实现选择现在将 head matching 和条件证明衔接：实例化后的 Boolean trait 前提交给同一个 capability solver，嵌套查询共享活动集合，正向或否定递归都不能自证。当前实现世界的肯定/排除结果只加入候选局部证明上下文；Resolution 保留条件证明和嵌套查询，支持检查索引身份/版本及局部证明重放。`verify_condition_support` 只验证条件支持，不是完整的 admission/head/selection 验证器。inherent impl 的条件路径尚未迁移到这套接口。

必需 comptime 快照只含被需求的布局，不能据此恢复完整名义类型身份。dispatch preparation 现在与该 invocation 的类型检查共享源声明建立的类型上下文，允许只用 `Box<bool>` 选择方法而不构造值或需求布局，同时保留实现初始化器的局部前提。

### 效应入口的有界词法路由核心

`nir::effects` 定义完整 operation 实例（declaration + 全部实例参数）、四类效应 ABI、入口及词法安装描述，并提供 S-expression Display。错误结果没有混入效应 ABI。`elaboration::effects::route` 在显式输入的安装链上选择最近入口；同一安装的多个匹配入口拒绝为歧义，部分覆盖保留有序外层回退且必须最终到达完整供应。分支环境排除该安装全部入口，主体的安装链保持原样。未确定的内层实例身份不能被跳过；PTC 仅证明 Type-sort 等价/不等价，非类型输入不交给 PTC，opaque head 不展开。输入结构、字符串/整数载荷和递归深度有预算；先验证作用域，再比较/克隆。返回的路由借用安装链和类型上下文，不能跨输入变更复用。

这是独立路由组件，尚未接入源码 elaboration 或运行时。输入 entry 的覆盖性标记需要后续 pattern checker 的真实证明；它不是已验证的 executable evidence，不代替操作签名检查、coverage、资源责任、continuation/async 协议或 direct-passing 安装时求值。

### 源码独立 effect 请求进入 NIR

源码 `operation(args)#` 已通过已形成实例的请求检查进入上述节点，允许行取自当前函数或已注明闭包的结果限定。支持普通位置参数、显式泛型操作和组成员投影；组本身不是可调用操作。多次请求各保留节点、使用同一允许层，不复制效应行层次。未声明允许行、缺失标签、错误参数、comptime 请求以及未注明效应的闭包借用外层环境均拒绝。泛型操作可使用当前声明给出的 trait 约束完成形成检查。

### 函数体计算环境与表达式传播

`computation_body` 在带效应结果的函数/已注明闭包边界安装共同允许行，体内 request 产生普通操作结果，边界保留 `EffectComputation`。算术、条件、短路与顺序组合复用同一行，不按请求次数复制层次；纯主体也可处于更宽的允许环境。未注明效应的闭包进入独立环境，不能借用外层允许行。

新增 `EffectRun` 保存计算表达式到当前环境的 occurrence 槽位映射，并同步 Display、类型代换、共享遍历、phase 与未实现执行拒绝。泛型结果实例化后可能仍含 residual computation；原节点只消去建立映射时的前缀。计算类型实参在作为计算参数传递时保留；表达式使用结果时才生成映射。泛型调用的结果上下文在输入推断后观察已实例化计算结果，避免先把未知 T 固定为普通类型、丢失 `T = #b bool` 的剩余效应。

程序状态分析按源码顺序检查请求实参，在请求/运行计算之后保守 havoc；循环写入扫描也视其为未知写入，不能沿用 handler 可能破坏的事实。这不是精确 memory-effect 摘要，也不代表资源/continuation 或 handler 执行完成。错误结果 ABI、开放行、隐式 effect 操作泛型实参、runtime-dependent effect 源码输入等先前未完成部分仍保留限制。

### Direct passing 的静态请求次数上界

新增程序验证层 `verification::effect_usage`，不调用 PTC。按具体函数实例迭代求解零次／至多一次／可能多次请求的有限不动点；调用实参与 callee 表达式仍使用 caller 行，调用体摘要经已检查槽位映射进入 callee 行。分支取上界，顺序执行累加，常量条件和布尔短路跳过确定不执行的路径。普通 handler 的外层请求按主体请求次数传播；direct passing 提供过程按每次安装一次传播，即使其值槽没有被读取。guard 与部分转发的外层需求也参与计算。

`interpret_effects_with_protocols` 在执行前消费此分析，拒绝不能证明至多一次交付的 Move 值槽；Copy 槽允许多次请求。原始参考解释路径仍保留 `EffectValueConsumed` 运行时检查。结果使用 S-expression 报告实例、安装来源、完整操作身份、上界和交付策略；图绑定、预算失败及重试有测试。函数主体、契约、默认值与闭包内部安装分别检查。

目前循环和未知高阶调用采用可能重复的上界，某些带退出相关性的安全路径仍需更精细的控制流证明。这是值槽请求次数检查，尚不证明普通 handler 对捕获 owner 的重复交付、全部指针访问、资源清理或跨帧退出协议，不能据此解除 cleanup gate。

### 请求次数分析保留局部控制退出

请求上界现在分别记录正常完成、return、带词法目标的 break／continue、resume 与中止；顺序组合只把正常路径送入后继。循环将正常落回与匹配的 continue 作为回边，只有回边上的非零请求会扩为可能多次；匹配的 break 汇入循环后继，其他目标继续向外传播。由此可以接受提前 return、在实参中 return、循环内单次取值后 break／return、嵌套 break，以及不发请求的 continue 循环。

调用准备和计算行映射保留 caller 实参求值的退出结果。确定失败的运行时 predicate 和 Never 结果保留中止路径，不继续统计其不可达后继。尚未细化的控制结构继续使用保守汇总，同时保留其中的词法退出，避免把含 handler break 的循环错误当作永不退出而漏查后继请求。

这没有解除未知高阶目标、复杂 match／handler 控制关联、循环数据状态不变量、捕获 owner 交付及资源清理的剩余限制。新增拒绝例保留真正重复的 continue、同一 break 路径内两次消费，以及 handler break 之后的重复消费；运行时 predicate 的失败仍由运行时验证报告。

### 请求次数分析按模式探测顺序传播

`effect_usage/control/matching.rs` 将模式探测分成匹配成功、失败与词法控制退出；match 候选按顺序接收此前失败路径的请求计数，let-else 只把失败路径送入 else。产品模式逐字段组合，Or 模式逐候选组合，Then 保留中间表达式求值；只有不含 Guard／Then 的模式才能使用整个模式的纯语法判定，避免后续字段不匹配抹掉前面已经执行的 guard。未匹配路径中止，不进入正常后继。计算行映射中的 match 主体和 guard 仍使用 caller 行，选中的结果按槽位映射。

guard 的布尔事实仅用于其正常完成路径；分析先保存求值期间的请求和控制退出，再识别 block／call preparation 尾部的常量布尔结果。不以尾部常量跳过前置副作用。新增正例覆盖提前返回、确定不可达候选、let-else 与带副作用的常量 guard；拒绝例覆盖失败 guard 留下的消费。产品字段测试从合法源程序实例化 IIR，再将 guard 放入首字段，分别验证后续字段成功／失败时的重复请求：静态检查均拒绝，原始参考执行均报告 EffectValueConsumed。

### Handler 候选与部分转发的请求上界

普通 handler 和 direct passing provider 的分支组现在复用有序模式探测：分别保留候选成功、失败和控制退出，只有失败路径继续到下一候选。确定匹配的分支终止后续探测；失败 guard 的已发生请求保留。fallback 只叠加到全部候选失败的路径，不再与已经成功的分支消费相加。请求实参在函数摘要中仍视为未知，不凭某个调用点的实参缩小所有请求的上界。

### Direct passing 安装阶段的控制退出

全 direct passing 的安装组现在先按源顺序分析 provider，再分析可达的主体。provider 的 return、带词法目标的 break／continue 和中止保留到外围控制结构；确定退出后不再分析后续 provider 或主体。resume 在当前 provider 边界转换为供值完成，不会跳过主体。主体中安装槽位的请求上界单独检查，随后只将外层行计数与供值过程顺序组合；退出之前已发生的消费始终保留。

新增源程序验证提前 return 跳过重复请求主体、跳过后续 provider、带消费的 provider return、provider break 后的循环后继，以及 resume 后继续消费的拒绝。退出前两次消费和 break 后再消费仍拒绝。混合普通 handler 的安装组继续使用保守分析；这不是完整 handler 非局部退出分析或资源清理实现。

### 混合 handler 组的安装前缀

### 元组解构的函数别名

别名索引现在保存借用初始化表达式和有序投影路径，路径区分元组位置与名义／匿名记录字段。无 guard、无 else 且仅含 Tuple／Wild／简单 Binding 的 let-pattern 可以产生唯一别名定义；其他模式保持暴露／未知处理。普通 Let 与模式绑定共用重复定义检查，因此之前的同号 LocalId 重绑定拒绝仍成立。路径解析复用实例索引、条件构造和 block 处理，不重新执行初始化表达式。

### 结构体解构与 guard 中的可调用绑定

结构化别名准备扩展到名义记录模式和 Guard 包装，并允许 let-pattern 的 guard／else。只提取成功匹配时绑定对应的结构投影；guard 实际执行、失败后的 else 和控制退出仍由模式控制分析负责。Then、Remap 等未建立结构对应关系的模式仍保守排除。guard 中赋值、取址和重复定义继续通过整个实例的失效收集排除旧目标。

新增源程序覆盖 `{call:f}` 结构体解构、元组嵌套记录、guard 两种结果、失败后 return，以及 guard 中调用新绑定函数、guard 中改写函数变量。guard 成功后再调用导致重复消费时拒绝；guard 只调用一次随后失败退出的合法路径通过。未弱化失败 guard 的请求累计或同号 LocalId 重绑定规则。

### 转换模式的独立绑定来源

结构化别名准备现在为每个绑定保存自己的来源表达式与投影路径。Pattern::Then 的 first 沿用输入来源，next 从中间 value 重新开始；不得将转换后的函数绑定解释为原输入。Literal／Unit 本身不产生绑定，可与结构路径组合。中间表达式的执行仍由模式控制分析负责，索引只借用表达式，不重复执行、不绕过前段失败或 guard。

源程序测试覆盖原输入和转换结果具有不同请求次数、分别调用前后绑定、转换表达式引用先前绑定、转换为元组后解构、转换过程先消费、前段确定失败后跳过转换，以及取址／重复调用的拒绝。部分转换模式按现有覆盖性检查补充 diverging else，未放宽该规则。Remap／Or 等多来源模式仍保守处理。

### Or／Remap 的多来源可调用绑定

结构化别名索引允许同一个 let-pattern 的绑定拥有多个候选来源，调用与后缀投影取候选摘要的上界；不同定义节点复用身份仍视为重绑定失效。Or 收集各候选来源，Remap 按解释器的同时读取语义从内部结果快照建立目标映射，不把连续映射误当作串行赋值。无法在内部结果中找到源绑定时整体退回保守处理。

Remap 保留来源绑定依赖，失效信息传播到统一目标：guard 中对分支临时绑定的赋值／取址，不能在映射后恢复成已知的旧函数。内部来源也保留供 guard 中的调用查询。映射复制、候选合并及失效传播均计入预算；候选成功条件的相关性目前仍取保守上界。

新增源程序回归覆盖不同元组位置的同名 Or 绑定、两种分支结果、不同调用摘要的合流、失败 guard 消费、取址、合流后赋值，以及右分支 guard 先改写局部绑定再 Remap 的拒绝。原同号 LocalId 重绑定和规模回归继续通过。

按 docs/functions/parameter-elaboration.md 的已确认规则，普通 runtime implicit 参数可通过 `.name = expr` 显式供应。签名保留 HIR 的 implicit 标记；调用路由将其登记为命名入口并跳过位置分配，展开实参的形状提示也跳过该位置。泛型转发、前序 implicit 输入参与 optional 默认、变参并用、inherent／trait 方法使用同一供应路径。省略输入明确报告自动供应协议尚未实现，不在作用域中猜选同类型值；comptime／quote 等组合仍未接通。

### post do 的调用路由与闭包边界

修复旧 lowering 将 `f(args) do ...` 错当成调用 `f(args)` 返回值的问题。HIR 新增 Arg::PostLambda 并提供 S-expression Display，保持 trailing 输入身份到签名路由阶段。存在唯一 lambda 标记时优先选择该位置，否则选择最后锚定参数；位置实参分配预留目标，拒绝无目标、标记歧义和重复供应。展开实参的上下文推断与准备阶段保留此标记，目标位置不占用 packet 的位置槽。

普通 lambda 标记参数现在接受函数／显式闭包输入；post do 的显式 lambda 使用普通闭包检查，块／表达式正文进入新的闭包作用域，延后执行。覆盖标记位于前部、默认参数、泛型、间接调用、inherent／trait 方法和展开实参；捕获的 owned 值可交付给 implicit 输入并恰好析构一次。返回作用域用例在闭包 return 后继续计算外围结果，未调用正文的用例检查无正文事件。`_0`／`_1` tactic lambda、quote 接入和完整参数协议元数据仍未实现，不把本次工作称为 lambda 参数全部完成。

### Tactic lambda 的目标参数与词法边界

`_0`、`_1` 等现在作为完整标识符 token 进入 HIR 的 TacticParameter，而不是拆成 underscore 和数字。lambda 标记的实参经路由建立 TacticArgument 边界；普通函数值和显式 lambda 仍走常规接入。出现当前边界的自由占位符时，依据完整目标／部分可调用上下文构造全部参数，不按最大下标猜 arity。缺少目标参数表、越界下标、未标记入口以及显式 lambda 中的自由占位符均拒绝。

标记实参的试探复用现有推断事务，失败恢复局部状态；嵌套标记输入与显式 lambda 保存并替换占位符帧。帧限定正文源码范围，定义侧默认表达式不能偷用调用侧参数。上下文构造器（例如 `.some(_0)`）可在回调结果类型下检查，但必须实际引用当前帧参数才接受这种解释，不能把仅有内层占位符的普通调用包成外层闭包。post-do 正文保留独立 HIR 节点，在标记位置使用完整目标签名形成闭包。

占位符最终引用普通 NIR LocalId，值读取、赋值、取址、捕获与仿射交付共用已有实现。用例检查重复下标不重复外部计算、二元签名只用 `_0` 仍保留两个参数、后续参数帮助泛型推断、展开实参、上下文 variant、nested 边界、捕获、写回和单次 Drop；重复消费 owned 参数被资源检查拒绝。新增三个 HIR 节点均有 S-expression Display，并纳入完整表达式结构测试。

### Explicit sysroot compilation and package-scoped CLI entries

`--sysroot PATH` now loads `builtin/lib.fl` and `std/lib.fl`, plus any present `meta`, `build`, `attrs`, and `verification` package directories, for HIR/NIR compilation. Source resolution reuses the package-set pipeline: builtin.prelude is an ordinary default glob; std.prelude requires explicit import. AST output remains a single-source parse. Standalone semantic identities are local to the compilation; build tools retain the explicit package-input API for stable identities.

CLI invocation, reference execution (including cleanup-checked execution), instantiation, and resource analysis select entries only from primary semantic package 0. Library APIs preserve unscoped selection and provide explicit `_in_package` variants. Protocol names remain explicit, uniquely resolved driver configuration across the supplied package set. Output paths cannot alias any loaded source, including dependency source hardlinks.

Validation in `/home/fin/luna`: `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test frontend_cli --test packages --test modules --test instantiation` exited 0: 83 CLI, 14 package, 43 module, 18 instantiation tests (158 total). Output: `/tmp/luna-sysroot-integration.log`. Tests cover same-name dependency entries, missing primary entries, prelude precedence, explicit std imports, malformed/missing dependency source, and source preservation on failure.

This does not certify the shipped library: roots and core traits now pass AST parsing, but the whole builtin HIR probe still fails at iterator.fl's legacy `type Item` declaration. Option/Result, operator and iterator APIs require further migration. Explicit package inputs now delimit recursive discovery: other supplied directory packages and single-file inputs are excluded from the current package scan. A nested lib.fl without a corresponding package input remains ordinary module source.


Package-boundary regression checks: `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test packages --test modules --test frontend_cli` in `/home/fin/luna` exited 0 (16 package, 43 module, 84 CLI tests; 143 total), log `/tmp/luna-package-boundaries.log`. Coverage includes nested sysroot execution, unique provider declaration identity, denial of filesystem access without a dependency edge, ordinary nested lib.fl without an explicit package input, and single-file dependencies alongside local modules.


Trait Type defaults now support `.Rhs: Type = Self`, named override and definition-scoped substitution across trait use sites. The actual shipped primitives+ops module pair passes NIR compilation and explicit-method reference execution. Source declaration identities now use resolver definition IDs, sharing the correct namespace with type parameters instead of dense HIR owner numbers. Expanded regression evidence: 1,847 tests passed via the Cargo wrapper (command and counts in implementation-plan.md, `/tmp/luna-trait-default-identities.log`). Other nominal/function optional clauses, operator language-item dispatch and the rest of shipped library migration remain separate work.


Struct/enum Type defaults now use the shared declaration/default routing implementation with traits. See `development/examples/type-defaults.fl` for same-type defaults, named heterogeneous overrides and defaulted enum payloads; `python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/type-defaults.fl --interpret run` prints `(bool true)`. The expanded 1,854-test regression passes (`/tmp/luna-nominal-default-regression.log`). Function optional clauses and non-Type inputs remain separate work.


Typealias Type defaults are now connected through resolver, HIR and elaboration. Defaulted struct/enum/alias applications also preserve computed Type inputs as once-evaluated bindings in source order, allowing later defaults to reuse them. The executable type-defaults example includes a defaulted alias; default/order, cross-package and opaque-head checks pass. Evidence and precise suite counts are recorded in implementation-plan.md.


Function Type defaults now compose with direct calls, function-value contexts and methods; the type-defaults example includes `keep` with a bool default and a named char override. Across six affected suites, 1,799 tests have passing evidence (see implementation-plan.md for the diagnostic-only rerun). Computed defaults depending on active call inference now wait for their inputs and constrain the candidate after invocation; this also covers chained defaults, methods and contextual function values. The final six-suite regression passes 1,801 tests, and the example executes to `(bool true)` (see implementation-plan.md). Arbitrary computation on still-symbolic caller binders remains open. Non-Type optional clauses and normal-form-head defaults remain open.

Normal-form heads now support defaults in all-Type clause telescopes, preserving opaque head identity and complete input vectors. `development/examples/normal-form-defaults.fl --invoke-comptime Defaulted` demonstrates once-evaluated preceding inputs shared with a default. Named overrides keep source order and skip the overridden computation. ### Driver-bound automatic Splice

The frontend can insert ordinary runtime Splice calls for module-constant
references and comptime invocation results. Supply a trusted, package-qualified trait identity through
`elaboration::program::Protocols { splice: Some(declaration) }` to
`frontend::compile_in_package_with_protocols`, `packages::compile_with_protocols`,
or `elaboration::program::elaborate_packages_with_protocols`. The protocol's
surface is validated against the current elaborated trait declarations; its
source name does not designate it. A declaration ID belongs to the corresponding
resolved package revision and must not be guessed or reused after resolution
changes.

Type observation, required comptime computation and staged arguments keep their
existing paths. Runtime constant uses select an implementation and enter the
same call preparation, staged-input freezing and concrete-instance machinery as
explicit `Type.as(Splice).splice(value)`. The target may differ from the source.
Program checks and constructor calls in the conversion remain runtime behavior.
Anonymous structural record constants also work with an explicit implementation.

The CLI resolves an explicit `--splice-protocol Splice` selection after HIR
construction, in the same compilation. Use `package::Trait` to select from one
source package (the standalone input package is named `input`). Unqualified
ambiguous names are rejected, as are malformed protocol signatures even when no
conversion is used. Merely declaring a trait called Splice does not bind it.
`packages::compile_with_splice` supplies the same source selection to build tools;
the identity-based APIs remain available. A selector conflicting with an explicit
identity is an error.

```sh
python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/automatic-splice.fl --interpret run --splice-protocol Splice
```

This prints `(tuple (tuple (bool true) (bool false)) (tuple (bool false) (bool true)))`.
`development/examples/explicit-splice.fl` demonstrates explicit conversion without
a driver binding. Aggregate automatic derivation and the remaining staged-value use forms remain open.


`development/examples/splice-comptime-calls.fl` exercises direct and generic
comptime producers plus a producer depending on an enclosing staged input. Run
with `--interpret run --splice-protocol Splice`. Producer calls are completed at
comptime; the conversion instances and their constructors execute at runtime.
Method/default/spread/property-collection entrypoints preserve the same boundary.
Runtime arguments cannot be read by these producers. Resource-checked execution
also retains cleanup of runtime values constructed by Splice.

`development/examples/splice-higher-order.fl` extends this to immediately invoked
comptime function/closure results, including a staged outer input and a block tail
used as a callee. Run with `--interpret run --splice-protocol Splice`. Intermediate
comptime callables stay inside the comptime invocation; only its final value is
converted. This does not authorize callable values to escape into runtime or make
runtime callback arguments comptime. Function result arrows associate to the
right, so `fn() -> fn() -> bool` retains both callable layers.

### Semantic comptime query cache foundation

`comptime_executor` now provides a bounded cache for already-authorized pure
queries. It calls a driver-supplied comptime key protocol, compares candidates
using semantic Eq after Hash filtering, and invalidates entries on definition,
protocol-world or target revision changes. Query identity includes package,
declaration and operation; ordered input hashes do not stand in for equality.
Key-protocol failure, evaluation failure, budget exhaustion and capacity failure
publish no entry. Eq/Hash uses an uncached invocation path while a key is forming.

This is not automatically installed in elaboration or IIR instance formation.
The driver must supply completed immutable values, select and validate the source
Eq/Hash implementations, establish the query's pure promise, and ensure that its
computation respects the supplied input equivalence. The source integration test
uses real comptime trait methods on a nominal record and checks a runtime-phase
Hash rejection. Arbitrary nominal values are still not admitted as structural
instance keys; nominal Splice input freezing remains outstanding.

`luna::protocols::select_comptime_key` now selects Eq/Hash by trusted language-item
identity using the existing implementation world. It checks the comptime signature,
proves type requirements, and preserves generic/default-body arguments, both
interface and body program contracts, capability obligations and the complete
scoped selection evidence. Runtime-only methods and abstract assumptions cannot
supply executable key operations. Hash result support currently covers primitive
integer types; general associated result protocols are not implemented.

The cache integration test now obtains its concrete methods through this selector.
Selection alone does not authorize invocation. `luna::comptime_keys::Protocol`
now prepares both selected methods in a private dispatch package, establishes
their type capabilities and executes them through the interpreter's ordinary
function-instance path. Generic and default methods keep their type arguments;
program checks run on each uncached invocation. The adapter accounts for input
copying and execution, rejects reference/callable data, and hashes the complete
integer result rather than requiring it to fit a host u64. This hash is only a
bucket digest; source Eq still determines a cache hit.

Resource authorization, query/equality compatibility and automatic production
cache installation remain caller responsibilities. Validate selection and cache delivery
with `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test execution comptime_key_selection`
and `python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test execution pure_query_cache`.


The adapter and direct host type-instance path have targeted execution tests:
`comptime_key_adapter` covers generic trait dispatch, default methods, signed and
arbitrary-precision hash results, failed program checks, budget exhaustion, wrong
input types, callable rejection and cache recovery. `instantiated_host_invocation`
checks retained type requirements, program checks and recovery after failed calls.


`Protocol::admit` now constructs a private immutable `Snapshot` after checking
its exact type, nominal arguments and formation requirements. The representation
supports immutable scalar/aggregate/nominal data, including enum tags and payloads;
storage, pointers and callable captures are rejected instead of copied as handles.
Phantom nominal constraints and nested Type values are checked too. Normal-form
heads retain their identity; only their declared input contracts are checked.
Computation/effect type values now validate each operation against retained source
declaration metadata, including complete type arguments, type requirements and
capabilities. This validates a Type value without executing an operation or
installing its handler. Reference execution from IIR does not retain this source
metadata and cannot use it to admit additional effect type values.

Snapshots expose only shared read access and retain their prepared protocol-world
identity. A fresh protocol rejects snapshots from an earlier preparation, even if
its source names agree. This identity check is provenance validation, never source
value equality. `KeyProtocol<Snapshot>` still delegates comparison to source Eq.
The collision integration test now caches these typed snapshots. No structural
nominal term has been added to IIR instance keys, and snapshot construction alone
does not authorize resource duplication or cross-stage delivery.


Effect-type Eq now also has replayable PTC refutations for nonempty prefixes
versus ordinary constructors, incompatible result types, and proven occurrence
multiplicity differences. Unknown label relationships contribute possible matches;
they never prove absence. Prefix-count arguments require both result tails to be
known ordinary constructors, so an unresolved result that may itself carry more
effects cannot produce a false inequality. Independent labels still commute and
same-label occurrences are retained. A source Eq/Hash snapshot cache test covers
commuting rows, distinct operations, repeated layers and an empty row.


Effect-row proofs now flatten explicit nested prefixes and result aliases known
in the current Boolean branch. For example, `T == #read U` and `U == bool` let
`#write T` meet `#[read, write] bool`; the distinct labels may commute, while
repeated occurrences are retained. Empty raw wrappers have the same meaning as
their result. Unresolved/cyclic aliases remain pending, and normal-form bodies are
never evaluated by this view. The same view feeds equality and refutation rules.

`development/examples/effect-result-aliases.fl` demonstrates a generic caller
discharging that contract. Run
`python3 -B development/cargo.py run -p luna -- development/examples/effect-result-aliases.fl --interpret entry`
to obtain `(bool true)` without installing or executing any effect operation.


`luna::invocation::MemoizedInvocation` is now an optional reusable call entry for
one ordinary pure comptime function with concrete generic arguments. Ordinary
comptime Type parameters bind later parameter and result types in source order. It owns its compilation/dispatch snapshot and
prepares an Eq/Hash protocol per argument slot. Calls take fully evaluated inputs;
default evaluation and resource authorization remain outside the cache.

Source Eq/Hash is mandatory, followed by exact immutable representation comparison
as an additional query dependency check. This deliberately avoids reusing a
function that observes a field ignored by user Eq. It does not redefine source
value equality. Generic instances, argument order and compilation worlds stay
separate. Valid immutable results are published only after execution and formation
checks. Unsupported result representations return uncached; genuine contract or
execution failures remain failures. At capacity (including zero capacity), misses
execute without growing the cache and existing entries can still hit.

This entry does not yet replace arbitrary elaboration/invocation queries.
Value-index dependencies and arbitrary higher-order staged dispatch remain
incomplete. Direct call chains can now specialize from ordinary Type inputs.
Ordinary Type-input-dependent equality contracts bind and check
in the optional memoized entry, including the `T: kind` domain refinement below. The strict `Cache::query_pure` API retains
its capacity-error contract; `query_pure_admitted` provides the optional-publication
behavior used by the invocation entry.


Dependent memoized calls retain a bounded registry of concrete input/result
bindings, each with its own source Eq/Hash protocol instances. The result capacity
is shared across bindings. Additional bindings execute transiently when the
registry is full; invalid inputs do not publish results or install a new binding.
Dumps include each retained binding and its protocol slots. Tests cover bool/u8
rebinding, multiple Type parameters with interleaved values, capacities 0/1/8,
wrong kinds, out-of-range values, missing protocols and recovery of earlier hits.

`python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test execution memoized_invocation`
(6 passed; `/tmp/luna-dependent-memo-tests.log`).


### Type domains justified by signature contracts

`comptime fn keep(comptime kind: Type, comptime T: kind, value: T) -> T`
now accepts `where requires kind == Type`. Signature preparation uses available
type binders and positive equality conjuncts, including symmetric/transitive
equalities, to establish the Type domain. It retains the declared requirement;
negation, disjunction and program-state predicates do not supply that evidence.

The comptime interpreter checks closed function requirements at formation.
Requirements that still depend on ordinary Type inputs wait until invocation,
then bind those inputs and check before entering the body. A rejected call does
not poison a retained function instance. This does not implement arbitrary
value-index substitution or input-dependent trait dispatch.

### Dependent type contracts in memoized invocation

The optional memoized entry admits each requirement in the function telescope
after clause-parameter substitution. Closed requirements are checked at preparation;
requirements with ordinary Type inputs are retained and rebound on each call,
before protocol preparation or cache lookup. Missing bindings, failed proofs and
exhausted budgets publish no result. This also preserves contract checks on cache
hits. The S-expression dump includes retained requirements. Nontrivial proofs
share the invocation budget through the metered solver entry. PTC reports
consumed work; world-dependent trait decisions still reserve their partitioned
allowances. Syntactically established truths bypass proof search. Program/resource contracts still belong to interpreter execution.

Tests cover a two-level Type-domain contract, disjunctive equality contracts,
rejection before missing-protocol diagnostics, recovery after failed calls and
budget exhaustion, and preservation of existing hits. This does not complete
ordinary-input-dependent trait dispatch or replace all compiler query entrypoints.

`python3 -B development/cargo.py test -p luna --test execution memoized_invocation`
passed 7 tests, exit 0 (`/tmp/luna-memo-contracts.log`).


### Trait receivers bound by ordinary Type inputs

Method selection now substitutes interface/implementation arguments in the caller's
ordinary input scope. Receiver comparison removes the method's own telescope
frame before comparing or constructing an address. This fixes `value.as(Inspect)
.inspect()` when `value: T` and `T` is an ordinary comptime Type input with an
explicit `T :- Inspect` requirement. The runtime staged-call path is covered.

On a memoized miss, Type inputs are bound with the existing IIR staging pass in
a private package snapshot. The resulting private entry has concrete requirements,
receiver types and body types, so dispatch preparation can select the actual
implementation/default. Original declarations and cache keys remain unchanged.
Hits reuse validated results; full/disabled caches still specialize and execute.
Staging work is charged and dispatch reserves a bounded solver allowance.

0/1/8, reject a type without the required trait, and recover the old hit afterward.
This initially implemented direct trait dispatch at the bound entry. The staged
comptime graph entry described below extends it to nested direct calls and
recursive instances; automatic integration into all compiler query paths remains
unimplemented.

### Shared work budgets for retained type contracts

`Context::prove_metered` updates a mutable Budget on successful proofs,
countermodels, malformed inputs and exhaustion. The existing `prove` entry
delegates to it while preserving its value-taking API. World predicate checks
now offer a metered entry that shares one allowance between direct PTC search
and world-dependent fallback. Proposition input traversal and final PTC search
consume measured work; individual trait decisions conservatively reserve their
disjoint allowances. Existing evidence remains verifiable in the same world.

Memoized contract checking now deducts this reported consumption instead of
always reserving the entire configured limit. A nontrivial Bool/u8 disequality
contract completes with a 150000-step invocation budget, leaves room for dispatch
and execution, then hits the cache. Dispatch preparation itself still reserves
its allowance: its internal traversal counter does not yet cover all nested
selection/index work, so returning that counter as total consumption would be
incorrect. Arbitrary higher-order staged dispatch remains unfinished.

### Staged comptime instance graphs for memoized calls

Memoized calls needing ordinary Type staging now reuse full IIR materialization,
rather than collecting only dispatch tables. A bounded scan follows direct
function calls (including from a zero-input root) to decide whether staging is
needed. The private bound entry is materialized with its transitive functions,
trait implementations and nominal layouts. Existing instance identities and
visited sets handle repeated and recursive calls; no second specialization
algorithm or global mutable dispatch table is introduced.

`Interpreter::from_iir_for_comptime` validates the retained graph and applies
comptime phase authorization at every invocation. Runtime roots and runtime
callees remain rejected. Graph invocations use their specialized definitions
for phase and contract checks, without reapplying a staged instance key as
clause arguments. Results are admitted against the same owned source package
because IIR intentionally does not retain all source formation metadata. Both
execution and result-admission work are charged before cache publication.

Tests cover nested Type forwarding, finite same-instance recursion, two Type
instances of a shared helper, clause-generic helpers, zero-input wrappers,
nominal results, cache reuse, and phase rejection at roots and nested calls.
Arbitrary higher-order dynamic staging and automatic compiler-wide cache use
remain incomplete; materialization still uses a conservative work reservation.

### Staged invocation contract and preparation failures

Regression coverage now exercises program preconditions, postconditions and
entry snapshots through the memoized IIR path. Repeated failing calls publish
no result; a subsequent valid call succeeds and can hit. A saved parameter value
still agrees with `value'old` after the live parameter is mutated. The negative
postcondition test first compiles a valid function, then corrupts its checked
producer, independently testing the interpreter's contract enforcement without
weakening the frontend's static proof requirement.

`from_iir_metered` and `from_iir_for_comptime_metered` return graph-validation
consumption through a mutable Budget even on failure. Existing value-taking
constructors delegate to them. Memoized invocation now charges this failed
preparation work, instead of losing it when no VM is constructed. Successful
construction hands the remaining allowance to the VM; execution accounting
continues from that remainder. Invalid graphs, tiny budgets and subsequent
valid preparation are tested.

constraint. Concrete input views remain justified by the caller's equality
evidence, and trait truth stays local to that implementation world. Method
selection and retained declaration contracts are unchanged.

does not treat a Bool value as the Bool type and rejects unresolved trait bounds.
This classification is intentionally local to method routing: globally changing
Type-input expression classification lost the parameter provenance needed by
memory-summary forwarding. The existing expression representation is preserved.

### Open comptime function values defer input-dependent dispatch

Dispatch-only expression traversal no longer enters an ordinary-Type function
body solely because its value is retained. Direct calls and explicit execution
roots still demand bodies; strict IIR materialization still requires completed
instances. Both plain function values and generic instances can be stored
without attempting trait selection on an unbound ordinary input.

At generic comptime function formation, capabilities depending on those inputs
wait until invocation binds the telescope. Invocation rebinds and checks these
deferred obligations before the body runs, including repeated calls to an
already-created closure. Closed capabilities retain their existing executable
or assumed dispatch checks; they are not replaced by new solver requests.
The deferred check lives outside the recursive invocation frame to preserve
the interpreter's stack budget.

Source regressions cover retained plain/generic open functions and rejection
of a call without the required trait. An interpreter regression isolates
capability metadata from duplicate source predicates, verifies the solver sees
the concrete input type, and rejects two consecutive invocations.

### Immediately invoked local function values enter staged specialization

Before collecting executable dependencies, materialization recognizes a block
whose final statement binds a function declaration or generic instance and
whose result immediately calls that binding. It moves the function expression
to the callee position, retaining earlier statements and the original argument
expressions. Function formation still precedes arguments. The existing direct
call staging path then binds Type inputs and checks the selected definition's
contracts, for both runtime and comptime functions.

This transformation requires a matching callable type and a staged input. It
does not apply if an argument reads or assigns the eliminated binding, or
contains a closure that could capture it. Non-adjacent bindings, escaping
callables and dynamically selected targets still need broader higher-order
specialization; this is not a general callable inliner.

### Conditional selection of staged callable targets

Materialization can distribute a staged call over an `if` selecting two known
function targets. Each target receives a concrete specialized call; the
condition remains outside those calls, so runtime selects its target before
evaluating arguments and executes arguments only in the selected arm. Adjacent
local binding elimination also recognizes such conditional values. Declaration
targets, generic instances and static trait methods share this path.

This initially required completed `TypeValue` expressions for all non-runtime
inputs; the data-input extension below also admits completed immutable values.
It still requires no default-argument preparation bindings and branches containing only
a known target (possibly wrapped in an empty block). It deliberately does not
duplicate computed staged producers or move arguments across effectful branch
scopes. Nested selection is handled by the follow-up below; general computed
callable transport remains unfinished. Traversal and type copying consume the
materialization budget.

The source regression runs runtime and comptime entries, both condition values,
generic and trait alternatives, condition/argument writes that detect ordering
or repeated evaluation, and failure/recovery after a small budget. A target
whose Type requirement contradicts the supplied type remains rejected.

tuple bindings initialized from a comptime input or another such alias. Their

missing local bindings. Runtime inputs are not assigned this provenance.

When binding completed inputs, IIR staging recovers those aliases and tuple
elements through a budgeted dependency fixed point. It evaluates no initializer
and skips nested call/closure environments. Existing write/address-escape
analysis applies to both original inputs and derived locals before substitution;
a mutated or escaped local cannot silently reuse its initial constant. Ordinary
runtime uses and original let/pattern statements remain in the function body.
This does not yet cover arbitrary computed initializers, effectful patterns or
derived bindings inside separate closure/default environments.

### Forwarding total Boolean derivations of comptime inputs

The frontend and staged-input recovery share a bounded dependency classifier
for total Boolean/structural initializers: `not`, Boolean `and`/`or`, conditional
selection, tuples, completed data and anonymous-record projections. An immutable
binding is stage-derived only when it depends on at least one known comptime
binding and every local dependency is available at that stage. The collector
substitutes completed inputs and uses the existing non-invoking fold path to
recover the derived value, retaining normal let statements in the residual body.

This path does not execute user functions, dereference pointers, perform writes,
or speculatively evaluate checked arithmetic. Unsupported subtrees are pruned
from classification; mixed runtime dependencies and invalidated sources do not
become constants. Field folding retains label/index/type checks and lives in a
separate non-inlined helper to avoid enlarging every recursive Boolean fold's
stack frame.

### Forwarding IEEE floating-point comparison results

Same-precision f32/f64 comparisons now participate in the stage-derived Boolean
fragment. Static folding uses partial comparison, matching the interpreter:
NaNs are unordered, both signed zeros compare equal, and infinities and subnormals
retain their numeric ordering. In particular, `<=`/`>=` require a present ordering;
negating the opposite strict comparison would incorrectly accept NaN.
Mixed precision and runtime-only dependencies remain rejected. This path neither
adds floating-point identities to PTC nor invokes user comparison protocols.

The source regression previously failed with `MissingBinding`
(`/tmp/luna-float-forward-baseline.log`). It now exercises all six relations for
both precisions through runtime and comptime entry points. Staging tests use an
independent rank table for pairwise quiet/signaling NaNs, signed zeros, subnormals
and infinities, including exhausted budgets and recovery.

### Forwarding composed BitVec locals

Derived staged locals now include BitVec `not`, eager `and`/`or`, equality,
concatenation and statically bounded slices. Classification checks operand and
result widths, checked concatenation width addition, and slice bounds before
admitting an initializer. Folding reuses the budgeted BitVec kernel and validates
the resulting constant. Bitwise operations evaluate both operands; an all-zero
or all-one left operand cannot hide an unavailable right operand.

Bit folding has its own small dispatch path, so deeply nested operations reach
the existing semantic depth limit rather than exhausting the host stack. Tests
cover 0/1/33/129-bit compositions, high/low concatenation order, padding, empty
out-of-range slices, malformed domains, budget failure/recovery, unavailable
operands and 160-level nesting. Runtime-only origins remain rejected. Representation
conversions are covered below; dynamic slice producers and location writes are
not admitted by this derived-local classifier.

The derived-local classifier and static folder now support `TakeBits` and
`BitConvert` for the existing unrestricted scalar domains. Signed integers and
IEEE floats retain their exact bits; signed/float reconstruction requires exact
width. Unsigned integers and BitVec results may zero-extend, never narrow.
Boolean, character and other validity-sensitive representations are not admitted.
Budget accounting includes conversion and output copying, and the separate
folding path preserves depth-limit errors for nested representation operations.

Source tests round-trip signed/unsigned integers through 128 bits and both
floating-point negative zeros before forwarding the resulting local. Unit tests
check quiet/signaling NaN payloads, zero-width unsigned reconstruction, widening

representation as the interpreter. Negation flips only the sign bit, retaining
NaN payloads and signed zero. Both binary operands must complete; multiplying by
zero does not bypass an unavailable operand. Checked integer arithmetic remains
outside the total initializer classifier.

Source tests cover runtime/comptime entry paths in both precisions, ordinary

### Closed local inputs in ordinary function instances

Total immutable local initializers no longer require a dependency on an erased
comptime formal to participate in staged forwarding. The frontend records their
availability, and ordinary function materialization resolves closed locals before
specializing calls. This follows the comptime chapter's rule for known inputs
without runtime obligations. It fixes `let flag = true; keep(flag)` when `keep`
requires a comptime input, including tuple destructuring and owned closure captures.
Previously the source regression failed with `MissingBinding`
(`/tmp/luna-closed-locals-baseline.log`).

Only the existing total structural fragment is admitted: runtime function calls
do not become comptime merely because they return constants. Original runtime
statements remain, and writes/address escape still invalidate substitution.
The new test verifies a surrounding runtime write, runtime-producer rejection
and the specific invalidated-input diagnostic.

### Closed locals in independent closure frames

Closure bodies now collect their own closed local producers before staged-call
substitution. The closure-local collection starts with no enclosing values, so a
captured runtime input cannot become an assumed invocation constant. Its write
and address-escape set is combined with existing substitution invalidations;
parameter/capture masks remain in force. Nested closures repeat this process in
their own frames, and shared bodies are detached before mutation.

### Contract-proved type views for default stability

Default stability analysis now uses a private expression copy whose annotations
can be viewed through proved type equalities. This lets `options: T` under
`T == Options` support the same scalar-record field reads/destructuring as a
concrete Options input. The original source annotations and invocation frames
remain unchanged. PTC supplies type equality only; structural default analysis
still decides the admitted program operations, without admitting arbitrary calls
or owned cleanup. Opaque normal-form heads retain the existing view rules.

`Context::structural_view_metered` reports traversal work and reserved proof
allowances on success and failure. Default analysis charges this work, expression
copying and cached type-view copying against its existing budget. Views are cached
only within the current default analysis/context.

Local Boolean matches now participate in total staged derivation when unguarded
arms cover both Boolean values. Supported patterns are Boolean literals, wildcard, binding wrappers, ordered
alternatives and binding remaps; executable pattern views and other match domains
remain outside this folding path. Arm bindings are removed
from external dependencies. Guarded arms do not contribute to the coverage proof.

only after its pattern matches and evaluates only the chosen body. Each attempt
has a fresh binding map. The source regression previously failed with MissingBinding
(`/tmp/luna-bool-match-baseline.log`). Direct tests cover guard fallthrough without

chain that reads a name introduced only by the same remap. Unsupported executable
patterns still do not count as unconditional coverage.

### Negated Boolean patterns through lowering and elaboration

AST lowering now preserves `not pattern` as HIR `PatternKind::Not`, with a nested
S-expression Display representation. Boolean elaboration checks the inner pattern
in an isolated binding scope and computes the complement of pure Boolean literal,
wildcard, binding, remapping and alternative patterns. It emits existing literal,
wildcard or empty-alternative patterns, so runtime interpretation, coverage and
staged local forwarding agree without adding a separate execution convention.
Inner bindings do not escape negation. Type evidence such as `T == bool` can expose
the Boolean domain without rewriting the source type head.

The new source regression initially failed at elaboration after HIR preservation
(`/tmp/luna-negated-pattern-baseline.log`). It now covers single/double negation,
alternatives with remapped bindings, both Boolean inputs, runtime and staged
execution, empty complements, non-exhaustiveness, generic type evidence and
rejection of leaked bindings. The static complement operation does not approximate executable guards or views.
Executable candidates use the ordered matching path described below. The scalar
extension below also admits integer, character, floating-point and BitVec domains;
resource-bearing negation remains unsupported; scalar structural aggregates are
covered by the extension below.

### Executable Boolean candidates under negation

When a Boolean candidate contains guards or other executable matching operations,
elaboration now captures the observed Boolean in a fresh internal binding and
uses an ordinary nested match to invert only the final success result. Candidate
bindings remain scoped to the nested match. Guard side effects, source-order
alternatives, control exits and runtime verification failures follow the existing
matching machinery. Static Boolean complements retain their simpler literal or
wildcard representation. Executable negation does not claim unconditional
coverage or eligibility for pure staged-local forwarding.

Regression coverage verifies zero guard calls after an inner literal mismatch,
one call after success, double negation without duplicated effects, candidate
bindings inside guards, restoration of shadowed outer names, ordered effects in
alternatives, return propagation and ProgramContractRejected propagation. Counter
helpers use an immutable snapshot and a checked assumes before machine arithmetic;
pointer reads themselves are not admitted as assumes predicates by the current
verification implementation.

remaining regions after each arm and credits only regions whose selected result
is true. Complementing requires exact pattern evidence: an unsupported guard,
call, body or match source returns no evidence rather than turning a partial
positive approximation into an unsound complement. Work and recursive depth stay
bounded; no program predicate is sent to PTC.

This admits exhaustive pairs such as `not (3..7)` with `3..7`, integer alternatives
with their negation, and Unicode character ranges with their negation. Guard calls
that cannot be analyzed remain conservative, including calls nested in an or
alternative. Interval pattern remaps now resolve sources simultaneously and remove
obsolete source bindings, matching runtime remapping semantics.

### Ordered alternatives in scalar and bit coverage

Fixed two false exhaustiveness proofs. Interval analysis previously unioned every
or alternative's bindings before an outer guard, even though runtime matching
commits to the first successful alternative. A preceding computed pattern could
bind zero, fail the outer nonzero guard, and incorrectly let coverage use a later
subject binding. Bit coverage similarly unioned different projection bindings
before a following `and ... is ...` test, crediting values that the first selected
projection could not match. Both source regressions were incorrectly accepted
before the fix (`/tmp/luna-or-coverage-baseline.log` and
`/tmp/luna-bit-or-coverage-baseline.log`).

Both analyzers now remove regions matched by prior alternatives before considering
later ones. Unknown earlier matches prevent later alternatives from supplying
coverage evidence through different bindings. Integer regions use interval
subtraction; bit regions split symbolic fixed-bit conjunctions with bounded work,
without enumerating all bit-vector values. Bit remaps also remove obsolete source
bindings after simultaneous source lookup.

budget limits are unchanged; the 129-bit example fits the default budget.

### Boolean combinations in bit coverage

Bit-pattern guards now compose exact symbolic regions with `not`, `and`, and
`or`. Negation subtracts true regions from the current input region; conjunction
checks the right operand only where the left succeeds, and disjunction checks it
only where the left fails. Unknown computations remain unknown when evaluated;
short-circuited computations need not provide coverage evidence. This operates in
the bounded coverage analyzer, without adding program predicates to PTC.

Source regressions prove complementary Boolean formulas, execute short-circuit
cases containing an otherwise failing contract, and reject missing values and
unknown left operands. A unit oracle checks every pair of two-bit truth tables
against Boolean operations, requires disjoint output regions, and checks budget
failure followed by successful recovery. Subject projections still require known
pattern bindings; this change does not infer aliases to an outer scrutinee local.

### Conditional bit guards and local projection bindings

Bit coverage now partitions an `if` guard's input region by its condition, then
analyzes each reachable branch in that region. Unreachable branches do not need
proof evidence. Blocks can introduce local aliases of known bit projections;
these bindings are scoped to the predicate and only resulting bit constraints
escape. Other statements (including assignment or evaluated calls) remain unknown.
No program predicate is delegated to PTC.

(`/tmp/luna-bit-conditional-baseline.log`). It now proves conditional tautologies,
checks aliases in nested blocks, and executes cases whose unreachable branch has
a failing contract. Rejection cases cover unknown conditions, reachable unknown
branches, mutation, evaluated calls, and a genuinely missing input region. An
explicit fallback case verifies all four two-bit runtime results. The small-domain
unit oracle also checks conditional selection and disjoint regions for every pair
of two-bit truth tables, including budget failure/recovery.

### Type-list values for the Tuple normal-form migration

The author clarified that `Tuple` has the signature
`pure comptime fn Tuple<...Es: meta.List<Type>> -> Type`. Its input is one
collected comptime list of types; its Type identity must preserve the head and
that input. The current frontend's independent `Term::Tuple` construction and
structural inference are not a completed implementation of this contract.
Earlier tuple execution tests establish behavior of that implementation, not
compliance with the clarified identity model.

The first migration step adds `Term::TypeListValue`, a comptime-value term with
Type-sorted elements, distinct from both `Tuple` and `TupleValue`. Lists do not
introduce a binder. Substitution, interning, runtime dependency collection,
associated-type resolution, implementation candidate indexing, materialization,
and bounded term traversals visit their elements. Dumps use
`(type-list-value (...))`. PTC lifts established element-type equalities forward
through a list and an admitted enclosing normal-form head; it neither admits a
standalone list-value equality proposition nor inverts the enclosing head.

This is IR infrastructure, not source-level Tuple completion. Remaining work:
connect `meta.List<Type>` and variadic clause collection to normal-form input
metadata/checking and comptime execution, construct the actual Tuple head
application, and migrate tuple consumers to the corresponding contracts. The
legacy `Term::Tuple` producer and decomposition paths still exist and must not
be reported as the final language model. This change adds no source alias that
would hide that gap.

### Type-list values in the comptime executor

`comptime_interpretor::Value::TypeList` now preserves the identity of a completed
`meta.List<Type>` through immutable-copy accounting and normal-form freezing.
It freezes to `Term::TypeListValue`, including when nested in another immutable
value. It is distinct from a tuple of Type values, even when empty. Display uses
the same S-expression structure as the frozen term.

Freezing checks every element as a completed Type, preserves opaque normal-form
heads, rejects wrong-sort elements, active declaration inputs, unbound variables,
associated queries, and runtime dependencies. Bound variables belonging to an
inner function type remain legal. Width and element work consume the shared
budget. Host admission does not accept a list where Type or a tuple is required;
formation traversal now visits the list's element types.

This does not yet connect the `meta.List<Type>` declaration, variadic head input
metadata, or source list construction. Constant reconstruction reports its
unsupported list case explicitly instead of encoding a tuple. The next stage
must establish the actual list type identity and its collector before admitting
lists against source signatures; no Type or tuple stand-in has been introduced.

### Trusted Tuple head identity

`intrinsic::LangItem::Tuple` is an explicitly registered source normal-form head,
not an automatically installed primitive. `bind_source_normal_form_heads`
checks the package-qualified metadata identity and, when a body is transported,
requires one pure NormalForm-phase definition. Missing/duplicate identities,
runtime or impure definitions, wrong language-item categories and conflicting
registrations are rejected transactionally. Repeating the same binding is
idempotent. External head metadata can be registered without transporting a
body. Neither source spelling nor body reduction establishes this identity.

This entry point establishes identity/kind only; it does not validate Tuple's
`...Es: meta.List<Type>` telescope. The frontend driver, list identity/collector,
normal-form argument checking and old tuple consumers are not connected to this
registration yet. These remain necessary before claiming source-level Tuple
support. No assumptions about the declaration form of `meta.List` were added.

### Executable type-list normal-form input contracts

Normal-form input metadata now has `Kind::TypeList`. This is a trusted producer
contract, not a deduction from a type spelling or function body. `Parameter::ty`
still carries the actual declared list Type. The representation guard requires
an opaque/nominal Type application to `Type`; the guard itself does not designate
a language item. A future source producer must resolve the trusted list identity
before attaching this kind. Primitive Type, bool and a structural tuple are not
accepted as stand-ins.

Metadata validation and closed argument checking accept a TypeListValue for this
kind, with Type-sorted elements and bounded width. The interpreter recognizes the
exact declared list type carried by validated metadata, admits completed list
values, and reconstructs typed frozen list arguments with element validation and
budget charging. It does not unfold the list or Tuple heads.

invocation whose body builds a normal-form Type from its list parameter. Empty,
singleton, repeated and heterogeneous Type lists preserve head and input identity;

elements are rejected, and a later valid invocation on the same interpreter
succeeds. Metadata and immutable admission are also checked. These tests construct

### Source variadic normal-form Type-list collection

`Protocols::meta_list` now carries the trusted package-qualified identity of the

whose type is that constructor applied to Type. This identity is explicit;
spelling a declaration `List` does not register it. The source Splice selector
preserves other driver bindings when updating its own field.

remaining positional inputs into one TypeListValue. Ordinary prefix inputs
retain their declaration positions. Symbolic Type elements in aliases/signatures
remain symbolic. Expression inputs lower to `NormalFormArgument::TypeList`, with

effect-use traversal and staged-input support. The interpreter prepares Type
contexts and evaluates elements once in source order; early exits stop collection
and skip later elements. The resulting Type retains its opaque head and one list
argument. No Tuple/List definition body is unfolded or invoked.

### Named whole Type-list supply to normal-form collectors

A final Type-list collector now accepts `.Es = expression` after its positional
prefix. The expression is checked against the collector's declared list Type and
passed as its complete value; it is neither collected again nor wrapped in a
singleton list. The expression path preserves source evaluation once, and the
type-expression path can retain a declaration-side symbolic list input.

The shared supply check rejects duplicate pack names, unknown names, and mixing
a complete named pack with collected elements (in either order within the tail).
Incorrect whole-pack types are rejected by ordinary type checking. Other normal
arguments retain their existing routing; this does not yet implement moving a

### Whole-list supply reordered around normal-form anchors

Named whole-list supply can now precede, split, or follow a normal-form call's
ordinary positional prefix. A shared router checks names, duplicates, missing
anchors, and forbidden collected tail elements before checking input expressions.
It keeps separate declaration-slot and source-evaluation orders. Expression
elaboration emits a `NormalFormInputPlan` only when the orders differ; static
Type applications likewise evaluate inputs in source order and then assemble the
opaque arguments in declaration order. List identity and whole-pack semantics
are unchanged.

The source test `normal_type_list_named_supply_preserves_order_around_positional_anchors`
checks all three placements using distinct Type-generating calls and a list
forwarder, including exact interpreter event order. It also checks symbolic
whole-list supply before anchors in a comptime callable type, a later scalar
input dependent on an earlier computed Type, and early return from the first
named input (later anchors must not execute). Invalid missing/extra anchors,
duplicate supply and unknown names have explicit diagnostic assertions.

### Type-list spread inputs in normal-form calls

Diamond-call parsing now includes `...expr` arguments, matching the existing
argument grammar. The prior parser lacked that rule; the source test initially
exposed it with a spread block expression, and it now accepts that form directly.

Normal-form Type-list collectors accept explicit Type elements mixed with
multiple list spreads. `NormalFormArgument::TypeListSpread` preserves the spread
role through Display, expression/pattern traversal, divergence and effect-use
analysis, contextual preparation, immediate evaluation and staged evaluation.
Each spread is checked against the declared list type, evaluated once, and its
elements appended in order with budget charging. Later inputs do not execute
after an early return. A sole spread after all anchors takes the whole-list path,
which also preserves a symbolic list in a type expression without wrapping it.
Static mixed collection can flatten completed list terms; mixed unknown symbolic
lists in a Type expression still require a residual representation and currently
report that limitation. Spreads that must supply ordinary anchors and optional
collector/default combinations also remain unsupported.

checks empty and heterogeneous lists, repeated spreads with explicit elements,
whole-list forwarding, symbolic sole forwarding in a callback type, spread-block
early return, wrong-type rejection, the retained opaque result and exact call
events. Neither the Tuple head nor the List head is unfolded.

distinct from both TypeValue and Tuple. Required-invocation reconstruction and

list domain against trusted TypeList parameter metadata and validate each Type
element. Copy accounting includes embedded types. Missing authority, non-Type
elements, unbound types and wrong result domains are rejected.

### Release rejected aggregate freeze inputs without recursive destruction

record could overflow the host stack while being dropped after freezing rejected

destruction of the remaining input bypassed that protection.

exhausted semantic fuel: the rejected owned data must still be released. The
normal-form result, integer canonicalization, field order and label checks are
unchanged. This does not claim to make destruction of arbitrary embedded IR or
executable environments stack-independent.

### Contextual library enum variants and explicit impl subjects

The shipped library no longer treats Option/Result constructors as module-level
functions. Root/prelude exports retain the enum types, and implementations,
iterator matches and collection results use contextual `.Some`, `.None`, `.Ok`
and `.Err`, matching the formal enum construction/pattern forms. Generic impl
subjects now carry their declared arguments (`Option<T>`, `Result<T,E>`, adapter

### Prepared BitVec compound assignment

Compound assignment now supports BitVec views of local/field/pointer storage,
including nested static and dynamic selections. It freezes the target pointer,
evaluates selectors once in source order, snapshots the selected old bits, then
evaluates the RHS and dispatches the bound arithmetic protocol. The final write
uses the frozen selectors and preserves other bits as modified by the RHS.
Private preparation bindings use fresh identities and generated source ranges;
the implementation reuses existing NIR nodes and their S-expression displays.

An initially failing early-return regression revealed that a divergent selector
must propagate Never to the prepared read instead of attempting operator
selection for BitVec<0>; that is corrected. Dynamic widths still need the same
known width/context as existing bit windows (the pointer-rebinding regression
supplies an explicitly typed BitVec delta). No intrinsic BitVec arithmetic was
added. Runtime and comptime tests cover evaluation order, pointer rebinding,
nested and empty ranges, heterogeneous RHS protocols, selector/RHS exits,
immutable whole bindings, out-of-bounds ranges, and wrong-width operator results.

### Contextual heterogeneous RHS for BitVec compound assignment

A regression using `bits[0..4] += .enable` exposed premature RHS contextualization:
the location planner forced unresolved RHS expressions into BitVec before normal
arithmetic protocol selection. The planner now retains an unresolved compound
RHS; after preparing the selected old bit value, ordinary operator elaboration
supplies the unique RHS domain. Already checked RHS expressions are reused and
still evaluated once after the old value. Ordinary bit assignment continues to
require a fully checked width-matching RHS. Final compound-result expectations
are checked after arithmetic elaboration, including divergence.

New cases cover contextual enum variants directly, in blocks and conditionals,
for all five compound arithmetic operators at runtime and comptime (30 positive

expected associated annotations through the immutable package dispatch world,
then still requires exact equality with the selected body's signature. Completed
signature views are local to the inference; normal-form heads are not unfolded.

### Complete optional propagation in partially inferred callback results

A callback expected to return ?T can now propagate an optional operand before T
is known. Its successful paths determine the payload; pending missing returns
are completed with that result type before the callback leaves elaboration or
enters cleanup planning. Pending sites are isolated across nested checking
contexts and restored with argument-attempt transactions. Operand and result
payloads may differ. A callback with no payload evidence still rejects; arbitrary
unknown return shapes and automatic sysroot binding remain unsupported.

An explicit `return null` in a callback expected to return `?T` no longer demands

return is tracked privately and completed before exporting the closure. Missing
returns contribute no payload evidence; nested callbacks keep separate pending
sites and observations. All-missing callbacks and conflicting successful payloads
still reject. This change covers explicit missing returns, not arbitrary deferred
null-valued expressions.

### Avoid repeated no-evidence optional branch probes

no-evidence result immediately after exhausting their candidate branches. The

### Indirect pointer paths in body-derived memory footprints

ParameterPlace now retains successive pointer loads separately from final field
selection. Composition across calls and pointer results preserves these paths;
its S-expression dump spells each load explicitly. Call-site checking resolves
loads against current stored pointer provenance after argument evaluation and
checks intermediate slots as well as final targets. Loaded pointer results retain
their actual owner dependencies when the original slot is subsequently rebound.

Conditional borrowed-body checking creates bounded pointee-validity premises on
demand, without scheduling cleanup or asserting non-aliasing. Concrete callers
must discharge the footprint against their actual targets. Premise IDs use a
separate namespace and a shared allocator across branches and nested frames.

Consumers without pointer contents cannot flatten these paths: program-flow
analysis falls back to conservative invalidation for indirect writes, and captured
Drop access checking rejects indirect accesses until it receives stored pointer
provenance. Body-derived summaries still reject pointer-slot writes and owned
pointee transfers; ordered pointer mutation contracts remain future work.
