### Resolve indirect destructor footprints at cleanup time

The Drop access checker now accepts a borrowed PointerMemory snapshot containing
root types, stored pointer alternatives, and positions retired earlier in the
cleanup sequence. Each load checks its slot, all target alternatives, the actual
pointee type, and final access availability. Missing/empty provenance, wrong target
types, exhausted budgets, and dead targets reject without modifying the snapshot.
AccessCheck records resolved targets in access order and dumps them as stable
S-expressions. The original API without pointer evidence remains conservative.

CleanupSession and owned local/replacement planning now supply this snapshot.
The planner tracks retired subobjects in emitted cleanup order; variant branches
keep separate retirement histories, and variant refinement retains other roots
needed by indirect accesses. Local exit planning also tracks previously retired
locals. Replacement planning checks the old object's pointer contents before
installing the replacement's origins. This permits valid destructors to read or
write an external scalar through stored pointers while rejecting dependencies on
already destroyed locals or earlier-cleaned sibling fields.

Conditional borrowed-pointee roots are keyed by analysis-frame identity and
pointer-slot path. Branches and loop iterations share the same premise for the
same slot; nested closure/default/call frames use separate identities. Joins
complete these conditional premises without adding owned storage or granting
noalias facts. Actual invocation still validates every rebased target against the
caller's storage state. This closes the prior declaration-order mismatch for
branches loading different pointer-valued fields.

Memory-summary inference now retains direct, capture-free local closure identities
through bindings, copies and strong assignment. Compatible branches retain the
identity; unknown or different assignments remove it, including loop backedges.
The immutable body reference remains local to inference and is never published
as a synthetic function declaration. Its footprint is derived on invocation,
rebased through the existing argument preparation path, and preserves returned
pointer origins. Enclosing generic substitutions reach the closure signature and
body analysis. Anonymous bodies share the named-function worklist so recursive
edges cannot recursively restart complete summary inference.

memory summary classified these local closure calls as unknown dynamic calls
(`/tmp/luna-borrow-context-current.log`, exit 101). All three borrowed-pointer
regressions then passed, including distinct pointee types in closure frames,
actual aliasing, loops and rejection of a consumed actual target.
New summary regressions cover alias copies, rebinding, unknown assignments in
branches and loops, returned pointers, recursive calls, unused closure bodies,
generic substitution, budget failure and recovery.

### Local closure candidate sets in memory summaries

Local capture-free closure evidence now retains a finite candidate set across
branch and loop joins. Calls derive every candidate's footprint using the shared
package worklist, then merge accesses, possible checked rejection, and returned
pointer targets before rebasing to the caller. Strong assignment replaces the
current value; loop history unions possible identities. An unknown alternative
removes the complete-set evidence rather than silently keeping only known code.
Blocks, if expressions and match arms snapshot their closure result while their
own environment is active. Candidate ordering uses deterministic first-visit
ordinals; source-node addresses are only ephemeral lookup keys, never dump order
or published declaration identity.

failure/recovery and existing recursive/generic closure tests remain passing.

### Mixed named and anonymous local code candidates

Memory inference now interns complete named instance identities and capture-free
closure definitions into one invocation-local candidate table. Candidate joins
therefore retain both kinds across if/match results, mutable assignments and loop
backedges. Named instance arguments remain part of identity. Each candidate still
uses its existing body/summary checker, and all footprints are merged before
checking actual pointer targets. The table uses deterministic first-visit ordinals
and never invents a source declaration for anonymous code.

instances, distinct Boolean/byte instantiations in one analysis, returned pointer
unions, runtime choice, budget failure/recovery, a third unknown alternative, and
rejection of a consumed target. Unknown or forwarded code without complete
premises still cannot establish a complete local candidate set.

### Local owned capture environments and construction-time code snapshots

Named-function memory inference now invokes local closures with supported
pointer-free owned captures. Scalar capture values remain abstract; captured
named-code identities are snapshotted at construction, including code stored in
owned fields. Initializers are observed in source order. Later outer-variable
assignments cannot change an earlier closure's snapshot. Repeated construction
of one closure node interns distinct code snapshots and reuses equal snapshots,
so loop analysis converges instead of conflating different captured functions or
allocating a fresh abstract identity on every iteration. Branch results now
retain candidates for environment-bearing closure types as well as plain fn.

The existing closure-summary checker validates each saved code premise and its
field type. Local invocation uses the shared recursive worklist and enclosing
generic substitution. No source declaration or PTC memory proposition is created.
Pointer-bearing captured storage and anonymous callable captures still require
richer environment transport and are not admitted by this path.

A soundness check found that simply reusing construction snapshots across calls
would be wrong when the closure itself overwrites captured code: the baseline
reported only the first function's target even after a second call could use a
different function. Local snapshot-based invocation now rejects writes to captured
code slots or aggregates containing code until environment transition contracts
are propagated. This is an implementation limitation, not a language ban on
mutable closures. The existing per-invocation public closure checker remains
available with fresh caller-supplied premises; ordinary outer rebinding remains
supported and does not trigger this restriction.

### Reusable capture invariants for source-defined code transitions

Local closure memory summaries now close captured named-code identities over
source-defined assignments. Each analysis pass records code writes to capture
slots independently of continuation environments, including writes on early
return paths. The next pass widens the capture premise with these named instances;
analysis stops only when the set no longer grows, under the shared fuel budget
and package worklist. The resulting footprint covers possible later invocations
of the same closure. Ordinary scalar capture state remains abstract.

Supported writes include direct named definitions/instances, conditional choices
of fixed source definitions, callback fields and whole owned records containing
those callbacks. Their source evaluation remains in the original body. Code
provided by one invocation's parameters or returned dynamically cannot be made a
reusable invariant by assuming that invocation's identity persists; such writes
still require explicit environment-state transport and are rejected. Unknown
initial capture identities and anonymous-code transitions are also incomplete.
This is a conservative reusable footprint, not precise per-call environment-state
analysis, and it can require targets that a particular first call will not use.

slot and aggregate replacement, early return, a loop, budget recovery, actual
successive calls selecting different functions, rejection of a dead second-call
target, and rejection of a captured assignment derived from invocation input.

summaries still do not transport these local anonymous identities.

### Anonymous callback premises across named function boundaries

Named memory instances now include transaction-local prepared-code identities in
addition to the declaration, type arguments and named callback inputs. The
worklist interns complete owned closure definitions and named capture snapshots;
forwarding or recursive calls reuse structurally identical entries. Definitions
are specialized in their defining frame before crossing a named boundary. This
prevents the recipient's generic parameters from being used to interpret the
callback's body. Each published `Summary.prepared_inputs` retains its actual code
premises, with S-expression Display; private arena ordinals are not published as
language identities. No normal-form head is unfolded.

carry anonymous/mixed callbacks through scalar and owned-field parameters. The
resource bridge validates input layouts and environments, and the cleanup path
uses the same bridge. Construction-time provisional calls can retain the specific
unknown-callback obligation for actual invocation, without inventing a memory
footprint or pointer result. Other failures, including exhausted budgets, are not
converted into deferred success.

### Data-only environment replacement and complete mutation paths

Capture mutation discovery now includes environment-bearing callable leaves in
owned records and tuples. It has a separate traversal mode from the published
named-result lattice. Previously a whole-record replacement could skip such a
leaf: the new regression inferred only parameter 0 although a later invocation
read parameter 1. `/tmp/luna-capture-data-baseline.log` records this missing-target
failure (exit 101). The corrected invariant retains both targets and caller-side
checking rejects a retired second target.

Replacement closure literals may capture abstract data: supported intrinsic
scalars and recursively plain owned records/tuples. Their runtime values remain
unknown to memory inference, so values supplied by a particular invocation cannot
narrow future code targets. The closure definition itself and all possible
pointer accesses still participate in the invariant. Capture initialization is
walked at its source evaluation point; importing the resulting code snapshot does
not rerun initialization. Captured function/closure identities and pointer-bearing
or unsupported layouts are not classified as abstract plain data. In particular,
a record that hides a callback is rejected instead of silently authorizing a new
environment from its type alone.

runtime Bool values, nested plain records, callback identities hidden in a record,

### Complete anonymous code results across memory summaries

Memory summaries now retain owned, specialized code candidates at callable result
paths, including anonymous definitions and their captured code premises. Result
leaves distinguish recursive `NoReturn`, complete `Known` candidates and absorbing
`Unknown`; an unknown branch cannot disappear when joined with a known callback.
Returned descriptors participate in the named worklist, so recursive factories
can converge without restarting inference on the Rust stack. Interning, cloning,
comparison and nested descriptor traversal consume the shared inference budget.

This connects named and anonymous factories, returned record fields, forwarding
of supplied callbacks, generic definitions and factories that return another
factory. Captured callbacks remain in the defining environment rather than being
rebound to the receiving invocation. Both explicit returns and implicit block
results contribute to result evidence. Calls still discharge pointer accesses
against actual live origins; a returned code identity does not establish pointer
validity or ownership of a returned capture environment. Resource fallback from
these summaries recovers only environment-free code, while existing contextual
ownership analysis handles supported environment-bearing returns.

Two older Drop fixtures expected every anonymous result candidate to be rejected.
They now execute both known branches, distinguish their writes and check named
call counts; their existing retired-pointer rejection cases remain. New tests
cover result specialization, recursive bottom versus unknown, nested callback
captures, explicit return branches, actual target retirement and budget recovery.
Review also fixed a dump bug that repeated result code fields inside prepared
input premises. Its regression checks balanced single-root S-expression nesting
and requires result fields to occur exactly once at summary level.

### Recursive returned closures with Copy data environments

Resource analysis can now recover returned code identity for closures whose
captures have closed, identity-free data layouts and established Copy delivery.
The memory fixed point supplies the complete candidate set; resource checking
separately checks every capture's layout and Copy capability. Supported layouts
contain intrinsic scalar values, owned records/tuples and known struct fields.
Trusted Tuple metadata supplies structure without replacing its normal-form
identity. Pointer, callable, enum and opaque layouts cannot use this recovery.
No returned runtime data is reconstructed or evaluated during analysis.

This fixes recursive factories returning a Bool-capturing closure: their memory
footprints already included both possible reads, but the finite ownership walk
lost code identity at the recursive edge and rejected invocation. The new fallback
works for nested Copy structs as well. Unknown or unsupported candidates invalidate
the whole result leaf; they are never removed to leave a known subset. Capture
layout traversal consumes the shared analysis budget. General affine capture
state, code-bearing captures and pointer origin transport still need separate
returned-environment evidence.

### Stable callback captures across recursive factory returns

Returned code recovery now imports complete captured callback candidates from
both named capture premises and prepared anonymous descriptors. Each capture
still needs Copy delivery and a closed supported layout. Environment-free
function leaves may occur directly or inside owned records, tuples and known
structs; every callable leaf needs complete evidence. Unknown, empty or conflicting
premises invalidate the entire result candidate instead of dropping uncertainty.
Named candidates are checked against the expected callable signature.

Construction-time code identity is usable only while the corresponding captured
positions remain stable. A bounded body walk rejects assignments and address-taking
that overlap a protected callback position, including replacing an ancestor record.
Disjoint data-field updates are permitted. Copies of the original input may change
independently without changing the returned environment's snapshot. This mechanism
neither replays capture initialization nor reconstructs runtime capture values.

General mutable callback state remains a separate requirement: a recursive
factory returning a closure that replaces its own captured callback still needs
current environment-state transport. Pointer-bearing, enum-tag-dependent, affine
and nested environment-bearing callback captures do not gain ownership evidence
from this fallback.

### Explicit representation-copy delivery operations

Ownership reports and published function cleanup schedules now distinguish Copy
representation deliveries from ownership transfers. Both operations retain source,
binding and field path identity, including contextual function/closure schedules.
Report merging preserves copy operations; publication deduplicates them. Dumps
emit `(copies (representation-copy ...))`. Runtime admission rejects duplicate
copy operations and a copy/move conflict at the same source place.

The interpreter executes the published copy at value delivery and at implicit
lexical capture acquisition. Recursive representation copying gives owned closure
capture storage fresh cells while preserving code and external pointer identity.
Records, tuples and variants recursively carry this behavior. Ordinary invocation
receiver observation has no copy delivery operation and retains its receiver.
Copy rejects capture cells with transferred child responsibilities; recursive
copying is depth/fuel bounded. This is the operation mechanism, not an automatic
capability grant or an implicit user Clone call.

A semantic prerequisite remains open for nested returned environments. The formal
`docs/type/qualified-types/closure-type.md` explicitly forbids user impl subjects
of closure type. An initial attempted `impl Duplicate for Toggle` regression was
therefore invalid and correctly failed subject eligibility; it was removed from
the suite. The user has been asked whether closure Copy should be a built-in rule
when every capture has legal Copy capability and no unique cleanup responsibility.
No such automatic classification rule was introduced. Copy acquisition's supported
representation categories now include closure layouts, but capability acquisition
remains an independent prerequisite. Nested recursive-return recovery still does
not accept environment-bearing callback captures on the strength of layout alone.

### Bounded borrowed representation copying

Representation copying now borrows the source tree instead of cloning closure
metadata and captured payloads before visiting them. It respects the configured
interpreter depth in addition to the hard recursion ceiling. Aggregate widths,
owned labels, type arguments, pointer metadata and integer/BitVec storage are
charged before their corresponding allocations or clones. Immutable code bodies
and string storage remain shared. A failed copy does not replace or consume its
source value.

Storage copying obtains a guard that keeps both ownership metadata and payload
stable while visiting them. The ownership tree is checked iteratively with depth
and width accounting; partially transferred children are rejected before payload
copying. Nonblocking guard acquisition rejects malformed cyclic owned storage
instead of recursively waiting on a lock already held by the same copy. Errors
release every guard and partial result; the same interpreter can retry after a
malformed source is repaired. Ordinary pointers retain weak external targets and
are not followed by the copy visitor.

### Source List/Tuple heads and sysroot language-item defaults

The library now provides `meta.List<T>` and
`builtin.tuple.Tuple<...Es: meta.List<Type>>` as pure comptime normal-form heads.
Their bodies return their own opaque applications. Head construction retains
identity without unfolding a body or substituting a placeholder scalar type.
Tuple is re-exported at builtin root and through builtin.prelude. Current list
value support remains the compiler's immutable `List<Type>` representation;
general List element operations are not implemented by these declarations.

For explicit `--sysroot <directory>` NIR compilation, the standalone driver reads
an optional `<directory>/language-items.conf`. This is a bounded UTF-8 key/value
configuration, not a source-name heuristic. Version 1 requires `version = 1` and
accepts `splice-protocol`, `meta-list-type`, `tuple-type`, and `optional-type` keys
with unquoted `package::definition` or `package::module::definition` values.
Blank lines and `#` comments are allowed. Unknown/duplicate keys, invalid selectors,
unsupported/missing versions and files larger than 64 KiB are errors. The shipped
configuration selects `meta::List` and `builtin::tuple::Tuple`.

Explicit CLI selectors or supplied driver identities take precedence over these
defaults. Existing identity/signature checks still apply after resolution, and a
same-spelled user definition does not acquire compiler Tuple authority. AST/HIR
inspection does not require type-constructor configuration. A configuration file
used as an input cannot also be the output, including through a hard link. Without
an explicit sysroot or supplied constructor binding, the legacy unbound tuple
path remains; this is not completion of that migration.

### Comptime type-list indexing

Compiler-bound `meta.List<Type>` values now support `values[index]` with a
comptime `Integer` index. The NIR `TypeListIndex` operation retains both operands
and dumps as `(type-list-index (values ...) (index ...))`. Type rewriting,
materialization, required-expression inspection and phase traversal visit both
operands. List evaluation precedes index evaluation, each occurs once, and an
index expression's nonlocal return propagates with `Never` type. The selected
`Term` preserves its normal-form head; inspecting Tuple's collected arguments
never unfolds Tuple or substitutes structural tuple identity.

Negative, empty-list, oversized and out-of-range indexes report
`IndexOutOfBounds` at the indexing source. Selecting a type charges its bounded
type inspection work against the interpreter budget. Indexing operates on the
evaluated list value without changing a stored source list. Runtime storage,
noninteger indexes, unsupported element types and a same-spelled unbound List
remain rejected. This adds indexing for the supported type-list representation;
it does not implement general-purpose `meta.List<T>` operations or finish the
legacy structural Tuple migration.

### Resumable Type invocations: elaboration foundation

`elaboration::type_computations::Session` now owns invocation-local waiters for
ordinary, already checked comptime functions whose result is `Type`. Enqueueing
reserves a Type inference variable; both each argument's domain and value can
refer to existing `InferenceTerm`s. Resumption follows current alias leaves,
waits without interpreting when inputs remain unresolved, then invokes the
existing comptime interpreter and assigns only the completed Type. The returned
normal-form term is retained exactly. Waiting state is neither a Type nor a
normal-form head and never enters NIR. The session has an S-expression Display.

The session is tied to one package, one committed inference context and one
interpreter budget. Candidate contexts cannot execute it; committing pure input
inference first permits later resumption in the original context. Invocation
failure is terminal and does not replay effects. Failed producers propagate an
associated failure to consumers, and dependency cycles are found with iterative
graph traversal before invocation. External assignment of a reserved output is
rejected before effects. Completed results and failed calls are not rerun.

This is a tested foundation, not completed signature integration. The source
checker still needs to retain pending signature expressions, connect their
inputs to this machinery and resume body/signature checking before producing
successful IIR. The ignored `type_list_indexing_specializes_runtime_parameter_and_result_types`
acceptance test remains unfinished. Current session admission accepts ordinary
functions without clause type parameters and with a directly known Type result;
generic target instantiation and arbitrary expression-root preparation remain
separate integration work. No PTC obligation executes these invocations.

### Stable residual Type invocation descriptors

`nir::type_computations::Invocation` is the immutable saved-call representation
paired with the active elaboration Session. It contains a declaration target,
explicit binder sorts, typed canonical argument templates and the actual free
input slots read by those templates. It contains no inference IDs, wait tickets,
interpreter state or provisional Type identity. Its constructor validates scope,
rejects reads of runtime input slots and bounds structure before recursive binder
operations. Nested normal-form heads remain unchanged. Display uses the
`residual-type-invocation` S-expression form.

`Session::enqueue_residual` instantiates such a descriptor into fresh output
inference variables. It checks demanded binding sorts and uses capture-avoiding
inference substitution; unused slots do not become wait dependencies. The saved
descriptor can be shared by independent instances without sharing mutable state.
Admission/execution against the package still belongs to Session, so a structurally
valid descriptor is not proof that its target or argument values are executable.

This adds the stable descriptor and its execution adapter, not source signature
integration. Automatic production of these descriptors from marked HIR expressions,
definition-side Any/refinement checking and completion of signature/body instances
remain pending. Successful IIR must not contain unexecuted descriptors for its

### Demand-driven Type computation dependencies

`elaboration::type_computations::Session::resume_dependencies` drives a demanded
output's reachable pending computations in deterministic dependency order.
It preflights the reachable graph with an explicit scheduling fuel budget before
invoking any ready node. Cycles become terminal failures through the existing
resume contract; scheduling budget exhaustion remains retryable without replay.
External inference leaves remain waiting, shared producers execute once, and
unrelated computations are not scheduled. A synchronous pass reuses its cycle
check: publication produces stable Types and cannot introduce new inference
edges. This avoids rescanning each transitive dependency graph during execution.

The source-backed tests cover a diamond, delayed input assignment, scheduling
budget exhaustion and retry, an unrelated recursive computation, terminal query
replay, producer failure propagation, and a cycle with an otherwise ready sibling
that must not execute. This scheduling API does not yet connect open deferred
source signatures or implement their Any/refinement checking.

### Stop invocation after a failed Type demand

Dependency driving now stops invoking independent siblings once a reachable
producer fails, while continuing to publish dependency failures toward the
requested output. Preflight also detects already-cached failures, so an earlier
ready sibling cannot execute merely because the failed branch appears later in
scheduling order. Skipped siblings remain pending and may still be demanded
independently; they do not inherit unrelated errors. Work completed before a new
failure is discovered is not rolled back.

### Gradual descriptions without equality axioms

`elaboration::gradual` introduces a definition-side description boundary:
`Description::Any` is separate from `Known(InferenceTerm)`, and never becomes an
immutable type identity or an inference assignment. Compatibility reports
`Gradual`, a full exact PTC outcome, or unresolved inference dependencies.
A gradual result is not member/trait evidence, a conversion, a layout, or a
runtime delivery plan. Known operands still require Type sort and valid scope,
even when compared with Any. All descriptions and results have S-expression
Display implementations.

The no-target join retains an equal description only with equality evidence.
Distinct types, or opaque identities for which equality lacks a validated model,
may widen to Any without claiming inequality or creating a union. Budget
exhaustion remains an unproven result, rather than silently changing precision.
Existing PTC assumptions can prove exact equality; description checks add no
facts to that context. Computation outputs remain waiting inference terms until
invocation publishes their actual Types.

This is currently a top-level description/checking API. Source Any/any syntax,
nested gradual descriptions, refinement extraction, ordinary member checking,
and runtime specialization/delivery are not connected by this change. Open

callee bodies are elaborated. Once admitted, the Bool atom participates in

separate. Full signature resolution reuses the same ordered advancement.

### Definition-local refinement assumptions and separate instance admission

`gradual::RefinementScope` binds a collection of type refinements to a fresh
declaration-local subject. Construction validates every formula before adding
any hypothesis, including formulas after a false requirement. Its proof context
is private and local to definition checking; it does not represent Any as a Type
identity or add equality facts to inference. The caller must allocate a fresh
declaration subject. The S-expression dump retains the subject and conjunction.

`check_instance` deliberately uses the borrowed parent context, excluding the
definition hypotheses. A concrete instance must prove all requirements. Any
still needs instantiation, unresolved inference remains waiting, and a failed or
unknown proof grants no admission. A proof of a type requirement alone does not
deliver a member origin, implementation route, layout, or conversion.

### Lexical facts after successful let patterns

After a let-pattern statement completes normally, block checking adds its
audited pattern/guard type facts to the context for subsequent statements and
the block result. A divergent initializer or guard publishes no continuation
facts. Let failure branches are checked before these success facts are added,
and the declaration's final guard can use facts established by its pattern.

success and error. Inner blocks inherit outer successful-let facts but do not
export new facts to their enclosing block, sibling branches, or loop exits.
This uses only immutable TypeValue observations; it does not infer facts about
mutable program state or treat arbitrary Boolean guards as type propositions.

### Normal-completion type facts and loop guards

Statement continuation analysis now computes bounded formulas from checked
control flow. A divergent if branch leaves the opposite condition on the normal
continuation. When both branches complete, their path formulas are disjoined;
PTC can derive a common consequence even when the two paths establish it through
different equalities. A predecessor with no available facts prevents unsound
narrowing. Nested blocks and initializers contribute only their normal-completion
formula, not their local proof context or bindings.

This extends the earlier conservative lexical isolation: an immutable type fact
supported by every normal exit may survive an inner block. Facts from only one
of several completing paths still cannot escape. Successful let facts and
constant Type-pattern identities participate in this summary.

`while` already lowers to a loop with a conditional break. The surviving guard
path now supplies its positive type facts to the loop body. Loop completion
itself supplies no body fact or negated condition, because break can exit while
the condition remains true. Runtime state predicates remain outside PTC.

of its annotation and all later annotations. Zero-budget execution runs no

position once; later writes to the original storage do not change that value.

analysis include the position expression. Dynamic extraction is not treated as
a total structural initializer or a fixed projection by the bit coverage solver.

Source checking elaborates the position once and classifies its dependencies:
closed comptime computations still use required invocation, while runtime calls,
free inputs, pointer/effect operations and enclosing control-flow exits remain
in the body. Interpreter failures are never used to select the other phase.
Comptime invocations check concrete positions; residual runtime operations enter
the mandatory program-flow gate, which requires `0 <= i < width`. Fixed-width
arithmetic in the index must first satisfy its own overflow obligations. Unknown
bounds report a diagnostic directing the author to contracts or checked assumes;
no program-bound proposition is sent to PTC. The verifier may use type premises
only to recover abstract operand domains. Proof reports include `bit-index` points.

### Runtime BitVec slice endpoints

Dynamic half-open reads now retain a `BitWindow` NIR/IIR node. Its operands are
visited and evaluated in source order: value, lower endpoint, upper endpoint.
The result type carries the fixed width and the dump exposes all three operands.
Closed comptime endpoints are evaluated once and replaced by typed literals.
Both-static ranges retain the existing `BitSlice` path.

Without a result context, the checker infers a constant endpoint difference from
the side-effect-free integer polynomial fragment, through degree three. An
explicit `BitVec<N>` context can instead supply the candidate width. Neither
route supplies a safety assumption: the mandatory program verifier proves both
endpoints are in `0..=input_width` and their actual difference equals N. It freezes
the first endpoint before evaluating the second, retaining snapshot evidence
across calls and writes and allowing later checks to refine surviving relations.
Machine arithmetic in either endpoint must satisfy its own obligations first.
Comptime invocation checks the concrete range and result width directly.

preconditions relating endpoints, late checks, pointer writes, operand snapshots,

absence of comptime replay, malformed IR and interpreter recovery. Insufficient
bounds, negative positions, mismatched widths, reversed/out-of-range windows and
unknown widths without a result context are rejected.

### External scalar pointer observations and call preconditions

The program verifier now gives repeated reads through the same external pointer
binding a stable scalar observation until a write, call, effect, loop boundary,
or rebinding invalidates it. Observations cover Boolean and fixed-width integer
pointees. They are ghost values, not ownership roots or evidence that distinct
pointers cannot alias. Branch joins retain only matching observations; pattern
scope cleanup retains observations whose address binding remains in scope.
Dereferences in `requires` are classified as program predicates, never PTC
propositions. This supports checking bodies such as `read(p)` with
`ensures result == p.*`, bounded arithmetic under `requires p.* < 255`, and
inherited trait method contracts with renamed pointer parameters.

Calls without selected defaults import scalar pointee facts only after all
arguments have evaluated. Known targets use the captured address and current
contents; external observations must still be current. Later argument writes
cannot reuse an earlier memory bound. Rebinding the pointer variable does not
change an already evaluated argument's address. Calls with defaults do not yet
import these facts; general pointer memory postconditions are not exported to
callers, and arbitrary pointer expressions or aggregate pointees do not yet gain
this observation cache. The readonly-default extension below supersedes the
initial restriction on calls with defaults.

Boolean expression results now discard relations whose value identities became
stale during operand evaluation or a branch join. Independently computed ranges
remain available. Current Boolean relations can refine result ranges, allowing
stable repeated reads to establish Boolean postconditions. Regression cases
cover both `and` and `or` with writes in the second operand and reject subsequent
calls whose preconditions would hold only for the pre-write value.

### Dynamic bit-view writeback

Local and field destinations now accept dynamic single-bit and fixed-width range
selections, including nested mixtures of static and dynamic slices. `BitUpdate`
retains a source-ordered `BitSelection` plan; both have S-expression displays.

are accumulated. Endpoints reuse the read-side width and program-bound rules;
an explicitly typed RHS may supply the final candidate width. Endpoint checking
precedes RHS staging and prepared endpoints are never elaborated or invoked again.

Interpretation evaluates every selection once, then the RHS, then reads the
current destination and commits the bit replacement. This freezes positions and
RHS values while preserving RHS changes to untouched bits and sibling fields.
Failure or a control-flow exit before commit leaves that replacement unperformed.
Selection count is charged to interpreter/traversal/validation/resource budgets.

node and its position expressions. Ownership checks destination availability
only after positions and RHS have finished; a move during either phase cannot
leave a writable target. Program flow proves relative bounds and invalidates
facts about the updated storage, without sending program propositions to PTC.

### Protocol divergence and enclosing method-contract premises

Index and binary arithmetic now share the final protocol-call construction.
A diverging argument contributes no type evidence: the checker recovers a
uniquely established protocol argument context instead of incorrectly querying
for `Access<Never>` / an arithmetic implementation on Never. The original
Never-typed expression stays in the call, preserving its control transfer and
ordinary argument-temporary lifetime. Missing or ambiguous input context is
still rejected; the checker does not arbitrarily choose an implementation.

Source method program-contract checking now imports the enclosing trait or impl
**type** premises into its local checking context before the checked interface
world is published. Previously a trait constraint such as `K == u8` was only
inherited later, so `requires idx < 255` failed while forming the method contract.
The local context is restored afterward; program facts are never sent to PTC,
method requirements are not fabricated, and callers still have to prove the
actual program preconditions. Implementation bodies still have to establish
postconditions. Regressions reject violated bounds, incorrect implementations,
ineligible type instances and leakage of these premises into unrelated code.

A cleanup-scheduled regression verifies the exact trace: receiver evaluation,

ordinary-call cleanup machinery rather than a special indexing lifetime rule.

### Inherited method-contract premises and preserved predicate reads

Trait checking now collects the complete method-free declaration graph and
validates parent cycles before forming method program contracts. Those local
headers supply bounded forward implications from Self capabilities, including
substituted and diamond parents. They are never published as callable methods
with empty preconditions. This removes declaration-order dependence while
retaining the distinction between subject guarantees and parameter-only
formation requirements: the latter cannot justify their own admission.

Bodyless method contracts can resolve their declared `self` receiver. Function
NIR now retains the same implied type requirements used to check a generic or
default method body, so later program verification can recover its scalar input
domains. The facts come only from declared capabilities and type implications;
no program-state proposition enters PTC. Regressions cover forward declarations,
three diamond declaration orders, substituted parents, default methods, ordinary
generic callers, violated bounds, incorrect postconditions, missing parent
implementations, cyclic parents and premise isolation.

Program-contract rebinding now traverses the pointer reads, addresses and field
pointers already admitted by the predicate-shape checker. Writes remain rejected.
Source tests exercise renamed implementation parameters and read predicates;
NIR tests inspect the rebound roots for direct, addressed and projected pointers.
When a scalar observation has a known interval but no stable symbolic identity,
flow comparison can now prove only relations that hold for every pair in the
two intervals. Exhaustive small-domain tests compare these decisions against
concrete integer pairs for all six relations. Overlapping ranges do not imply
that two reads observe the same value.

An independently observed limitation remains: proving equality between repeated
reads through unknown external pointers needs a persistent memory-observation
model. Symbolic pointee views in generic pointer predicates also remain limited.
No external pointer is assigned a fabricated distinct storage identity, and no
unproven observation equality was admitted to make those examples pass.

### Scalar observations through nominal and anonymous field pointers

External scalar observations now use a pointer binding plus a checked field path
instead of only a local pointer name. Nominal paths retain declaration identity;
anonymous paths retain slot identity in the checked root type. Nested pointer
projections share observations only for the same path. Rebinding the root removes
all its observations, scope cleanup follows the root lifetime, joins intersect
complete paths, and copying/joining paths charges the verification budget.
The existing field-path S-expression display is reused. These keys are still
ghost observations, not ownership or non-aliasing evidence.

Call preconditions now drive the set of scalar pointee reads imported into the
prepared frame. After all arguments run, each required path is projected from
captured caller targets, or matched to a still-current captured external
observation with the same scalar view. Relative paths allow passing a field
pointer, forwarding an entire struct pointer, and aliasing that pointer through
a readonly default. This supersedes the earlier scalar-pointee-only call import.
No aggregate contents are invented for unknown pointers; non-scalar leaves and
pointer expressions outside local bindings and checked field projections remain
unsupported by this observation mechanism.

New source cases cover nested nominal and anonymous records, Boolean and integer
fields, whole-struct forwarding, readonly default aliases and actual execution.
Reject cases distinguish sibling paths, invalidate rebinding and writes, and
check later argument writes before importing a field bound. Anonymous record
construction through an unconstrained runtime factory uses an explicit checked
`assumes` to establish the returned flag, rather than inferring the factory body
as a result contract.

### Readonly scalar pointee postconditions at call sites

Call result export now admits scalar pointer reads when the callee and selected
defaults have proved readonly memory summaries and the callee's parameter
bindings remain stable. Required observations are imported after argument
evaluation from known caller targets or unchanged external observations, using
the same field-path mechanism as preconditions. Result facts reconnect to the
original caller values through the checked copy mappings, preserving both bounds
and equalities. For example, `ensures result == p.*` can prove `read(p) + 1`
under `p.* < 255`, and a caller can compare the result with its stable prior read.
Scalar result-only and entry-snapshot postconditions retain their existing path.

The new export is gated independently of ordinary precondition checking.
Writing or opaque callees cannot connect result facts to entry memory. The
bounded body check also excludes parameter rebinding and address-taking, because
memory-readonly alone does not establish the identity of a parameter address at
return. Effects in later arguments are accounted for before observations are
imported. General post-write memory relations and readonly inference for opaque
trait/closure calls remain unimplemented; no runtime reads are inserted by this
proof analysis.

Regression cases cover concrete and external pointers, field pointers, readonly
default aliases, result bounds and exact relations. They reject weakened
contracts when equality is required, overflowing contents, writes in later
arguments, writing callees, and IR parameter rebinding that changes the address
observed by the callee's postcondition.

### Scalar observations after external pointer writes

Direct scalar pointer writes now establish a fresh observation for the written
path after invalidating possibly aliased facts. The verifier captures the root
binding's value identity when evaluating the address, evaluates the RHS once,
and checks that the root still denotes that captured address before installing
the new observation. RHS effects that rebind or invalidate the pointer prevent
attaching the write to its new address. The existing known-target update path
continues to use its captured targets and weak updates for multiple candidates.

The replacement's scalar range and copy evidence are captured before unknown
memory havoc. They can prove subsequent reads, checked arithmetic and body
postconditions such as `ensures p.* == 41`, including nested field pointers and
Boolean stores. This does not preserve old facts for other possibly aliased
pointers, and does not export general writing-callee memory contracts to callers.
Non-scalar writes and pointer expressions without a stable local/field path
remain conservative.

Source tests execute constant, field, Boolean and bounded-input writes. They
reject incorrect stored values, later alias writes/calls, and returning the new
pointer's contents after the RHS changed the pointer used to evaluate the write
address.

### Writing-callee scalar memory bounds for known destinations

The call verifier now applies proved scalar memory postconditions to uniquely
identified caller destinations, including nominal/anonymous field paths and
readonly default pointer aliases. After invalidating the call's write set, it
creates an exit-memory proof frame, explicitly retires entry-read identities,
imports current target bounds, and assumes eligible proved postconditions.
Resulting bounds refine the caller's current scalar identities without executing
another write. This supports `set(value.ref)` followed by checked arithmetic
under `ensures p.* == 41`, including void-returning functions and Boolean stores.

The destination comes from the argument value captured during evaluation, so a
later argument rebinding the pointer does not redirect the returned guarantee.
Only singleton target sets are refined: a guarantee about the selected address
does not apply to every possible address. Callee parameter binding stability and
readonly selected defaults are required for this mapping. Predicates involving
the function result remain on the existing result-export path; general joint
result/memory relations, unknown external destinations and conditional target
set refinements still need implementation.

and pointer rebinding in later arguments. Rejections cover retaining a pre-write

### Joint scalar result and post-state memory contracts

Writing calls can now solve eligible scalar result and memory postconditions in

Result export maps post-state observations back to the caller's current target
identities, preserving exact result/memory relationships as well as ranges.

before exit reads are created. This covers scalar results with uniquely known
local or field destinations and readonly default aliases. Unknown and multiple
destinations, non-scalar results, and general external memory export remain open.

Observation links carry only the target identity needed for result export rather

multi-call regression also exposed excessive work in retained short-circuit
conditions: proved Boolean expressions now become constant conditions, Boolean

symbolic relations. The existing verification budget was not increased.

trait-head admission rules as dispatch materialization. Invocation uses that
index together with the saved implementations, traits, assumptions and PTC
context; it cannot accidentally consult implementation candidates subsequently
added to the source checker. Caller type restoration is also independent of the
checker. The only mutable caller input is the shared execution step budget.
The dump includes the saved implementation index.

same loop identity stack used by ordinary break/continue checking, restoring it
on success or failure. Body expressions retain their descriptions, so mutable Any
locals can be updated and unknown values can be returned from a loop without
inventing a Type. Loop statements preserve the existing Void result convention.
Concrete instances retain the normal loop IR and resource analysis.

Source regressions execute conditional iteration, nested loops, early return,
named break and named continue. They reject invalid operations after continue,
immutable replacement, unknown conditions, missing/shadowed labels and transfers
out of a closure. Completed runtime-IIR resource tests accept single-pass moves
and self-move, and reject reuse of a moved input on a loop backedge.

### Open type assumptions provide evidence and discharge on specialization

Open-definition descriptions now admit extractable type `assumes` predicates as
local PTC facts. Block checking restores its entry context, preventing facts from
one runtime branch from leaking into siblings or the enclosing continuation.
Concrete open-body elaboration checks those predicates before publishing the
instance and erases a discharged assertion to Unit. False/unproved conditions
therefore reject instead of becoming unchecked axioms. Boolean program assumptions
continue through CheckPredicate and retain runtime verification.

Capability queries now include positive conjunctive trait facts from the active
PTC context, with bounded traversal; disjunction and negation are not extracted
as positive trait requirements. Symbolic trait evidence uses the actual context
sort frame where available, rather than an incomplete known-Type prefix.

Tests cover Type equality, concrete rejection, missing definition-side evidence,
branch isolation, positive trait assumptions, conjunctions, missing concrete
implementations, rejected disjunctive/negative method evidence and preservation
of runtime program checks. This checkpoint is limited to extractable predicates
in concrete open-function specialization. General generic-function assumptions,
arbitrary executable predicates, continuation fact export from nested blocks and
control-dependent assumption execution beyond this elaboration path remain work;
it does not introduce a general residual type-assertion IR instruction.

### Open assumption facts survive justified normal completion

A bounded source continuation pass now republishes checked type-assumption facts
after an open statement completes. Nested blocks, semicolon expressions and let
initializers export their unconditional facts. Conditional branches export a
disjunction of facts from their normal predecessors, preserve identical facts
without introducing a redundant disjunction, and exclude a syntactically exiting
predecessor. An absent normal-predecessor fact prevents export. Loop and closure
bodies do not contribute unconditional continuation evidence. The pass is used
both during ordinary description checking and concrete open-body checking; each
assumption still discharges independently before an instance is published.

Tests cover nested blocks, facts shared by both branches, a returning alternative,
trait-method evidence after normal completion and missing concrete implementations.
Single-sided conditional facts and loop-only facts cannot justify later operations.
This adds continuation export; general residual type-assertion execution, arbitrary
executable assumptions and more complete continuation analysis remain separate
work. Ordinary type predicates and program-state verification remain distinct.

### Mixed positional spreads and property collection

Extended calls now parse/lower `...expr` as positional expansion alongside
`name: value` properties. Elaboration infers against the collected record entrance,
retains already checked field producers, and remaps them into one source-ordered
preparation with tuple unpacking. Record construction is a trailing preparation
step, not a receiver prefix. Each opaque packet executes once, including empty
packets; early exits skip remaining producers and the invocation. Existing runtime
IR and move analysis retain responsibility for the resulting values.

The independent `extended_calls` suites cover literals and computed packets,
interleaving, empty packets, generic and explicit instances, contextual callbacks,
inherent/trait receivers, staged dependent defaults, invalid inputs and affine
reuse. A bound Tuple test verifies the normal-form head and single Type-list input
are retained. Grammar and parameter examples describe the same syntax. This adds
composition of the default collection paths, not custom collection protocols or
record-field expansion.

### Finite helper calls in runtime parameter defaults

Ordinary runtime parameter defaults now retain definition-scoped stability
obligations until checked function bodies are available. A bounded package-local
analysis admits acyclic direct calls and concrete generic instances, scalar
aggregates, private local mutation and function returns. It checks supplied
arguments, helper bodies and executable contracts without invoking suppliers or
rewriting emitted NIR. Summary keys include declaration and type arguments;
recursive identities and exhausted analysis budgets reject. Copying bound Tuple
values uses their registered representation contract without unfolding the head.
Machine-operation and call-contract validation remain mandatory after this gate.

Runtime evaluation order, omitted-only supply and later-default dependencies are
unchanged. Default evaluation precedes callee entry checks, so an entry precondition
cannot retrospectively justify an unsafe supplier call. Private mutation is distinct
from writing preceding input bindings or pointees. Unknown callbacks, recursion,
loops, pointer observations/writes and potentially observable owned cleanup still
require stronger evidence. This is not general runtime purity verification or the
implicit-supply protocol, and open-definition default admission retains its earlier
checking boundary.

### Runtime pure functions: P4 without a termination promise

AST lowering now retains `pure fn` as a runtime function. The package behavior
analysis in `compiler/elaboration/src/program/purity.rs` (formerly the default-call
analyzer) validates runtime pure bodies independently of comptime's policy.
It admits scalar value computation, private scalar mutation, loops and direct
recursive components, including calls through checked unmarked helpers. A recursive
backedge reuses only the same P4 obligation; every body remains checked, failed
roots abort publication, and changing polymorphic recursive keys remain bounded.
Runtime defaults use a separate finite-analysis instance and cannot reuse a P4
certificate as termination evidence. No optimization or eager execution is added.

Tests verify retained runtime phase/pure dump, mutual recursion, fuel-limited
divergence, loops, helper specialization, effectful argument evaluation, rejected
external reads/writes, unknown callbacks and owned cleanup, and preservation of
machine arithmetic checks. Bodyless pure declarations and open pure definitions
reject explicitly until their behavior contracts have a carrier. General resource
transfer, memory-view evidence and higher-order purity remain incomplete; this is
an initial value-behavior admission path, not the entire P0–P5 analysis system.

### P4 resource transfer uses affine cleanup evidence

The runtime purity checker now admits generic/owned value transfers through locals,
returns, branches, direct helpers and aggregate construction. It runs the existing
package-aware move analysis for each admitted runtime function and checks its
actual cleanup sites, including default evaluations and invoked closure reports.
Duplicate delivery fails; remaining non-Copy cleanup candidates require separate
Drop behavior evidence. Transfer alone neither grants Copy nor executes Clone.
Finite default-supplier analysis retains its preceding admission boundary.

Source tests execute generic identity, branch reordering, helper wrapping, whole
enum forwarding and bound Tuple construction. They reject lost/duplicated owners
and cleanup on early exit after preparing an owned call argument. Payload extraction
can retain a nominal wrapper cleanup even when its fields have moved; this is not
silently discarded. The classifier currently uses builtin representation-copy
evidence. Custom Copy/Drop protocol integration and proofs for remaining wrapper
cleanup are still pending; general resource purity is not complete.

### Pure trait method contracts and implementation admission

MethodContract now carries and displays its own `pure` promise; instantiated
program summaries and retained IIR interface contracts preserve it. Trait member
signatures may declare runtime `pure fn` without a body. Explicit implementations
inherit that promise even when they omit the modifier, and their effective bodies
pass the same P4 check. Default bodies preserve their declaration promise;
comptime implementations retain the separate comptime policy and phase.

Symbolic trait calls can use an established runtime P4 method contract. This is
behavioral evidence, not a new PTC proposition, and it does not certify termination
for runtime default suppliers. An unmarked interface does not gain a promise from
one stronger concrete implementation. Tests cover generic dispatch, method-local
binders, parent origins, default methods/overrides, effectful implementation
rejection and contract preservation through completed IIR. This replaces the
previous blanket rejection of bodyless pure trait members; non-trait bodyless
functions still require a supported external contract.

- CMTT 的首条源码执行链路接通：局部 `const` 表达式代码、显式 contextual expr type、虚拟 runtime 上下文、原绑定默认对应、同时端口替换、别名、comptime 条件选择、单洞组合及直接 splice。引用只检查主体，不产生 runtime 操作；接入后走既有资源／效应／阶段检查。解析器独立统计每份 quote，splice 操作数另属 comptime 子树；local const 与普通 let 保留阶段区别，并修正 ConstDecl 三子节点被当作四子节点读取的既有越界逻辑。
  类型重写共用的 NIR `Rewriter` 支持作用域敏感遍历：生成局部与控制身份新鲜化；调用默认参数保持所选函数的参数 ABI；闭包显式导入实际外部绑定、保留独立内部捕获槽，因此多个接口接到同一对象仍接受真实资源检查。新增 NIR/IIR 展开来源表和 `(generated-source ...)` dump，解决重复接入同一源码导致 ScopeEnd 清理边界不唯一的问题。代码值目前只保存在 elaboration 局部环境；一般生成器函数、Any/any 证据、上下文多态、依赖 runtime identity 的类型替换、pattern/arm、quote fn/template 尚未接通，不能称完整 CMTT。

### 条件效应闭包的实际指针来源核验（2026-10-14）

`memory::infer_closure_with_effect_inputs` 返回保留 handler 前提的 `ConditionalClosureSummary`，并提供 S-expression Display。直接指针捕获在摘要中映射为普通参数之后的虚拟输入；调用点把它们映射回实际捕获来源，再核验读写足迹。无前提的旧 API 不会把效应主体当成无条件内存安全，预算耗尽也不会发布成功摘要。

构造阶段遇到尚未安装 handler 的指针相关请求，记录待调用核验的义务。实际闭包调用复制当前安装的内存前提，独立验证每个普通指针参数与指针捕获的真实来源。只有经过核验的借用目标才进入该调用帧的稳定标量集合；它们不成为拥有型清理根，分支合流取交集。这支持同一闭包在不同安装下调用、handler 与闭包通过指针访问同一标量，以及拥有型捕获混合指针捕获时的正常／拒绝清理。

handler 仅捕获普通 Copy 标量时，现在也能与已经核验、且不别名到该直接捕获的外部标量存储共存；不再要求其必须额外捕获一个指针才能走同一稳定性检查。直接捕获本身的取址仍要求更丰富的契约，已存在的拒绝用例保留。捕获指针槽取址或重绑定、未建立来源的外部指针仍被拒绝。目前契约仍限于闭合的 scalar direct/direct-passing 操作交付与稳定的局部 Copy 标量；开放／fallback 行、指针或闭包形式的操作交付、一般聚合内存及通过任意高阶接口传递指针捕获仍需要更丰富的契约。

## 顺序模式与 let-else 的数据内存摘要（2026-10-14）

### Void observations across expansion boundaries

Guard observations now admit normally completing `void` results, local bindings,
match results and default arguments. Calls still require known targets and checked
observation behavior. A conservative syntactic rejection result may be refined
by the bounded memory summary even when the function has no callable parameters;
this covers code identities established inside the callee. Summary failure keeps
the rejection obligation. General owned locals still need destructor behavior

### Inline iteration pipelines and ambient effect forwarding

Direct inline handlers can now explicitly request their ambient effects during
joint expansion. Each handler template is normalized in its installing outer row,
separately from the handled computation. Ambient requests in the computation are
remapped after removing the installation; requests copied from a handler keep the
outer row and cannot recursively select that handler. Unsupported nested effect
boundaries, fallback handlers and unexpanded effectful calls remain conservative.

`development/examples/inline-iteration.fl` is an executable generic emit pipeline:
produce 1/2/3, map to 2/3/4, filter to 3/4, and sum to 7. The test executes ordinary
and expanded forms and verifies that the expanded entry has no remaining effect
request, run, computation or handler nodes. This is infrastructure for the intended
inline iterator protocol, not an implementation of source `for`. The old library
still exposes next-based Iterator; the new protocol interface awaits an explicit
decision rather than silently adopting that historical interface.

resume and lexical return clean Sink, Ticket, Middle, Producer, Caller exactly once
and in that order, with identical ordinary and expanded behavior. Existing routing,
invalid row, low-budget rollback and retained-boundary tests remain active. One old
expectation that outer requests must never expand was updated to require successful
expansion when budget permits, while preserving execution and rollback assertions.

### Literal suffix result inference

Literal conversion without an expected result now first considers scoped
interface evidence, then indexed implementation candidates for the exact source
and suffix. Each candidate uses a fresh call-inference scheme to infer its generic
inputs from the literal source type and recover its result type. A complete
interface capability query then checks applicability before accepting that result.
Multiple distinct results, unresolved generic inputs, conflicts, and pending
selection do not authorize a guessed conversion. Explicit/outer result context
continues to select a complete interface directly. Candidate traversal is bounded.

CLI/IIR coverage exercises an unannotated let with one result, a generic subject,
two ambiguous results, explicit disambiguation, scoped capability disambiguation,
unrelated suffixes in either declaration order, and a result-only generic that
remains unresolved. A generic identity call also passes its bool result context
back to the suffix despite multiple available conversion results. All execute
through the standalone CLI where appropriate.

This inference currently recovers generic result structure from subject matching;
result variables determined only by additional implementation predicates still
need further constraint integration. Exact Real literal sources remain unsupported.

### Implementation equalities in literal result inference

Literal candidate trials now import positive conjunctive implementation type
equalities as isolated inference obligations. A result-only binder constrained by
`R == bool` can therefore settle without a result annotation. This does not add
facts to the caller context: after trial inference, complete capability selection
still checks every implementation requirement. Disjunctions, negations, and trait
predicates are not mined for speculative equality branches.

CallCandidate exposes transactional generic-frame equation constraints with
bounded term validation. Budget failure preserves the prior candidate. The
matcher retains opaque normal-form behavior; equal opaque heads do not grant
injectivity of their arguments.

CLI execution verifies constraint-determined results and excludes contradictory
alternatives in either declaration order. Rejection cases preserve ambiguity for
a disjunction and reject an otherwise inferred result whose additional trait
requirement is absent. Core coverage verifies budget failure/recovery and opaque
head non-injectivity. This completes conjunctive equality proposals, not arbitrary
predicate-driven program synthesis or exact Real literal support.

### Exact finite decimal identities and comparisons

Terminology correction: current docs/basics/literals.md and
comptime/quoting-and-splicing.md name the compile-time literal source `Float`.
Earlier progress entries used the legacy `Real` spelling; that is not the
current language contract. The unsupported float-suffix diagnostic now says
exact comptime Float support.

comptime_runtime::decimal provides DecimalValue as a finite base-ten building
block. DecimalLiteral::exact_value canonicalizes redundant leading/trailing
zeroes and exponent spellings without selecting a binary proxy. Identity/hash
retain signed zero so later IEEE conversion cannot lose sign information;
explicit numeric comparison treats both zero signs as equal. This internal
identity policy does not define the complete language Float equality protocol.
Display emits a nested S-expression with canonical significand and exponent.

Comparison uses arbitrary-width decimal orders and padded significand digits,
never a power-of-ten buffer proportional to exponent magnitude. Parsing/copying,
comparison, and exponent arithmetic consume operation budgets; failures preserve
input values. Tests cover equivalent identities, signed zero, distinctions below
binary precision, huge positive/negative exponents, allocation/fuel rejection and
recovery, and 3969 pairwise comparisons against a scaled-integer oracle. Existing
IEEE rounding/subnormal/overflow tests remain passing.

### Exact finite Float addition, subtraction and multiplication

The decimal kernel now implements exact finite addition, subtraction and
multiplication. Alignment checks exponent distance, allocation width, fuel and
binary limb limits before expanding significands. Results canonicalize trailing
zeros without rounding. Cancellation yields positive zero, two negative-zero
addends retain negative zero, and multiplication combines signs by exclusive-or.
A budgeted base-1e9 integer-to-decimal transport routine supports result
construction and replaces repeated division-by-ten exponent serialization.

Source arithmetic, comptime interpretation and IIR folding share these kernels.
Exact division and remainder remain unsupported unless supplied by a selected
protocol; no truncation or binary-rounding policy was invented. Exact binary
arithmetic is foldable but excluded from total structural initializer analysis,
because valid inputs can exceed the result-size limit. Eager evaluation remains:
zero multiplication does not hide a failing other operand.

or unwrapping edge and returns an immutable conversion descriptor with explicit
source, target, owner and direction. It does not infer same-width conversions,

resource budget) are distinct from absence of a direct edge. Formation contracts
remain a producer obligation; the descriptor does not grant resource traits or

### Explicit newtype conversions in reference execution

Source `.as` now recognizes direct newtype representation edges and emits the
independent unary `NewtypeConvert` node. NIR traversal, phase checking, generic
substitution, constant reconstruction and conservative dependency walks retain
that node. It is not represented as a record constructor or field access.
The reference interpreter carries a distinct `Value::Newtype` and evaluates the
input once. Both endpoints and payload types are checked; IIR also rechecks the
edge against its concrete instance descriptor before execution. Generic IIR keys
retain arguments while already-substituted descriptors use empty telescopes.

comptime invocation tests count one producer call and check constant reconstruction.

values. Cross-stage constant use still requires the established Splice protocol.

none of this grants Copy or inherits the underlying type's operations.

### Newtype immutable values and comptime input transport

Newtype values freeze into nominal normal values with their declared identity and
one representation payload. Reconstruction consults nominal metadata and creates
`Value::Newtype`, never a struct value; wrong payload arity/type or enum tags are
rejected. Layout queries for canonical values understand both source newtype
telescopes and already-instantiated IIR representations. Freezing charges type and
payload work, enforces depth/size bounds, and rejects executable payloads.

Opaque-head value inputs and CMTT generator data inputs accept newtype domains.
The declaration category is available before layout demand, so a forward newtype
declaration is not spuriously rejected. Actual value admission still checks the
representation and contracts. Generic comptime Type construction also retains
newtype identity and arguments. Tests exercise nested freeze/thaw, forged values,
opaque-head retained inputs, code generation after explicit unwrap, forward
references, and failure/recovery. Distinct opaque inputs are inspected as retained
data; no inverse/injective equation for opaque result types was introduced.

Ordinary generic descriptions now recognize pending default dependencies as
inference sources. Unknown operands and already known generic arguments seed
a bounded dependency closure; a pending default is supported only when all its
input dependencies are supported. This allows U = Identity(T), V = Identity(U)
to wait for T without accepting unrelated phantom generics. Dependency visits
consume the elaboration budget. No default is executed or equated with an input
during this analysis; concrete calls retain normal default invocation/checking.

### Memory-call dispatch observes aggregate argument evaluation

Ordinary call dispatch previously inspected only each argument's root type. An
inline record containing an address therefore went through ordinary preparation
and was rejected only after exposing memory, while an equivalent already-bound
record used the memory path. Dispatch now uses a bounded NIR expression walk of
the current runtime scope to detect pointer-valued evaluations inside record and
block arguments before choosing the call path. It never evaluates an argument
twice, and deferred closure bodies, handler arms and nested call defaults stay in
their own contexts. The shared visitor is `nir::visit::expression_in_scope`.

Existing constructor/read examples now expect acceptance. Added lifecycle cases
cover direct construction, construction inside a block, and a later argument
moving the pointee after the earlier record argument captured its address.
Inspection of cleanup publication also identified the remaining explicit-premise
gap: only direct pointer parameters enter borrowed_parameters. Field borrows must
be represented and compared there before aggregate helpers can be claimed fully
executable; they must not become implicit validity assumptions.

### Explicit field borrow premises in executable cleanup publication

Added `moves::BorrowedField` (parameter slot, owned input path, pointee type),
its S-expression Display, and `Report.borrowed_fields`. A new field-context
analysis entry point preserves existing public entry points with empty field
premises. It rejects empty/duplicate paths, missing parameters, wrong layout
paths and mismatched pointee types before installing conditional nonowned roots.
Ordinary cleanup publication and contextual callback publication collect typed
field premises, require a matching memory footprint, and compare the report's
premises before publishing. Entry functions receive no implicit field validity.

Helpers that merely move an aggregate may have an unconditional cleanup plan.
Publication first attempts that plan with at most 4,096 work units and charges
the full allowance on failure before trying field premises. This preserves
unfinished-call cleanup without imposing an unsupported aggregate-return memory
summary. Runtime-generic formation does not demand a concrete layout for open
root types; concrete invocation still checks owned pointer fields. Forwarding
an opaque aggregate parameter is now routed through memory analysis even when
its expression contains no address operation.

New tests execute read/write, returned pointers, preceding-field defaults and
higher-order callbacks through acquired Copy/Drop protocols. They also verify
explicit premise requirements, malformed premise rejection and report dumps.

```flurry
typealias Type = .Type'builtin;
trait Allowed {}
impl Allowed for bool {}
comptime fn Select(comptime value: Type) -> Type where requires value:-Allowed { value }
struct Holder where T:-Allowed { pub const Payload = Select(T); }
comptime fn Build(value: Type) -> Type { Holder<value>.Payload }
comptime fn Valid() -> Type { Build(bool) }
```

上下文整数支持 Integer、定宽有符号/无符号整数和 BitVec。带预算解析、取负及精确范围转换，不环绕、不截断；BitVec 不被当作普通整数建立运算事实。回归覆盖 i8 最小值、u8 最大值，以及 0/1/8/32/65/129 位的位串边界、默认复用和错误输入。物化 NIR 的负整数拼写在 flow 和静态输入识别中均保留符号；源码负数模式由 parser/lowering 接通，支持数值后缀与组合模式，拒绝负号后的非数值模式。

静态输入识别只提供已知值/类型上下文，不移除原执行计划：

- 支持不可变局部绑定、成功的 LetPattern 解构、已知条件的 if、Bool 短路、已知 match 候选、tuple/record/enum 构造与字段读取。失败或未知的 let-else 不作为 fallthrough 推断；未知早期候选不能当作不匹配跳过。候选绑定隔离，or/remap 和顺序模式保留导出规则。
- 标量比较与浮点位身份分开处理。精确十进制支持字面量、取负和加减乘；f32/f64 复用现有运算。正负零相等，NaN 的有序比较为 false；Unknown 和预算耗尽保持未知。数值、字符串和十进制载荷的复制/比较计入预算。
- TypeEqual 仅处理 Type 项，通过 PTC 的计步接口分别求证相等与不等；未证明相等不等于证明不等。opaque Identity<bool> 与 bool 仍未知，normal-form 头不展开。
- 支持 PointerType、BitVecType、FunctionType、FunctionResultType、ClosureType，保留求值顺序、函数阶段和环境身份。位宽使用受检的精确整数转换。NIR 回归确认五种构造节点实际存在。
- 已知 TypeListIndex 可为后续输入提供上下文。正式 Tuple 头模式提取 List<Type> 后可索引、重复读取及供默认值复用；不改变原列表或所选 opaque type。负数、越界和超过 u128 的下标仍由原 invocation 报 IndexOutOfBounds。

### Inline Integer range expansion

`inline for` now expands bounded comptime Integer ranges, including inclusive
endpoints and staged function parameters. Iteration bindings are substituted
without allocating runtime Integer storage. Per-iteration scopes preserve
runtime mutations, nested labeled break/continue and return. Inactive ranges
check ordinary bodies without invoking nested staged computations; unsupported
iteration sources and excessive expansion retain explicit diagnostics.

Memory-summary exit predicates now bind pointer results to the accumulated

call could not prove its precondition. Consecutive-call and known-local-target
compound-update regressions now pass. External pointer parameters still lack
complete returned-address range export; this change does not claim that solved.


Direct external pointer return identities now carry the captured argument address

Multiple result targets, pointer-field/indirection result paths and generalized
postcondition export remain separate work. Negative source regressions reject
later-argument pointee writes, rebinding to another pointer, returning a different
argument, and callee writes before return.

### 程序契约关联常量与 required 契约依赖
